Hence it is added: If you do not believe, you shall not remain, as Symmachus translated, that is, you too shall not remain in your kingdom, but shall be led into captivity, suffering the penalties of those whose unbelief you have imitated. Or certainly, according to the Seventy, you shall not understand. And the sense is: because you do not believe the things that the Lord says are to come, you will not have understanding. This much we have said according to the history. But according to the tropology we have begun, we must consider that Isaiah is ordered to meet the impious king, going out from his own place, not at the beginning of the conduit, but at the outermost bounds of the upper pool, which was in the fuller's field, where filth and stains were washed away. For although Ahaz was reigning over Judah, yet because he was impious he lingered at the outermost bounds of the upper pool. So God has mercy not so much on the king, whom he judged unworthy of salvation, as on his people. And by the two tails of smoking brands, as we said before, he means secular wisdom and heretical speech, whose end is burning. They took counsel in vain to go up against Judah, and to seize it as though negligent and sleeping, and to join it to their own errors, and to set over it as king the son of Tabeel, that is, of the good God. For each adversary judges that the truth is with himself, that the best doctrine is with himself. Indeed Marcion the heretic thinks that Christ is the son of the good God, that is, of another, and not of the just God whose the Prophets are, whom he calls bloodthirsty, cruel, and a judge. While they say these things, the Lord threatens that their counsel shall not stand, but that for the meantime, now, as long as this world stands, the things also that are of the world hold sway within their own bounds and in their own cities. But when the time of the consummation has come, that is, the sixty-five years, and both the things of the world, which were made in six days, and all that pertains to the five senses have received their end, then all things are to be dissolved, which the gentiles and the heretics do not believe will come, and on account of their unbelief they do not understand the things that are said.

7:10-11

And the Lord spoke again to Ahaz, saying: Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God, in the depth of hell, or in the height above. He who had before spoken to Ahaz through the prophet: See that you keep silent; do not fear, and the rest, since Ahaz did not believe and therefore did not understand, himself speaks to Ahaz: that, terrified at least by the authority of the Lord, he may accept what is said. Because it seems difficult to you, he says, that most powerful kingdoms are to be ended in a short time, and that you with your people should be freed from great danger, ask for yourself a sign, not at all from the idols in whose error you are held, but from the Lord your God, who promises you help; and the very sign is of your own choosing, whence you would demand it, whether from the depth or from the height. Whereas the Seventy alone said this, the others, according to the Hebrew, translated more expressively, from the depth of hell. So just as the depth signifies hell, so by the height we ought to understand above the heavens: so that when you have received a sign from hell or from the height, you may believe that the things I have said will come. Do you wish, he says, that the earth be split, and that the underworld, which is said to be in the heart of the earth, lie open with a great gaping; or that the heavens be opened? Both of which pertain to the type of the Lord's death and ascension: For he who descended is the same who also ascended (Eph 4:10). And in the Apostle we read: Do not say in your heart, Who has ascended into heaven? that is, to bring Christ down. Or, Who has descended into the abyss? that is, to bring Christ back from the dead (Rom 10:6-7). And in another place, disputing about Christ, he says: What is the breadth, and length, and height, and depth of the surpassing knowledge and love of Christ (Eph 3:18). This, so far as concerns the mystical senses. But Moses too received signs from the earth, of which we read in the Psalms: He sent signs and wonders in the midst of you, O Egypt (Ps 134 [135]:9), frogs, locusts, gnats, and the dog-fly; and from heaven hail and fire and darkness of three days. I think that Hezekiah too, when the sun went back ten lines, received a sign from heaven (2 Kgs 20); and Joshua the son of Nun at Gibeon and Aijalon, when the sun and the moon stood still (Josh 10). Most think that Saul received a sign from the earth and from the depth of hell, when he seemed to have raised up Samuel through incantations and magic arts (1 Sam 28). But Jonah the prophet too, freed from the abyss, and from the deep and the jaws of death, gave and received the sign of hell (Jonah 2). I have read in the Commentaries of a certain man that this place was thinned out through allegory, so that he understood the depth and the height as αἰσθητὰ and νοητὰ, which we can call sensible things and intelligible things, of which the one is referred to the senses, the other to the mind and reason. The Virgin too he interprets as the soul which is corrupted by no consciousness of sin, and can bring forth from itself Emmanuel, God with us, that is, the present word of God. But we do not eat the flesh of the lamb boiled (Exod 12), but roasted, and such as can dry up in us all the phlegm of pleasures, lest, while we are wise beyond what we ought to be wise, we neglect the mystery of our faith.

7:12

And Ahaz said: I will not ask, and I will not tempt the Lord. It is not of humility but of pride that he will not ask a sign from the Lord. For although it is written in Deuteronomy: You shall not tempt the Lord your God (Deut 6:16), and the Savior used this testimony against the devil (Matt 4), yet, having been ordered to ask, he ought to have fulfilled the command by obedience, especially since both Gideon and Manoah asked for a sign and received it (Judg 6 and 13). And yet, according to the ambiguity of the Hebrew speech, in which is written ULO ENASSE ADONAI (ולא אנסה את יהוה), and all have likewise translated I will not tempt the Lord, it can be read I will not exalt the Lord. For the impious king knew that if he asked for a sign he would receive it, and the Lord would be glorified. So, as a worshipper of idols, who had set up altars at every corner of the streets and on the mountains and in the leafy groves, and had fanatics in place of Levites, he will not ask the sign that was commanded.

7:13

And he said: Hear then, O house of David: Is it a small thing for you to be troublesome to men, that you are troublesome to my God also? Who is this who said: Hear then, O house of David? Not at all God, who above had said to Ahaz: Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God; but the Prophet, as is proved from what follows: That you are troublesome to my God also. And the sense is: because you not only persecute the prophets and despise their sayings, but also contradict the sentence of God when he is present and commands; so that you cause labor to him who says in another place: I have labored in bearing it (Isa 1:14); for that reason the Lord will do the things that follow. For labor and trouble, which Aquila and Symmachus translated, the Seventy and Theodotion rendered agon, that is, wrestling and contest, because in their contentiousness they do not submit their neck to the service of the Lord, but, when he wishes to cure their wounds, spit out health. And this is to be noted, that when Ahaz, a most impious king, will not ask for a sign, the prophetic word is turned to the house of David, that is, to the royal tribe, of which we read above: And they told these things to the house of David, saying: Syria and Ephraim have come to an agreement.

7:14

Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, a Virgin shall conceive and bear, and you shall call his name Emmanuel. No longer at sundry times, according to the apostle Paul, and in many ways will God speak (Heb 1); nor, according to another prophet (Hos 12), will he be likened in the hands of the prophets; but he who formerly spoke through others will himself say, I am here (below, 58). Of whom the Bride too was asking in the Song of Songs: Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth (Song 1:2). For the Lord of powers is himself the king of glory (Ps 23 [24]:10): he himself will descend into the virginal womb, and will enter and go out by the Eastern gate which is always shut (Ezek 44); of which Gabriel says to the Virgin: The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you: therefore the holy thing that will be born in you will be called the Son of God (Luke 1:35). And in Proverbs: Wisdom has built herself a house (Prov 9:1). And when it is said: The Lord himself will give you a sign, it ought to be new and marvelous. But if a young woman or a girl, as the Jews would have it, and not a virgin, gives birth, what sort of sign can it be called, since this is a name of age, not of integrity? And in truth, to set foot to foot with the Jews and not at all, with a contentious rope, give them occasion to laugh at our lack of skill: a virgin is called in Hebrew BETHULA (בתולה), which is not written in the present place; but in place of this word is set ALMA (עלמה), which all except the Seventy translated young girl. Now ALMA is an ambiguous word among them: for it is said both of a young girl and of one hidden, that is, ἀπόκρυφος..... Hence also in the title of the ninth psalm, where in the Hebrew is set ALAMOTH (עלמות), the other Translators translated for youth, what the Seventy rendered for the hidden things. And in Genesis we read, where Rebecca is called alma (Gen 24), that Aquila translated neither young girl nor girl but hidden. The Shunammite woman too, having lost her son, when she had thrown herself at the feet of Elisha and Gehazi was keeping her back, hears from the Prophet: Let her be, for she is in grief, and the Lord has hidden it from me (2 Kgs 4:27). In place of what is said in Latin, has hidden it from me, in the Hebrew is written EELIM MEMMENNI (העלים ממני). So alma is said not only of a girl or a virgin, but, with ἐπιτάσει, of a hidden virgin and a secluded one, who has never been open to the gaze of men, but has been guarded with great diligence by her parents. In the Punic tongue too, which is said to flow from the fountains of the Hebrews, a virgin is properly called alma. And, though we may give the Jews something to laugh at, in our own speech too alma means holy. And the Hebrews use words of almost all languages: as in the Song of Songs (Song 3:9), from the Greek φορεῖον, that is, litter, Solomon made himself one, which we also read thus in the Hebrew. The words nugas (trifles) and mensuram (measure) too the Hebrews call in the same way and with the same senses. And as far as I can contend with my memory, I think I have never read alma of a married woman, but of one who is a virgin: so that she is not only a virgin, but a virgin of younger age, and in the years of girlhood. For it can happen that a virgin is an old woman, but this virgin was in the years of girlhood. Or certainly a virgin, not a little girl and one who could not yet know a man, but now marriageable. Indeed, in Deuteronomy (Deut 22:25ff.) under the name of a girl and of a young woman a virgin is understood. If, he says, a man finds in the field a betrothed girl, and, overpowering her by force, lies with her, you shall kill only the man who lay with her, and to the girl you shall do nothing: the young woman has no sin worthy of death. For as when someone rises up in ambush against his neighbor and kills his life, so this matter happened. He found her in the field: the betrothed girl cried out, and there was none found to help her. And in the volume of Kings we read (1 Kgs 1) that they sought a girl, a virgin, named Abishag, and brought her in to the king, to sleep with him and to warm him; and the girl was exceedingly beautiful, and she ministered to him, and the king did not know her. And what follows: And you shall call his name Emmanuel, both the Seventy and the three others translated likewise, in place of which in Matthew is written they shall call: which is not found in the Hebrew. So this child who will be born of the Virgin, O house of David, let him now be called by you Emmanuel, that is, God with us, because by the very facts, being freed from two enemy kings, you will prove that you have God present; and he who will afterward be called Jesus, that is, Savior, because he is to save the whole race of men, let him now be called by you by the name of Emmanuel. The word CARATHI (קראת), which all have interpreted you shall call, can also be understood as she shall call: namely, that the Virgin herself, who will conceive and bear, is going to call Christ by this name. In many testimonies which the Evangelists or Apostles have taken from the old books, we must attend more carefully to the fact that they followed not the order of the words but the sense. Hence also in the present place, for shall conceive in the womb, Matthew set shall have in the womb (Matt 1:23); and for you shall call, they shall call. The Hebrews think that this is prophesied of Hezekiah the son of Ahaz, because in his reign Samaria was taken: which cannot be proved at all. Since Ahaz the son of Jotham reigned over Judah and Jerusalem sixteen years (2 Kgs 16), and his son Hezekiah succeeded him in the kingdom at twenty-five years of age, and reigned over Judah and Jerusalem twenty-nine years. How then, granting that this prophecy was made to Ahaz in his first year, is it said of the conception and birth of Hezekiah, when at the time Ahaz began to reign Hezekiah was already nine years old? Unless perhaps they say that the sixth year of Hezekiah's reign, in which Samaria was taken, is called his infancy, not of age but of rule. That this is forced and violent is plain even to fools. A certain one of our people contends that the prophet Isaiah had two sons, Jasub and Emmanuel, and that Emmanuel was begotten of the prophetess his wife, as a type of the Lord and Savior: so that the first son, Jasub, which is interpreted left or returning, signifies the Jewish people, which has been left and will afterward return; but the second, that is, Emmanuel, and God with us, the calling of the nations, after the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us.

7:15

He shall eat butter and honey, that he may know to refuse evil and to choose good. For which the Seventy translated before he knows; and what follows, to take up evil, is not found in the Hebrew. And the sense is: O House of David, who are commanded by the word of God to call, that is, to call upon, when set in danger, the name of Emmanuel, that is, of God with us: do not marvel at the novelty of the thing, if a Virgin bears God, who has such power that, though he is to be born a long time after, being called upon he frees you now; for he it is who was seen by Abraham and spoke with Moses. I will tell you something else more marvelous, lest you think he will be born in a phantasm: he will use the foods of infancy, he will eat butter and milk. And although many ages later the Evangelist testifies of him: And the child advanced in wisdom and age and grace with God and men (Luke 2:52), and this is said so that the reality of his human body may be proved; yet while still wrapped in swaddling clothes, and fed on butter and honey, he will have judgment of good and evil, so that refusing evil things he chooses good things. Not that he did this, or refused, or chose; but that he knew how to refuse and to choose, so that by these words we may know that the infancy of the human body did not prejudice the divine wisdom. Indeed, the Angels announce him to the shepherds as he lies in the manger; the Magi, coming from the East, worship him, who surely, we must believe, were chosen. And on the contrary, Herod, the Scribes and the Pharisees are refused (Matt 2), because for the sake of one infant they slaughtered many thousands of little ones.

7:16

For before the child knows to refuse evil and to choose good, the land which you abhor shall be forsaken before the face of its two kings. In the sixth year of Hezekiah's rule Samaria was taken by the Assyrians (2 Kgs 18), that is, in the thirty-first year of his age. If, then, this one who is to be born, whether of a Virgin, as we prove, or of a young woman, as the Jews would have it, will eat butter and honey, and will be so small that he cannot distinguish evil from good, and before he passes beyond the time of infancy the land of Syria and of Samaria is to be laid waste by the Assyrians: let the Hebrews answer how Hezekiah at thirty-one years is proclaimed a little infant, and of such untrained age that, eating honey and butter, like the children of Nineveh, he knows neither left nor right, that is, neither evil nor good. But referred to Emmanuel, which is interpreted God with us, it will have an easy understanding: that at the mystery and the invocation of his name the land of Syria and of Samaria is laid waste by the conquering Assyrian, and the house of David is freed from the two kings whom it fears, namely Rezin and Pekah.

7:17

The Lord will bring upon you, and upon your people, and upon the house of your father, days that have not come since the days of the separation of Ephraim from Judah, with the king of the Assyrians. This place is to be read by hyperbaton. Indeed we too, following the Hebrew truth, have interpreted it thus: O house of David, listen to what I say: so that the land of Syria and Samaria may be forsaken before the face of the two kings whom you most vehemently dread, the Lord will bring days upon you, and upon the house of your father David, such as you have never had from the time when the ten tribes were separated from the two tribes and began to have a kingdom in Samaria. And he will bring those days, that is, times, with the king of the Assyrians, so that when those kings have been conquered and overthrown, you may be freed by the presence of Emmanuel. The Seventy rendered this place thus: The Lord will bring upon you, and upon your people, and upon the house of your father, days which have not yet come, from the day on which Ephraim took away the king of the Assyrians from Judah. What sense this has we cannot know, unless perhaps this must be said: that Ephraim, that is, Samaria, by the greatness of its sins first made the onslaught of the Assyrians turn aside to itself. Otherwise: For the meantime now the two kings Rezin and Pekah, who besiege you and hasten to lay you waste, will be overthrown in a short time; but the time of your own laying waste will come when the Assyrian comes, which you had never expected, indeed never feared. By which he teaches that the house of David must fear not Syria and Samaria but the Assyrians. So he frees it from the present dread, and threatens concerning the time to come.

7:18-19

And it shall be in that day, the Lord will whistle for the fly that is at the farthest part of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria: and they shall come and shall all rest in the torrents of the valleys, and in the caves of the rocks, and in all the thickets, and in all the holes. When the land of the two kings, Damascus and Samaria, which you now abhor and fear, has been deserted, then, O house of Judah, the Lord will bring upon you and your people days such as you have never seen before, and the king of the Assyrians. In vain, therefore, do you fear things present, half-burnt brands that have no fire at all: for you ought to know that with his whistle the Lord is going to call the flies of Egypt and of its rivers, by which without doubt he means the seven διωρυχὰς of the Nile, and the bee that is in the land of Assyria. And he calls the Egyptians flies on account of the filth of idolatry and because they were an unwarlike people; and the Assyrians a bee, whose kingdom at that time was the most powerful and the readiest for wars; or for this reason, that almost the whole region of the Assyrians and of Persia made use of arrows. These, then, will all come and occupy your land, in the torrents of the valleys, and the caves of the rocks, and in all the thickets and holes, and in the leafy woods. These things are said by metaphor, so that, since he had once named flies and bees, he might keep the figure in the rest. Let us read the books of Kings and Chronicles, and we shall find that the holy king Josiah was slain by the Egyptians, and the people of Israel subjugated to the Egyptian power (2 Kgs 23; 2 Chr 35), so that it appointed a king for them. And not long after, Nebuchadnezzar came with a countless multitude of warriors, and having taken Jerusalem and torn down the other cities of Judea, he burned the Temple and settled Assyrian inhabitants in Judea (2 Kgs 24).

7:20

In that day the Lord will shave with a hired razor, by those who are beyond the river, by the king of the Assyrians, the head, and the hair of the feet, and the whole beard. Some think that this is prophesied of the Assyrians, who for thirteen hundred years before they overthrew Jerusalem possessed the kingdom of Asia, of Egypt and of Libya: that they were to be conquered by the Medes and Persians and their empire destroyed. Others, however, judge that the Egyptians were slain beyond the river Euphrates. But we judge that the razor hired for a wage is the Assyrian himself, whom in Jeremiah, for the punishment of the sinful people, he even calls his dove (Jer 25). Indeed in the vision of Tyre too (Ezek 29:18-20), because Nebuchadnezzar had toiled very greatly in building siege-works and in heaping up a mound, and, when they fled by fleet, had been deprived of his wage, Egypt was given to him as the wage for his labor. So with this most sharp razor, and by those who dwell beyond the river Euphrates, namely by the Assyrian king, the Lord will shave from Judea all the hair and the hairs of the whole body from head to feet, and the comeliness of the beard, which is the mark of manhood, so that nothing strong, nothing beautiful may remain in it, but they may be compared to effeminate men, or rather to disgraced women.

7:21ff.

And it shall be in that day, a man shall rear a cow of the herd and two sheep, and for the abundance of milk he shall eat butter: for everyone who is left in the midst of the land shall eat butter and honey. And it shall be in that day, every place where there were a thousand vines at a thousand pieces of silver shall become thorns and briers. With arrows and bow they shall go in there: for briers and thorns shall be in all the land. And all the mountains that shall be hoed with the hoe, the terror of thorns and briers shall not come there: and it shall be for the pasture of the ox and for the treading of the flock. After the overthrow of Jerusalem, and the captivity of the people, and the burning of the Temple, Nebuzaradan the chief of the soldiery, whom the Seventy call ἀρχιμάγειρον, left in the land a few of the people, and those poor, to till the vineyards and fields. Then Gedaliah, who, left from the royal line, had been set over them, exhorts them and says: Do not fear the Chaldeans: dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you (2 Kgs 25:24). In that day, then, that is, at that time, when all the wealth of the Jews has been carried off into Chaldea, so great will be the desolation in the land of Judea, and so incredible the devastation, that they will by no means have herds of oxen, nor flocks of sheep, as they had been accustomed to have before; but a rare inhabitant will scarcely be able to rear one cow and two sheep; not for ploughing, but for the food of their milk and the clothing of their fleece. For through the want of grain and of everything that the earth brings forth for eating, they will feed on milk and butter and wild honey. And what he says, For the abundance of milk he shall eat butter, signifies this: that the land, through the scarcity of tillers, is more fertile and better suited for pastures. At that time, through the fewness of men, so great will be the want of wine, the vineyards being deserted and by no means pruned for fear of the enemy, that single vines will scarcely be bought for single silver shekels. For the whole land will be reduced to briers and thorns; and so great will be the dread, with swords raging everywhere, that no one will dare to visit his own field without bow and arrows, and, abandoning the places in the plains, they will flee to the mountains, and there, protected by the difficulty of the places, they will scarcely dig the rough mountains by hand: because they will not have oxen, ploughs and ploughshares. Wherever, then, a rare tiller is found in the mountains, they will sustain a miserable life from there. But the rest will lie open to pastures, and will be trodden down by brute animals without any keeper. Would that we did not know that these things are wont to happen after a captivity! But now a great part of the Roman world is like Judea of old: which we do not think has come about without the wrath of God, who avenges contempt of himself not through Assyrians and Chaldeans, but through savage nations, once unknown to us, whose countenance and speech alike are terrible, and who, displaying womanish and shaven faces [he means the Goths, who shaved their beards], stab the fleeing backs of men, and well-bearded men at that. I know that I have read in these places a very broad and inextricable tropology: that all the things we have set out according to the history happened spiritually to the Jews, who scarcely have one cow and two sheep, that is, clean animals: so that they are nourished not on solid food but on the milk of infancy, and eat the honey of words that drips from the lips of the harlot woman; and they do not have wine, which gladdens the heart of man, but all their works are reduced to thorns, so that they are wounded by adversaries who shoot in the dark at the upright of heart (Ps 10 [11]). And if at any time they wish to be wise in something higher, and, sweating with excessive labor, to find something mystical in the holy Scriptures, nonetheless they bring forth no fruits of doctrine, but are filled with briers and thorns, which spring up in the hands of a drunkard. And their land and doctrine is trodden down not by men, rational living beings, but by oxen, for whom God has no care, and by brute animals.

8:1, 4

And the Lord said to me: Take for yourself a great book, and write in it with the pen of a man: Swiftly strip the spoils, quickly take the prey. And I took to me faithful witnesses, Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Barachiah, and I went in to the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. And the Lord said to me: Call his name, Make haste, strip the spoils, hasten to take the prey: for before the child knows how to call his father and his mother, the strength of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of the Assyrians. The Seventy, for a great book, translated a new and great book. And in place of what is found in the Hebrew, I took to me faithful witnesses, they said: for it is at hand, and make faithful men witnesses for me. And for Uriah the Priest, only Uriah; the rest likewise. First the Prophet was sent to Ahaz (Isa 7), to foretell to him what the Scripture records: when he would not listen, the Lord himself speaks to Ahaz, and commanded him to ask for himself a sign in the depth or in the height. When he answered, I will not ask, and I will not tempt the Lord, the impious king is dismissed and the words of God are turned to the house of David, and there is promised to it a Virgin who will bear a son, whose name is to be Emmanuel, that is, God with us. If he is called upon often, Samaria and Syria will be overthrown: overthrown, however, by the king of the Assyrians, who is afterward to capture Judah itself too; so that the whole land of Judea is turned into a wilderness. So again, under another figure, the virginal birth is described. And the Lord told the Prophet not at all to bring out the secret of the new birth among the peoples, but to write it in this great volume which we now read. And, that it may be the more marvelous, to comprise the mysteries of God in human words, and with the pen with which men are accustomed to write. And what is it that is written with a human pen? That the child who is born should swiftly strip the spoils and quickly take the prey, that is, that he should no longer suffer the devil to reign; nor send Angels nor Prophets, but himself come down to save his creatures. So the Prophet does what was commanded, and takes to himself two faithful witnesses: Uriah the priest, who is a teacher of the law, as Malachi says: The lips of the priest shall keep knowledge, and they shall seek the law from his mouth, for he is the Angel of the Lord of hosts (Mal 2:7); and Zechariah the son of Barachiah, who, there is no doubt, was a Prophet. We read that in the reign of Ahaz, Uriah was priest of the Temple of the Lord (2 Kgs 16), whom Ahaz commanded to make an altar like the altar of Damascus. And the book of Days relates (2 Chr 29) that Hezekiah the son of Ahaz sought the Lord in the days of Zechariah, who was instructed in the fear of God. And Isaiah showed himself worthy of the prophetic spirit, and offered himself to the prophetess, that is, to the Holy Spirit, which in the Hebrew speech is called in the feminine gender RUA (רוה), according to what is written: Draw near to the Lord, and be enlightened (Ps 33 [34]:6). So the Lord was conceived of the Holy Spirit. And although human speech cannot unfold the mysteries of his birth, yet Gabriel speaks to the Virgin herself who conceived: The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you: therefore the holy thing that will be born of you will be called the Son of God (Luke 1:35). Some interpret the prophetess as holy Mary, who, there is no doubt, was a prophetess: for she herself says in the Gospel: For behold, from henceforth all generations will call me blessed: for he who is mighty has done great things for me (Luke 1:48-49), and the rest. And Isaiah is commanded to call that very child, who before was called Emmanuel, now Make haste, strip the spoils, hasten to take the prey. For ascending on high he led captivity captive; he received gifts for men (Ps 67 [68]; Eph 4:8). And before he took a human body and, in the manner of infancy, called God his father and Mary his mother, the strength of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria will be taken away by the king of the Assyrians: so that, not yet born, he might save his people, the house of David, by invocation alone. Uriah is interpreted light of the Lord; Zechariah, memory of the Lord; and Barachiah, blessing of the Lord: by these witnesses the birth of Christ is proved. For he himself in the Gospel, to the two who were going to Emmaus (Luke 24), beginning from Moses and the Prophets, set out that all things had prophesied of him. According to tropology, in a virginal soul, stained by no filth, the word of God, conceived of the Holy Spirit, swiftly strips the spoils from the adverse powers and makes all things serve him. And since it now sees in part and prophesies in part (1 Cor 13), before it can be perfect and rightly call God its Father and the heavenly Jerusalem its mother, while still set in infancy and in progress, it will overcome the strength of Damascus, namely the doctrine of secular wisdom; and will take away the spoils of Samaria, with which the heretics have despoiled the Church, saying: We have no portion in David, nor inheritance in the son of Jesse (1 Kgs 12:16), in the presence of the king of the Assyrians himself, the devil, who will not be able to help them. And such sons are borne not only by Mary, the perpetual Virgin, to the Prophets, but also by holy women to the patriarchs: Sarah, which is interpreted ἄρχουσα, that is, princess; and Rebecca, which in our language sounds patience.

8:5ff.

And the Lord spoke to me yet again, saying: Because this people has cast away the waters of Siloam that go in silence, and has rather taken up Rezin and the son of Remaliah: therefore behold, the Lord will bring upon them the waters of the river, strong and many, the king of the Assyrians and all his glory: and he shall come up over all his channels, and shall flow over all his banks. And he shall go through Judah overflowing, and passing through he shall come up to the neck, and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of your land, O Emmanuel. He had said above that the strength of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria were to be taken away in the sight of the king of the Assyrians, and that the two kings would be captured when the Assyrian made war: now God speaks to the Prophet in the customary character of the Scriptures, by a figure of Siloam, the spring of Jerusalem, and of the most violent Assyrian river, that it would flood the whole land of Israel with its waters, and go out over the banks of its bed, and be borne with such force that, after it had occupied the land of the ten tribes, it would reach Judah and, passing through, would extend up to the neck: by which he signifies the captivity close at hand. For Judah was not captured at that time, but when all the cities of the two tribes had been subjugated, Jerusalem alone remained, which was freed by the incredible mercy of God. So the might of the Assyrian and of his countless army, which he had described under the flooding of a river, he now shows by another figure: that with his wings, that is, his generals and boundless multitude, he covered the land of Emmanuel, that is, of God who defends it, but yet did not possess it; although Emmanuel is fitted by the Seventy to the following section, not with its proper name, as it is called among the Hebrews, but translated, that is, God with us. And that Siloam is a spring at the roots of Mount Zion, which bubbles up not with continuous waters but at certain hours and days, and comes through hollows of the earth and caves of the hardest rock with a great sound, we cannot doubt, we especially who dwell in this province. And the sense is: because the people of the ten tribes preferred to be subject to Rezin and the son of Remaliah, that is, to the kings of Damascus and Samaria, rather than to the stock of David, which began to reign by my judgment, I will make it serve not at all these kings whom it has taken up, but the Assyrian king, whose might as it occupies the land of Samaria is compared to the flooding of a river. And an apostrophe is made to Emmanuel, that is, to God present, because the Assyrian raised himself up so far as to try to possess even his land, Judah. According to the anagogy, every heretic who joins secular wisdom to his help and seeks to attack Jerusalem, that is, the Church, forsaking the waters of the spring Siloam (John 9), which is interpreted sent, and which leaps up to eternal life, will be handed over to the prince of the Assyrians (whom we shall read of later as the great mind), and, handed over to his power, he will come into the depth of sins. For he is of such arrogance that he dared to show the Savior all the kingdoms of the earth and to say: All these have been handed over to me (Matt and Luke 4). He will try also to enter Judah, that is, the house of confession, and often, through those in the Church who are negligent, he will come up to the neck, desiring to choke those who believe in Christ, and he will stretch out his wings, filling the whole region of Emmanuel; but he will not be able to prevail, because Judah has God present. We read in the Gospel according to John (John 9) that the Lord sent the man blind from birth, whose eyes he had anointed with clay made from his spittle, to the waters of Siloam, and when the blind man had washed off the clay in them, his blindness was wiped away and he received the clear light of his eyes: which, beyond the greatness of the sign, indicates that the blindness of the Jews and of every unbeliever cannot be healed otherwise than if the darkness of former error is put to flight by the doctrine of the waters of Christ, which flows gently without the din and clamor of words. This which is read in the Seventy: And he will walk over all your wall, and will take away from Judea the man who can lift up his head or perhaps do anything, is not found in the Hebrew, and in the Greek codices it has been pierced through with ÷ the slaying spit.

8:9-10

Gather together, O peoples, and be conquered, and hear, all you lands far off: take strength, and be conquered. Gird yourselves, and be conquered: take counsel, and it shall be scattered: speak a word, and it shall not be done, for God is with us. For gather together, or be weak and be broken, as others interpreted, the Seventy set know. For the Hebrew word ROU (רעו), because of the likeness of the letter RES (ר) and DALETH (ד), they understood as DOU (דעו). So, O peoples of Samaria and Syria, know that you are weak and feeble, and that with Emmanuel present you can do nothing against Jerusalem, the city of God: and let not only you, who are neighbors, know this, but the whole land far off. For although you gather an army and gird yourselves for battle, and the number of the besiegers is greater than that of the besieged, yet not once but a second time I will say: you are conquered. And whatever counsel you take against Jerusalem will be scattered. And although you said above (Isa 7:6): Let us go up to Judah, and rouse it up while it is at rest, and set over it as king the son of Tabeel, you speak a word indeed, but it will not be done, because God is with us, that is, Emmanuel. We can use this testimony against the gentiles too in time of persecution: that although they seem strong and to overcome us in those who have lapsed, yet they are conquered in those who have shed their blood for Christ, and that after wars peace is restored to the Churches, and all their counsels against Emmanuel are scattered, because God is with us. Those who contradict the truth will also profitably hear it, so that at last they may be overcome by reason, and may not wish to win in falsehood, because whatever they say, perversity can never overcome what is right.

8:11ff.

For thus the Lord says to me: As with a strong hand he instructed me, that I should not walk in the way of this people, saying: Do not say, A conspiracy; for all that this people speaks is a conspiracy: and do not fear its fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself: let him be your dread, and let him be your terror. And he shall be for a sanctification to you, but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offense to the two houses of Israel: for a snare and for a ruin to those who dwell in Jerusalem; and very many of them shall stumble, and shall fall, and shall be broken, and shall be ensnared, and shall be taken. The Seventy translated this place thus: Thus says the Lord: With a strong hand they have withdrawn from the journey of the way of this people, saying: Lest perhaps they say, It is hard. For all that this people speaks is hard; but do not fear its fear, nor be troubled. Sanctify the Lord of powers himself, and he shall be your fear, and if you have trusted in him, he shall be for a sanctification to you, and you shall not run against him as against a stone of stumbling, nor as against a rock of ruin. But the house of Jacob shall be in a snare and in a valley for those who sit in Jerusalem: therefore very many among them shall be weak, and shall fall and be broken, and shall draw near, and shall be taken. And what follows, men in safekeeping, is to be marked in front with an obelus. Because the Hebrew and the common edition differ much from each other, we have therefore set down both. And first we must discuss the Hebrew. Thus the Lord spoke to me. Who, on account of good works, and the grace which on account of good works I have obtained; or with his strong hand instructed and trained me, that I should not walk in the way of this people and be held in the same error; or certainly he made me withdraw from the most evil way of this people, and said to me: do not fear the conspiracy of the two kings; but consider this rather, that all that this people speaks against me is a conspiracy; and, according to Symmachus, who interpreted ἄνταρσιν, has risen up against me in rebellion. But you, Prophet, and those who are with you, do not fear the plots of the people, but fear the Lord, and let him be your fear. For the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom (Prov 1:7; Ps 110 [111]:9). He will be for a sanctification to believers, but to unbelievers for a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, that is, to the two houses of Judah and Israel; and especially for a snare and a ruin to those who dwell in Jerusalem, on whom very many will strike, and will fall, and will be broken, and, ensnared in the chains of their sins, will be led into captivity. The two houses the Nazaraeans (who receive Christ in such a way that they do not give up the observances of the old Law) interpret as two families, Shammai and Hillel, from whom arose the Scribes and Pharisees, whose school Akiba took over, whom they assert to have been the teacher of Aquila the proselyte, and after him Meir, whom Johanan the son of Zakkai succeeded, and after him Eliezer, and in order Telphon, and again Joseph the Galilean, and up to the capture of Jerusalem Joshua. So Shammai and Hillel arose in Judea not long before the Lord was born, of whom the former is interpreted scatterer, the latter profane: because by their traditions and δευτερώσεις they scattered and defiled the precepts of the Law. And that these are the two houses which did not receive the Savior, who became for them a ruin and an offense. According to the Seventy, the people resisted the will of God with a strong hand, and says that all that the Lord has commanded is hard, according to what we read in the Gospel: This saying is hard; who can hear it (John 6:61)? Hence they are commanded to hear the Lord and to fear him alone. For if they have trusted in him, they will have him for a sanctification, and will not strike against him as against a stone of offense and as against a rock of ruin. From this place the Apostle too takes a testimony, that Christ became an offense to the Jews, but to the Gentiles foolishness (1 Cor 1:23). And again: Israel, by pursuing the law of righteousness, has not attained to the law of righteousness (Rom 9:31). Why? Because not from faith, but as if from the works of the law, they stumbled against the stone of stumbling, as it is written: Behold, I will lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense: everyone who believes in him shall not be put to shame (ibid., 33). So those who did not receive Emmanuel, but for whom he became a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, will be broken and led captive. And what he says, But the house of Jacob shall be in a snare and in a valley for those who sit in Jerusalem, signifies this: that they do not dwell on the mountains, nor move in the lofty places of the Scriptures, but always understand lowly things, joining sins to sins, and bound by the snares of their offenses.

8:16-17

Bind up the testimonies, seal the law among my disciples, and I will wait for the Lord, who hides his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him. The voice of the Lord speaking to the Prophet: Because, he says, the Lord has become a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense to the two houses of Israel, and they would not receive Emmanuel sent to them: Bind up the testimonies of the old Instrument, and hand them over to my disciples, who have received the Gospel, namely the Apostles, or apostolic men. Or certainly, let the law and the prophecy until John be bound up among them (Matt 11), and be shut and sealed, so that what they read they may not understand. For in place of disciples, according to the ambiguity of the Hebrew speech, we can also interpret doctrines. Hence the Prophet answered: Because, the Gospel taking its place, the Law has been shut and sealed among the Jews, and you command that it be assigned not at all to the Jews but to the nations: therefore I will wait for Emmanuel, whom you promise is to come, of whom you said above that he himself is our dread and he himself our terror, and that he is for a sanctification to us; and I will look for the Lord who hides his face from the house of Jacob, that is, from the Jews, because they would not receive him. The Seventy translated this place thus: Then they who are sealed shall be manifest, that they may not learn the law. Which has this sense: when very many have fallen and been broken, and have struck against the stone of stumbling and the rock of offense, then those who are sealed among the people will be manifest, so that they may by no means learn the law of Moses, but obey the precepts of the Gospel.

8:18

Behold, I and my children, whom the Lord has given me for signs and portents of Israel, from the Lord of hosts who dwells on Mount Zion. The Lord, he says, commanded me to bind up the testimony among the Jews and to hand over and seal the law for his disciples, because he had hidden his face from the house of Jacob: therefore I will look for him and wait for my Lord, and not only I, but also the children whom the Lord has given me, namely the other prophets and the sons of the prophets, who were born not of the will of the flesh and of blood, but of God (John 1:13). Of whom the Apostle too spoke: My little children, with whom I am again in travail until Christ be formed in you (Gal 4:19). And these children, that is, the prophets, were given for signs and for portents to Israel, according to what we read in Ezekiel: And Ezekiel shall be for a sign to you (Ezek 24:24). In Zechariah too, holy men and disciples of the prophets are called τερατοσκόποι, that is, watchers of portents and signs, because the Prophets always went before as a sign of things to come (Zech 3:8). This much meanwhile according to the letter. But the blessed Apostle, in the Epistle which is written to the Hebrews (though Latin custom does not receive it among the canonical Scriptures), teaches that this testimony ought to be understood in the person of the Lord and Savior: For which reason he is not ashamed to call them brothers, saying: I will announce your name to my brothers, in the midst of the Church I will praise you (Heb 2:12); and again: I will put my trust in him (ibid., 13); and once more: Behold, I and my children, whom God has given me. Since, then, the children have shared in flesh and blood, he himself likewise became partaker of the same sufferings (Isa 8:18). And how these children were for a sign and a portent to the wisdom of the world and to the pride of the Jews, the same Apostle teaches, who says that the Lord and Savior chose the foolish and weak things of the world, to confound the wise and the strong things (1 Cor 1). Hence the Savior too said to the Apostles: Unless you are converted as one of the children, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven (Matt 18:3). And the preacher of the new Gospel becomes a child, who puts off the old man, who is corrupted in the desires of seduction, and puts on the new, who is renewed unto knowledge after the image of the Creator. And that the Lord of hosts dwells on Mount Zion, the same Apostle writes: You have come to Mount Zion and the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem (Heb 12:22). Hence I wonder at a certain one of our people who understands these children as the two sons of Isaiah, whom he begot from the conception of the prophetess his wife, namely Jasub and Emmanuel: of whom the former went before as a sign of the rejection of the former people, the latter of the taking up of the nations. Whoever accepts this will consequently also affirm that the prophet Hosea truly had a harlot for a wife.

8:19ff.

And when they say to you, Seek from the Pythons and from the diviners, who hiss in their incantations: does not a people inquire of its God? on behalf of the living, of the dead? To the law rather and to the testimony. But if they do not speak according to this word, there will be no morning light for them. And it shall pass through it: it shall fall and shall hunger: and when it hungers, it shall be angry, and shall curse its king and its God. And it shall look up above, and shall gaze at the earth, and behold, tribulation and darkness, dissolution, distress, and pursuing gloom: and it shall not be able to fly away from its distress. If it is the voice of the prophet Isaiah, as the Jews judge: Behold, I and my children, whom the Lord has given me for a sign and for a portent of Israel, then these things that follow too must be believed to be said by him to his disciples. When, he says, the nations and peoples say to you, those of whom it was read above: Be weak, O peoples, and be conquered, why do you want to listen to prophets, why are you deceived by the words of Isaiah and think that he knows the things to come? Seek rather from the Pythons and from the diviners, who hiss in their incantations. In place of which the Seventy translated: Who speak from the earth, who cry out from the belly. For everyone who is of the earth speaks of the earth (John 3:31). And he whose god is the belly, and whose glory is in his shame (Phil 3:19), must be believed to cry out from the belly. Do you answer them and say: Does not a people inquire of its God? on behalf of the living, of the dead? If you, he says, in keeping with the variety of your idols (for you have not one god but many), consult those whom you judge to be gods, and inquire of the dead, or of the images of dead men, about the living: how much more ought we to hear our God through the prophets? So he teaches the disciples, and adds: to the law rather and to the testimony. If, he says, you are in doubt about anything, know that it is written: The nations which the Lord your God will destroy before your face listen to dreams and to diviners; but to you the Lord your God has not so delivered: The Lord your God will raise up for you a Prophet from your brothers, like me; him you shall hear (Deut 18:15). Hence, if you wish to know things that are doubtful, give yourselves rather to the law and to the testimonies of the Scriptures. But if your congregation will not seek the word of the Lord, it will not have the light of truth, but will move about in error and darkness. The light will pass through it, that is, through your congregation, or land, and you will fall, and you will hunger, and when you hunger you will be angry, according to what is written: And if they are not filled, they will murmur (Ps 58 [59]:16): and you will curse God your king, and in your necessities you will look up above to heaven and down to the earth: and behold, tribulation and darkness, dissolution of the knees, and distress of mind, and gloom of the eyes, and you will not be able to be rescued from the distress. This according to the Hebrews. But, as we said above, if it is the person of Christ saying: Behold, I and my children, whom God has given me, then he himself also speaks these things to the Apostles and to the believers from the nations who have received his Gospel. If, he says, your fathers whom you have left say: seek the ventriloquists, whom we understand as pythons (such as the slave girl we read of in the Acts of the Apostles (Acts 16), who was a source of gain to her masters), and those who speak from the earth, which the magi promise to do in the calling up of souls, and the other kinds of evil arts: you ought to know this, that each nation consults its own gods and questions the dead about the welfare of the living. But to you God has given the law as a help, so that you can say: the divination of the heathen, who often deceive their worshippers, is not such as ours, which is brought forth from the law without any payment. Hence the Seventy translated: Not as this word, for which there is no giving of gifts. For freely, he says, you have received, freely give (Matt 10:8). But upon the unbelievers will come a most grievous famine, not a famine of bread nor a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of God (Amos 8). And when you hunger you will be saddened, and will curse your prince and your fathers' traditions, that is, the devil and your ancient errors. And he says this to those who have suffered famine of the truth, and will look up above to heaven and down to the earth, and will be in distress, in darkness, and in tribulation: so that they may not see until the time when they too are converted to the Lord. These places call for a broad explanation, but we spare the size of the books, to remove the reader's weariness. These things we have touched on in part according to the translation of the Seventy, which in very many places is out of tune with the Hebrew. But the Nazaraeans set out this place thus: When the Scribes and Pharisees tell you to listen to them, who do everything for the sake of the belly, and in the manner of magi hiss in their incantations so as to deceive you, you ought to answer them this: It is no wonder if you follow your traditions, since each nation consults its own idols. So we too ought not to consult you, the dead, about the living: rather God has given us the law and the testimonies of the Scriptures; and if you will not follow them, you will not have light, but gloom will always oppress you, which will pass through your land and doctrine: so that when those deceived by you see themselves in error and suffering a famine of truth, then they will be saddened, or angry, and will curse you, whom they used to think of as their gods and kings. And in vain will they look back to heaven and earth, since they are always in darkness and cannot fly away from your snares.

9:1ff.

At the first time the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali was lightened: and at the last the way of the sea beyond the Jordan, of Galilee of the nations, was made heavy. The people that walked in darkness has seen a great light: to those dwelling in the region of the shadow of death, light has risen upon them. LXX: Drink this first, act quickly, region of Zebulun, land of Naphtali, and the rest of you who are by the sea beyond the Jordan, of Galilee of the nations. The people that walked in darkness has seen a great light: you who dwell in the region and shadow of death, light shall rise upon you. We have set down the double edition because the testimony is well known and was used by the Evangelist Matthew: so that either the difference of the translation or the likeness may be recognized. And first it must be noted that the Evangelist Matthew set down this testimony not according to the Seventy but according to the Hebrews. For the Gospel word says: Now when Jesus heard that John had been delivered up, he withdrew into Galilee, and leaving Nazareth he came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is by the sea in the borders of Zebulun and Naphtali: that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, saying: The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, the way of the sea beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations: the people that sat in darkness has seen a great light; to those sitting in the region of the shadow of death, light has risen upon them. From that time Jesus began to preach and to say: The kingdom of heaven has drawn near (Matt 4:13ff.). And John the Evangelist relates that Jesus, invited with his disciples to a wedding at Cana of Galilee, did his first sign there, turning water into wine: This beginning of signs Jesus did in Cana of Galilee: and he manifested his glory: and his disciples believed in him (John 2:11). Hence too it is said in the Seventy: Drink this first, act quickly: because the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali first saw the miracles of Christ: so that the land which had first seen the Lord doing signs might first drink the draught of faith. And according to the Hebrew it is said to have been lightened at the first time of the burden of sins: because the Savior first preached the Gospel in the regions of the two tribes. Hence too it is said in the sixty-seventh Psalm: Bless the Lord from the fountains of Israel. There is Benjamin the younger (Ps 67 [68]:27-28; Acts 9); Paul the apostle, in ecstasy of mind, who also said elsewhere: whether we are beside ourselves, it is for God (2 Cor 5:13): The princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali, their leaders; because in these tribes were the little villages from which our leaders the Apostles believed. And they believed, according to Symmachus, swiftly, so that, hearing: Come, and I will make you fishers of men (Matt 4:19), they at once left both their father and their boat. But at the last time their faith was made heavy, since very many of the Jews remained in error. And here he calls the sea the lake of Gennesaret, which is formed by the inflowing Jordan; on whose shore Capernaum and Tiberias and Bethsaida and Chorazin are situated: in which region above all the Lord stayed; so that the people which either sat or walked in darkness saw a light, by no means a small one, like that of the other prophets, but a great one, like that of him who says in the Gospel: I am the light of the world (John 8:12). And those who dwelt in the region of the shadow of death, light has risen upon them. Between death and the shadow of death I think the difference is this: that death belongs to those who have gone down to the underworld with dead works: For the soul that sins, it shall die (Ezek 18:20); but the shadow of death belongs to those who, while they sin, have not yet departed from this life: for they can, if they will, do penance. For Galilee of the nations Aquila translated θῖνας of the nations, Symmachus borders of the nations; and by θῖνας we understand mounds of sand, which are either on the shores or on the banks. The Hebrews who believe in Christ set out this place thus: At the first time these two tribes, Zebulun and Naphtali, were captured by the Assyrians and led into the enemy's land; and Galilee was deserted (2 Kgs 15), which the prophet now says was lightened, because it bore the sins of the people. But afterward not only the two tribes, but also the rest, who dwelt beyond the Jordan and in Samaria, were led into captivity (2 Kgs 17 and 18). And this, they say, is what the Scripture now says: that the region whose people was the first to be led into captivity and began to serve the Babylonians, and which before was moving in the darkness of error, itself first saw the light of Christ preaching, and from it the Gospel was sown into all the nations. The Nazaraeans, whose opinion I set down above, try to explain this place thus: When Christ came and his preaching flashed forth, the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali was the first to be freed from the errors of the Scribes and Pharisees, and shook off from its neck the most heavy yoke of the Jewish traditions. But afterward, through the Gospel of the Apostle Paul, who was the last of all the Apostles, the preaching was made heavy, that is, multiplied; and the Gospel of Christ shone into the borders of the nations and the way of the whole sea. Finally, the whole world, which before walked or sat in darkness and was held by the chains of idolatry and of death, beheld the clear light of the Gospel.

9:2, 4

You have multiplied the nation, you have not magnified the joy: they shall rejoice before you, as they rejoice in the harvest, as victors exult when the prey is taken, when they divide the spoils. For the yoke of its burden, and the rod of its shoulder, and the scepter of its oppressor you have overcome, as in the day of Midian. For every violent plundering is with tumult: and the garment mixed with blood shall be for burning and food for the fire. LXX: The greatest part of the people you have led down in your joy: and they shall rejoice in your sight, as they are wont to rejoice in the harvest, and as those who divide the spoils: because the yoke that was set upon them has been taken away, and the rod from their neck. For the rod of the oppressors shall be scattered, as in the day of Midian. For every robe gathered by deceit, and the garment of exchange, they shall restore: and they shall wish that they had been burned with fire. In obscure places we set down both editions, so that the diligent reader may recognize how far the common translation differs from the other editions and from the Hebrew truth. An apostrophe is made to the light itself, which appeared to the people set in darkness, that is, to the Lord and Savior. And it is said to him: You have multiplied the nation, that is, you have filled all the nations with the knowledge of you; but you have not magnified the joy. In accordance with which the Apostle says that he has unceasing sorrow for his brothers who are Israelites (Rom 9). And Jonah is saddened that the Ninevites were saved in such a way that the gourd, or CICEION (קיקיון), withered (Jonah 4). And the Lord himself says in the Gospel: I did not come except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel (Matt 15:24). And in the passion: Father, if it be possible, he says, let this cup pass from me (Matt 26:39). This place has this sense: If it can be that the multitude of the nations believe without the destruction of the Jews, I refuse the passion. But if they are to be blinded so that all nations may see, Father, let your will be done. So when Christ has come, and the nation of Christians has been gathered from all nations, then the Apostles will rejoice as reapers rejoice in the harvest, of whom the Lord spoke: The harvest indeed is great, but the laborers are few (Matt 9:37). And as victors exult who divide the captured prey. For when the strong man has been captured and bound, all his house is plundered and the spoils are divided (Matt 12). But you, O Lord and Savior, have pulled from their shoulders the yoke of his burden, that is, of the devil, who before exulted in the world, who ruled over all nations, who pressed down the necks of all with the most heavy yoke of slavery; and the rod with which he struck all men and compelled them to render him their sins as a kind of tribute; and you have made those freed serve you, without any army and without shedding of blood, by a hidden hand: as once under Gideon you gave the people of Israel victory over the Midianites (Judg 7). For just as a garment that has been bloodied with human blood cannot be washed, but, stained with blood, is burned with fire, so that the stains of the foul gore perish along with the garment: so the violent plundering of the devil, and the tumult and crowds by which he had subjected the human race to himself, have been assigned to the fires of Gehenna. The Seventy signify that not all but a certain part of the people believed: although for what they said, you have led down in joy, others have interpreted you have magnified. And while in the rest they hold the same sense, they add that he, that is, the devil, will restore the robe gathered by deceit and the exchanged garment: namely, that he is going to restore with their former ornaments all the souls which he had stripped of God's help; and not he alone, but also his satellites, the demons: who, if the choice were given them, would rather choose to perish in flames than to lose their prey.

9:6

For a little child is born to us, a son is given to us: and the government is upon his shoulder; and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counselor, God, Mighty, Father of the age to come, Prince of peace. His dominion shall be multiplied, and of peace there shall be no end: upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to establish it and strengthen it in judgment and righteousness, from henceforth and for ever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will do this. LXX: For a little child is born to us, a son is given to us, whose government is upon his shoulder: and his name is called messenger of great counsel. For I will bring peace upon the princes, and his health: great is his government, and of peace there is no bound, upon the throne of David and his kingdom: to set it right and to help in judgment and righteousness: from this time now and for ever. The zeal of the Lord Sabaoth will do these things. Therefore the devil, and all his violent plundering, by which he had oppressed the human race and mingled blood with blood, will be for burning and food of the eternal fire: because a child is born to us of a Virgin, of whom it was said above: Before the child knows to refuse evil and to choose good (Isa 7:16); and afterward, in the begetting by the Prophetess: Before the child knows how to call his father and his mother (Isa 8:4). This child, then, who was born of the Virgin, is called Emmanuel, that is, God with us; and, begotten of the Prophetess, that is, of the Holy Spirit, he was named Make haste, strip the spoils, hasten to take the prey: now he is called by many names. And although from what he had said above, Emmanuel, that is, God with us, he showed that he is God; yet now he says that his government was set upon his shoulder, either because he himself carried his cross, or, by the shoulder, showing the strength of his arm, as the same Isaiah says: The Lord God has revealed his holy arm to all the nations (Isa 52:10). And again: Lord, who has believed our report: and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed (Isa 53:1)? So after two names he will be called by six other names: Wonderful, Counselor, God, Mighty, Father of the age to come, Prince of peace. For not, as most think, are the names to be joined in pairs, so that we read Wonderful counselor, and again, Mighty God; but Wonderful is to be read separately, which in Hebrew is said PHELE (פלא); and Counselor apart, who in their tongue is called IOES (יועץ); and God separately, who in Hebrew is said EL (אל). Indeed, in what follows, where we read: For you are God, and we did not know; and again: I am God, and there is no other besides me (Isa 45:5), and many things like these: in place of what is said in Latin, God, in the Hebrew EL is written. And what follows, Mighty, is called in Hebrew GIBBOR (גבור). Hence too in the place where the same prophet records: They shall trust upon God, the holy one of Israel, in truth: and what is left of Jacob upon the mighty God (Isa 10), for mighty God the Hebrew has written EL GIBBOR. And the Father of the age to come and of the resurrection, which is fulfilled in our calling; and the prince of peace, who said to the Apostles: My peace I give to you, my peace I leave to you (John 14:27): no one will doubt this who has read, according to the apostle Paul, that the Savior is our peace. Terrified by this majesty of names, I think, the Seventy did not dare to say of a child that he was openly to be called God, and the rest; but in place of these six names they set what is not found in the Hebrew, Angel of great counsel, and I will bring peace upon the princes, and his health. Which seems to me to have this sense: He is the Angel of great counsel who announced to us that Israel was to be cast off for a time and the nations to be saved; and he gave peace to his princes, the Apostles and apostolic men, and left the health of his teachings to believers. And what follows: His dominion shall be multiplied, and of peace there shall be no end, in place of which the Seventy translated: Great is his government: we ought to know that the Hebrew word MESRA (משרה), both here and above, the Seventy interpreted ἀρχὴν, that is, government. In place of which we rendered government above, here dominion. But Aquila, deceived by the ambiguity of the word, interpreted μέτρον, that is, measure, which is called by the same name in Hebrew and in Latin. Nor can anyone doubt about the manifold dominion of the Savior and his peace, which has no end, who has read in the Psalms: Ask of me, and I will give you the nations for your inheritance, and the ends of the earth for your possession (Ps 2:8); and again: And abundance of peace, until the moon be taken away (Ps 71 [72]:7), that is, until the consummation of the age. And his government and dominion will be upon the throne and kingdom of David, which after the Babylonian captivity had been broken up, to establish it and strengthen it, and to teach that it is perpetual (lest the promise of God should seem empty), from the time of the Incarnation and for ever. And the zeal, that is, the jealousy, of the Lord of hosts did this for this reason, because they provoked him to jealousy with those who were not gods, and he provoked them to jealousy with a nation that was not a nation (Deut 32). The prophecy of Emmanuel and of the child to be born of a Virgin, begun at the place where it is said to Ahaz: Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God, is ended with this little verse, in which is added: The zeal of the Lord of hosts will do this (Isa 7:11). Now let us pass on to the rest.

Book Four

We dictate books of unequal length, and according to the diversity of the visions and of their senses one is drawn in, another drawn out. So, having finished the third volume, we pass to the fourth, which is smaller than the former by a third of the measure of its lines, especially since the fifth, which we have placed after this book, is of historical explanation and has nearly double the number. For while we are unwilling to divide what is joined, and to pass over what was interpreted long ago, we have steered our little boat as if between the two συμπληγάδας of the Pontic sea; and it, with the Holy Spirit blowing and the Lord Savior directing our course, slips out into the open sea, while you, virgin of Christ Eustochium, say: Come from the four winds of heaven, O spirit, and give life to the dead bones (Ezek 37:9): so that those which lay in the dust of the earth may be raised up as the Lord breathes upon them.

9:8ff.

The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it fell upon Israel. And all the people of Ephraim shall know it, and those who dwell in Samaria, saying in pride and greatness of heart: The bricks have fallen, but we will build with squared stones; they have cut down the sycamores, but we will change them for cedars. And the Lord shall raise up the enemies of Rezin against him, and shall turn his foes into tumult, Syria from the East, and the Philistines from the West, and they shall devour Israel with whole mouth. For all this his fury is not turned away, but his hand is still stretched out, and the people has not returned to him who strikes it, and they have not sought the Lord of hosts. We read above (2 Kgs 16) that in the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah king of Judah, Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel went up to Jerusalem to take it by storm. And (Isa 7) that Isaiah the prophet was sent to meet Ahaz with Jasub his son, to tell him not to fear, and that his heart should not be afraid of the two tails of smoking firebrands, because in them the rule of Syria and of Israel was to be brought to an end. When he did not believe, because of the greatness of the matter and the present danger, he is bidden to ask a sign for himself. And because he was an idolater, he refused to do even this: therefore the Lord gives a sign, not to the king himself, but to the house of David, the sign of his Son who was to be born of the Virgin, at whose invocation they were to be freed from the imminent danger, and the rest, which we have interpreted up to the present place. So, many mysteries having been set in between, he now returns to what he had begun, and prophesies the overthrow of Rezin and Ephraim, that is, of Syria and Samaria: A word, he says, the Lord sent into Jacob, and it fell upon Israel. Among the Hebrews DABAR (דבר), which is written with three consonant letters, DALETH, BETH and RES, according to the nature of the passage signifies word if it is read DABAR, and if DEBER, death and pestilence. For this reason many, deceived by the ambiguity of the term, say that not a word was sent, but death. So the Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it fell upon Israel. He willed that Judah should reign, as Jacob prophesies in Genesis (ch. 49); and Israel, that is, the ten tribes, claimed the rule for themselves, of whom it was said: They have reigned, and not through me (Hos 8:4). So the dignity of rule, which had begun in David at Samuel's anointing after Saul was cast off, sent into Jacob, that is, into the twelve tribes, which were once called Jacob, fell upon Israel: not, as the Seventy translated, came: for what had been appointed and directed to the saints fell among the wicked. So the people of Ephraim and those who dwell in Samaria shall know, who because of their multitude are lifted up into pride and say: The kingdom of Judah is small, and in comparison with ours most worthless. So, while they collapse like bricks, let us build ourselves a house of squared stone. When their sycamores, which are cheap wood, have been cut down by hostile incursion, we will build up our rule with cedars, which do not rot, so that they may signify an everlasting kingdom. Let all the people of Ephraim, then, and those who dwell in Samaria know this: that the Syrian, who is now its help, will go over to the enemy. Or certainly, that against the Syrian himself sudden wars of adversaries arise, and all are turned into tumult: so that against Israel Syria moves from the East, and the Philistines, that is, the Palestinians, from the West, and together they devour Israel. And when they have done these things, my hand is nonetheless stretched out, or lifted high, over Israel, and does not cease to strike them. And struck by God they will not return to him who strikes them, nor will they seek the Lord of hosts, worshiping golden calves in place of God. According to the anagogy, our writers expound this passage thus: God sent his Son to Jacob, that is, to the Jews; and he came to Israel, that is, to the people of the nations, whom the Apostle too says are called Israel (Rom 9). Others, however, thus: The Lord sent his Word to the Church, which supplanted the former people, and it fell upon Israel, that is, upon the heretics, who boast that they see God. So let their leaders know, and all who dwell in Samaria, that is, who say that they keep the law of God, and are in an abundance of virtues, and bear the fruits of righteousness (for this is what Ephraim means), who in the pride of their heart despise the Church, and, thinking its simplicity to be want of skill, say: In place of its bricks we will build our churches with squared and very strong stones, and in place of unfruitful trees, soon to perish, we will raise up the loftiest cedars; cedars which the Lord will crush, and which the righteous man, in the person of the wicked, relates that he saw, and their place was not found (Ps 36 [37]). So the Lord says that Rezin, which means worldly wisdom, whose help Ephraim used, will be turned against him, and all his enemies will fight against him, and he will be assailed both from the East and from the West, and they will devour Israel with whole mouth. In place of which the Seventy translated: And let us build ourselves a tower: and God will dash down those who rise up against mount Zion, and will scatter his enemies. For they desire to build themselves a temple in Samaria too, in the likeness of the Temple of God; but although they have moved their feet from the East and said: Come, let us build a tower, and make ourselves a name before we are scattered (Gen 11:4), with the Lord fighting against them their agreement will be dissolved and scattered, and their tongues will be divided against one another, lest by agreeing they become worse; rather they will be destroyed by one another. And when they have been so struck and devoured by their enemies, still they will not return to the Lord; but his hand is still ready to strike, according to what we read in Jeremiah: In vain have I struck your sons: you have not received discipline (Jer 2:30).

9:14ff.

And the Lord will destroy from Israel head and tail, bending and perverting, in one day. The aged and honorable, he is the head; and the prophet who teaches falsehood, he is the tail. And those who call this people blessed shall be leading it astray, and those who are called blessed shall be cast headlong. Therefore the Lord will not rejoice over its young men, and he will not have mercy on its orphans and widows, because every one is a hypocrite and wicked, and every mouth has spoken folly. For all this his fury is not turned away, but his hand is still stretched out. For impiety is kindled like a fire: it shall devour brier and thorn, and shall be kindled in the thicket of the forest, and shall be rolled together in the pride of smoke. In the wrath of the Lord of hosts the earth has trembled, and the people shall be like food for the fire. A man will not spare his brother, and he will turn aside to the right and be hungry, and he will eat on the left and not be filled: each one will devour the flesh of his own arm. Manasseh Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh, and they together against Judah. For all this his fury is not turned away, but his hand is still stretched out. Not only will the Lord raise up the enemies of Rezin against him, and turn his foes into tumult, Syria from the East and the Philistines from the West, so that they devour Israel with whole mouth; but because it has not returned to him who strikes it, nor sought the Lord of hosts, he will stretch out his hand to strike, so as to destroy from Israel the head, and the tail bending and perverting, namely him who perverts what is right (Jer 2). Who the head is, he himself has interpreted: the aged and honorable. And who the tail is: The prophet, he says, who teaches falsehood, that is, the false prophet. He has spoken of the leaders; now he joins the people as well to the nobles, because teachers and disciples, the learned and the unlearned crowd, will perish alike. For those who called the people blessed are seducers; and those who were called blessed, not for virtue but for gifts, will be cast headlong into death. Hence also we read above: My people, those who call you blessed lead you astray, and trip up the paths of your feet (Isa 3:12). In such a people God will have mercy on no person: not on the orphan, not on the widow, because every one is a hypocrite, pretending one thing and doing another: promising chastity and living luxuriously, making a show of poverty and filling the purse. Hence he adds and says: And every mouth has spoken folly. For all these things the Lord does not cease to be angry, but still raises his hand to strike. And because they have done these things, impiety will be kindled like fire, so that the ravening flame devours not the tilled field but briers and thorns, and consumes not fruit-bearing trees but the unfruitful forest in which wild beasts dwell. For this reason it is said that the thicket of the forest, when fire is set beneath it, is rolled together in the pride and height of the smoke. For everything that is lofty and rises up on high can be called proud. In place of which the Seventy, meaning I know not what, translated: and it will devour all things round about the hills.
