And what has been added according to the Seventy: the envoys will be troubled, and pains will seize them: we can interpret as those envoys whom the citizens had sent against him who had set out into a far country to seek a kingdom for himself (Luke 19:27). Hence he himself says in the Gospel: But those enemies who did not want me to reign over them, bring here and slay before me.

13:8

Twistings and pains will seize them; they will be in pain like a woman in labor; each one will be astonished at his neighbor; their faces are burnt countenances. When the warriors of the Lord have come from a distant land, and all hands have been loosened, and the heart is fearful and crushed, then strophomata, which we have translated as twistings of the belly, and pains will seize them, like the pains of women in labor. By this it is shown that they are tortured by their own conscience, and have their faces burnt with that fire which they had kindled for themselves: because they cannot say: The light of your countenance has been signed upon us, O Lord (Ps 4:7); and: We all, with unveiled face, beholding the glory of the Lord, are transformed into the same image (2 Cor 3:18). Each one will be astonished at his neighbor, seeing him in the same torments by which he himself is tormented.

13:9

Behold, the day of the Lord comes, cruel and full of indignation, and of wrath and fury, to make the land a wilderness and to crush its sinners out of it. For land the Seventy translated τὴν οἰκουμένην, that is, the world; for cruel, incurable. For when the day either of judgment or of death has come, that will be fulfilled which is read in the sixth psalm: But in hell who will confess to you (Ps 6:6)? For that is not a time of penance, but of punishments. And in another place it is said: How great is the multitude of your sweetness, O Lord, which you have hidden for those who fear you! Therefore the great mercy of God is hidden from those who are still set in fear and do not have the perfect love of God, so that, while they hear of the day of the Lord as cruel and incurable and full of indignation and fury, they may cease to sin. The world, or the land, will also be made a wilderness, and the sinners will be crushed out of it, the land which before was weighed down by the burden of sinners, so that, crimes having been blotted out and destroyed, righteousness alone may dwell and reign on the earth.

13:10

For the stars of heaven and their splendor will not spread forth their light; the sun is darkened in its rising, and the moon will not shine with its light. LXX: For the stars of heaven and Orion, and all the adornment of heaven, will not give their light: and they will be darkened when the sun rises, and the moon will not give its light. Where we have translated their splendor, that is, beyond doubt, of the stars, Aquila and Theodotion set down the very Hebrew word CHISILEEM (כסיליהם): for which the Seventy translated Orion, adding of their own and all the adornment of heaven, which is to be marked beforehand with an obelus. Now the fables of the Gentiles say that Orion has twenty-two stars, of which four are of the third magnitude, nine of the fourth, and again another nine of the fifth, and by others they are called Bootes. We read also in Job of the Hyades, and Vesper, and Arcturus, and the treasuries, or the inner parts of the South (Job 9:9), of which we must speak in their own place. Nor ought we to think that among the Hebrews these stars are called by these names which the Greek and Latin tongues sound forth, but that they have names of their own. For just as God called the light, day; and the firmament, heaven; and the dry land, earth; and the gatherings of the waters, seas (Gen 1); so too he called the several stars by their own names, whose proper meaning our language does not express. It is written of God in another place: Who numbers the multitude of the stars, and calls them all by names. When therefore the day of the Lord has come to make the whole world a wilderness and to remove the sinners utterly from it (Ps 146 [147]:4), then, in comparison with the divine majesty, the stars of heaven and all their splendor will withdraw their light. Nor is it surprising to say this of the lesser stars, since even the sun is darkened in its rising, and the moon does not have its accustomed splendor. But what the Seventy translated, that the stars and Orion and all the adornment of heaven are darkened when the sun rises, has nothing of a sign or of a wonder; for this happens at all times, that when the sun has risen the stars that are in the heaven do not appear. Nor is it surprising that he said this of the sun, since even when the moon is full and shining the whole night most of the stars do not shine. And that there are stars in the heaven even by day is proved by an eclipse of the sun: when it has been obscured by the shadow of the earth, as the philosophers argue, and by the disk of the moon set in its way, the stars are seen more clearly in the heaven.

13:11

And I will visit upon the evils of the world, and against the ungodly their iniquities. When God visits and strikes, he strikes for this purpose, that he may amend. Accordingly, when he is vehemently angry with those who do not do penance: I will not visit, he says, upon your daughters when they have committed fornication, nor upon your daughters-in-law when they have committed adultery (Hos 4:14). On the contrary, of those who are to believe in Christ it is said (Ps 88 [89]:33): I will visit their iniquities with a rod, and their sins with scourges: but my mercy I will not take away from them.

And I will make the pride of the unbelievers to rest, and I will humble the arrogance of the mighty. LXX: And I will destroy the insolence of the wicked, and I will humble the insolence of the proud. The Hebrew word GAON (גאון), which plainly sounds arrogance and pride, Theodotion and the Seventy always translated insolence, expressing the sense rather than the word, because every proud man is ready for insolence. Therefore the Lord visits upon the evils of the world, and against the ungodly their iniquities, for this reason: that he may curb the arrogance of the proud and humble the pride of the mighty. For God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble (1 Pet 5). And in Proverbs we read: Before ruin the heart of a man is lifted up, and before glory it is humbled (Prov 16:18). Ruin always follows pride, and glory humility: For he who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted (Luke 14). We read in another place: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the understanding of the prudent I will reject (1 Cor 1:19). Not that true wisdom and true prudence are destroyed by the Lord, but the knowledge falsely so called: those who treasure up for themselves a lying tongue, and fail searching with searching, and find nothing, speaking iniquity on high and setting their mouth against heaven. Hence the pride of heretics is properly called insolence against the truth.

13:12

A man will be more precious than gold, and a human being than pure fine gold. LXX: And those who have been left will be more honored than refined gold, and a man will be more honorable than the stone of Sophir. At the consummation of the world, when the world has been reduced to a wilderness, and the sun darkened in its rising, and the moon has not given its splendor, such signs and portents will be wrought by the Antichrist that, as iniquity increases, the love of many will grow cold, so as to deceive, if it be possible, even the elect of God (Matt 24). Then a man will be more precious than gold, which in Hebrew is called PHAZ (פז), and Aquila translated κιῤῥὸν, which is of the finest and blood-red color; and a human being than the purest fine gold, which in Hebrew is called OPHIR (אופיר), and Aquila translated σπήλωμα ὀφεὶρ, which the Seventy, intending I know not what, translated stone of Sophir. Now it is a place of India in which the best gold is produced; as we read in Genesis of the river Phison: This is it which encircles the whole land of Evila, where there is gold; and the gold of that land is the best: and there is the carbuncle and the green stone (Gen 2:11). And more precious is understood as meaning rarer. For everything that is rare is precious, as we also read in the volume of Samuel: And the word of the Lord was precious in Israel (1 Sam 3:1).

13:13

Upon this I will shake the heaven, and the earth will be moved from its place. LXX: For the heaven will rage, and the earth will be moved from its foundations. When a man has become more precious than gold, and a human being than pure fine gold, and that has been fulfilled which is written: Do you think, when the Son of Man comes, he will find faith on the earth (Luke 18:8)? then both the heavens and the earth will be moved. For heaven and earth will pass away, not by their own will and by their own choice, as many suppose, believing them to be living beings; but because of the indignation of the Lord of hosts, and because of the day of his fury, who looks upon the earth and makes it tremble. Hence what is said in the Seventy, for the heaven will rage, is to be taken μετωνυμικῶς of those who dwell in heaven, just as if we were to say: the whole city cried out, and the entire town went out to meet the judge. And of the foundations of the earth we read in Proverbs too: God by wisdom founded the earth (Prov 3:19). And the Lord says to Job: Where were you when I was founding the earth (Job 38:4)? Not that the earth has foundations laid down as a mass in the deep; but the will and power of God, by which all things are held together, is to be called its foundations. For he himself founded it upon the seas, and established it upon the rivers, and he himself hung it upon nothing (Ps 23 [24]; Job 26).

13:14, 16

And it will be like a fleeing fawn, and like a flock of sheep, and there will be none to gather them: they will turn each to his own people, and each will flee to his own land. Everyone who is found will be slain, and everyone who comes upon them will fall by the sword. Their infants will be dashed in pieces before their eyes; their houses will be plundered, and their wives will be ravished. When heaven and earth have been shaken, the devil, the crooked serpent, will flee, or every doctrine contrary to the truth, which is divided into teachers and disciples: the former of whom, because of their ὀξυδέρκειαν, are called in the Greek tongue Dorcades, that is, roe-deer; the followers are like brute animals, and wandering hither and thither they have none to direct them: for they have lost him of whom it is written: The steps of a man are directed by the Lord (Prov 20:24). And these, freed from their most evil teachers, will turn to their own people, and each will flee to his own land, from which they sprang: but whoever is found will be slain, or have his throat cut. And this happens not only at the consummation of the world, but to this very day in the Church: when the teachers have been overcome, the deceived flock returns to its people and to its own land; and in that it is found, it is slain, so that it ceases to be heretical, and whoever comes upon them will fall by the spiritual sword. Then their infants and little ones, who have not yet come to the full age of error, they will dash in pieces before the eyes of the teachers, and will plunder their houses and ravish their wives, depraved wisdom and perverse doctrine. Hence for fathers of this sort, whose little ones are to be slain, we ought to pray and say: Give them, O Lord. What will you give them? A barren womb and dry breasts (Hos 9:14). For they have travailed with iniquity, they have conceived sorrow, and they have brought forth unrighteousness.

13:17-18

Behold, I will stir up against them the Medes, who do not seek silver nor desire gold: but with arrows they kill the little ones, and on the sucklings of the womb they will have no pity, and their eye will not spare their sons. We find in Genesis (Gen 10) that Madai was the founder of the nation of the Medes, which means measure, or from the mighty one, or from the strong one. Therefore against the Babylonians, who are confused in mind, ministers of strength are stirred up by the mighty and strong God to punish, that they may render to each according to his works. For with the measure with which they have measured, it will be measured back to them. They will return into their bosom a measure shaken down and pressed together and full and running over (Matt 7, and Luke 6). They will receive neither silver nor gold, that is, neither beauty of eloquence nor sharpness of wit, in which they formerly applauded themselves; but they will afflict with punishments those handed over to them; and they will have no pity on the little ones and the sucklings of the womb, so that they may rather show pity. And would that we too might be stirred up by the Lord, and that this power might be given to us, that we should desire neither the silver nor the gold of worldly eloquence and wisdom, but should kill the sons of the heretics, and of all who have been deceived, with spiritual arrows, that is, with the testimonies of the Scriptures: and that those who are nourished with the milk of error may be slaughtered without any mercy, so that they may perish by a merciful cruelty, and that we may have pity on no infancy, and may be worthy of that beatitude: Blessed is he who will take hold of his little ones and dash them against the rock!

13:18ff.

And Babylon, that glorious one among kingdoms, renowned in the pride of the Chaldeans, will be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. It will not be inhabited to the end, and it will not be founded unto generation and generation: nor will the Arab pitch his tents there, nor will shepherds rest there: but wild beasts will rest there, and their houses will be filled with dragons: and ostriches will dwell there, and hairy ones will dance there; and owls will answer there in its dwellings, and sirens in the shrines of pleasure.

14:1

Its time is near to come, and its days will not be prolonged. LXX: And Babylon, which is called renowned, the glorious one of the king of the Chaldeans, will be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah; it will not be inhabited forever, nor will anyone enter it for many generations; nor will Arabs pass through it, nor will shepherds rest in it; but wild beasts will rest there, and the houses will be filled with noise, and sirens will lie down there, and demons will dance there, and onocentaurs will dwell there; and hedgehogs will make their dens in their houses. It will come quickly and will not delay. What follows: And its days will not be drawn out, ⁚ is to be marked with asterisks, because it was added from Theodotion. When the Medes have been stirred up against the city of confusion, who count neither gold nor silver among good things, who kill the little ones with arrows and have no pity on the sucklings of the womb, and whose eye does not spare their sons, the city once renowned, which was in the pride of the Chaldeans, who mean as demons, will be overthrown just as Sodom and Gomorrah were overthrown, so that no trace of its former dwelling remains in it: but after there has been a new heaven and a new earth, and the form of this world has passed away (1 Cor 7), the city of confusion will not be inhabited forever, and will by no means recover the same state. For after it has ceased to be in its former glory, the Arab, who means western and of the evening, will not pitch his tents there, so as to desire to dwell in that which he has seen to be deserted. Now the Arab in the present passage is taken in the good sense, because he always strains toward the end and, forgetting what lies behind, stretches himself out to what lies before. Nor will the shepherds rest there, who are accustomed to feed the most gentle flock of the Lord in Jerusalem; but on the contrary, wild beasts will rest there, which the Psalmist detests, saying: Do not deliver to the beasts the soul that confesses to you (Ps 73 [74]:19). For these Aquila and Symmachus and Theodotion set down the Hebrew word itself, SIIM (ציים). And their houses, that is, those of the Babylonians, will be filled, according to the Seventy and Theodotion, ἤχου, that is, with noise and clamors; according to Aquila, with typhoons, which we have turned into dragons; according to Symmachus, with OIIM (אחים), the word contained in the Hebrew. And ostriches will dwell there, an animal that always seeks out solitudes, of which more is written in Job: which, though it seems to have wings, yet is not lifted high above the earth: for which the Seventy translated σειρῆνας, that is, sirens. The hairy ones, who in Hebrew are called SIRIM (שעירים), Theodotion translated as with hair erect and standing up; Symmachus and the Seventy translated demons. For the onocentaurs too, which the Seventy alone translated, imitating the fables of the Gentiles, who say that there were hippocentaurs, the three other translators set down the Hebrew word itself, IIM (איים), which we have turned into owls. And where the Seventy said, hedgehogs will make their dens in their houses, and in the Hebrew THANNIM (תנים) is set down, Aquila and Symmachus and Theodotion translated sirens, signifying either some kind of beasts, or demons who, according to the error of the Gentiles, sing sweetly and deceive men who cannot pass through the shipwreck of this world with stopped ears. Moreover the name onocentaur, compounded of asses and centaurs, seems to me to signify those who in part have some human understanding, and again are drawn away into vices by pleasures and the mire of baseness. It is said, therefore, according to tropology, that at the end of the world, or of each one's death, all the glory and pride of the Chaldeans and the confusion of the world will depart from us; and that all things will be overthrown as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah; and that the state of this world will be no more, but will perish forever. Nor will the Arab pitch his tents there, of whom it is said in the sixty-seventh psalm: Make a way for him who rides upon the setting of the sun; the Lord is his name (Ps 67 [68]:5). Nor will the shepherds rest there, namely the angels who preside over the human race and daily see the face of the Father: but wild beasts and dragons and ostriches and hairy ones and owls and sirens will rest there, all of which beasts we understand figuratively as angels, or demons, and those to whom we are handed over for punishment. And in the houses once of pleasure, where there was gladness and joy, there will be the wailing of owls and the lamentable voice of the sirens, which leads its hearers to death. That the time of judgment is imminent, and that the day of the consummation of Babylon is not prolonged, he will by no means wonder who sees Babylon daily overthrown through holy men in those who believe in the Lord, and who sees that every length of time, compared with eternity, is near. Of the kinds of beasts, or rather of monsters, we have spoken briefly, because in the former book they were in part touched upon according to the history. This too is to be considered: that after the Church's preaching and the teaching of the Savior have overthrown the city of confusion, so that it is compared to Sodom and Gomorrah, it is not inhabited by holy men, nor do the shepherds rest in it who were accustomed to feed the flock of Christ: but on the contrary, wild beasts and dragons and ostriches rest there, and hairy ones dance in it. For whatever the heretics say in the synagogues of Satan is not the teaching of the Lord, but the howling of demons and of hairy ones, whom Esau imitated. And sirens will rest in the shrines of pleasure, who with sweet and deadly song draw souls down into the deep, so that, as the shipwreck rages, they may be devoured by wolves and dogs. Near, therefore, and pressing daily is the time of the ruin of the heretics, and their overthrow is not deferred.

For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose out of Israel, and will make them rest upon their own soil: the stranger will be joined to them, and will cleave to the house of Jacob. And the peoples will take them and bring them to their place: and the house of Israel will possess them upon the land of the Lord as menservants and maidservants; and they will take captive those who had taken them captive, and they will subdue their oppressors. And it will be in that day, when God has given you rest from your labor, and from your trouble, and from the hard bondage in which you served before: you will take up this parable against the king of Babylon, and you will say. For stranger, that is, proselyte, the Seventy translated γηώραν, which in Hebrew is called GER (גר). Hence I think that the son of Moses too, who was a stranger in the land, was named by his father Gersam (Exod 1). Therefore georas is a Hebrew word declined after Greek custom: although someone ignorant of the Hebrew tongue tries to express a Greek etymology in it, from the fact that it has the care of an earthly thing: for γῆ, he says, is the word for earth, and ὤρα, φροντὶς, that is, care. Again, for MASAL (משל), which Aquila and Symmachus and Theodotion translated parable, and whom we too have followed, the Seventy translated lament. Now the order is this: after Babylon has been deserted forever, so as to be a dwelling of wild beasts, the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, namely on him who supplanted vices; and he will choose Israel, him who beholds God with the mind. And note the propriety of the words: on Jacob, who is still set in the wrestling, he will have mercy; but to Israel, who received the name after the victory, not mercy but election is fitted. He will also make them rest upon their own land, of which the Savior speaks: Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the land (Matt 5:4), and I believe that I shall see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living (Ps 26 [27]:13). There will also be joined to the house of Jacob those who were chosen through the Apostles, the multitude of the nations; and they will take the remnant of the house of Israel and bring them to their own place, so that they may dwell in their tents; and the house of Israel will possess them upon the land of the Lord as menservants and maidservants. For it profits the wicked to serve the good. Hence it is said to Esau too: You shall serve your brother. And to Jacob: Your brother shall serve you (Gen 27). And they will take those who had formerly deceived them with sophistries: and they will reduce to bondage their oppressors, who do all things for the sake of gain. And after Jacob and Israel have rested from their labor, in which they had labored much fighting against the world and the heretics, and from their trouble and bondage, in which they had formerly served a malignant interpretation and false doctrines, then they will take up a lament and parable against the king of Babylon, namely the discourse of heretical error and confusion, and will say what follows. The Jews interpret this passage carnally, but they will not be able to show that it came to pass after they returned from Babylon. For neither did the Babylonians, who had first taken them captive, serve them; nor, when the Babylonians were conquered, did they possess their houses; nor did they have them as menservants and maidservants. It remains, therefore, that according to their fables they think this will come about in respect of this Roman empire: that when the Romans have been overcome in the last time, the nations whom they formerly served will serve them. But if, by following the letter, they deceive themselves with a false hope, who will grant them that Rome is called Babylon, and Nebuchadnezzar the king of the Roman empire?

14:5-6

How has the oppressor ceased, the tribute come to rest? The Lord has broken the staff of the ungodly, the rod of the rulers, which struck the peoples in indignation with an incurable stroke, which subdued the nations in fury, persecuting cruelly. In the Epistle of Peter we read: It is time for judgment to begin at the house of God (1 Pet 4:17). And in Ezekiel it is said to the tormentors: Begin at my holy ones (Ezek 9:6). For the order of judgment is arranged according to the diversity of sin, so that those who have offended less are purged first. And the last enemy to be destroyed is death. Therefore, when Israel has been freed from hard bondage, he will take up a parable against the king of Babylon, which we ought to understand as a parable. For if the discourse is against Nebuchadnezzar, and a simple exposition of the history, how is it called a parable, when it παραβάλλεται, that is, is compared, to nothing else? Israel therefore wonders how the oppressor has ceased, who was accustomed to exact payment down to the last farthing. And he was accustomed to exact from none but debtors, who say in the Lord's Prayer: Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors (Matt 6:12). To this exactor debtors are handed over by the judge, who sends them into prison and exacts down to the least sin. Accordingly Paul the apostle too handed over to the exactor the Corinthian fornicator, who had taken his father's wife, and also Phygellus and Hermogenes (1 Cor 5; 2 Tim 1). And of these exactors it is also said above: My people, your oppressors plunder you; and those who demand payment rule over you. For tribute Aquila translated famine. For since the bridegroom has been taken from us, we suffer a famine of the word of God and fast continually from the body of the Lord. And for this reason the rod and staff of the ungodly, for which the Seventy translated yoke, strikes us, or oppresses us, because we would not bear the lightest yoke, the yoke of the Savior. And with this staff and this rod he struck the nations with incurable fury, and cruelly pursued those who fled: not wishing to amend those handed over to him, but to kill them.

14:7ff.

The whole earth has come to rest and fallen silent; it has rejoiced and exulted; the fir trees too have rejoiced over you, and the cedars of Lebanon. Since you have fallen asleep, no one comes up to cut us down. Hell beneath was troubled: to meet your coming it stirred up the giants for you. All the princes of the earth have risen from their thrones; all the princes of the nations, all of them will answer and say to you: You too have been wounded as we were, you have become like us? Your pride has been dragged down to hell, your corpse has fallen; beneath you the moth will be spread, decay, and worms will be your covering. At the destruction of the ungodly king, who struck the nations with an incurable stroke and pursued them cruelly, the whole earth came to rest and fell silent, which before was full of tumults and sedition, so much so that the fir trees and the cedars of Lebanon rejoiced, of which it is written in the psalms: You brought a vine out of Egypt, you cast out the nations and planted it. Its shade covered the mountains, and its branches the cedars of God (Ps 79 [80]:9). These cedars of God, because at one time they sinned, the Lord handed over to punishments to be broken. Hence in another psalm it is said: The Lord will break the cedars of Lebanon (Ps 28 [29]:5). And the fir trees ought to be taken as all the lofty, those who are sublime in the service of the Lord, who said with harmonious voice: Since you have fallen asleep. Note that even the death of death is called a sleeping. No one comes up to cut us down. For when the strong man has been overcome and his vessels plundered, the rest of his attendants also have fallen. Hence the Lord too says in the Gospel (Matt 25:41): Depart into the eternal fire, which has been prepared for the devil and his angels. How many have these fellers of timber and trees cut down with their axes and made to fall? Hell too, troubled, or turned to bitterness, to meet the coming of the true Nebuchadnezzar, is the place of punishments and torments, in which the rich man clothed in purple is seen: to which the Lord also descended, to release the bound from prison. We can also call hell, coming to meet him, that angel who is set over the punishments of hell, who stirred up all the giants: for which some have translated Raphaim, others Titans. And they are called giants according to the custom of the heathen, who suppose them earth-born, whom the earth begot. But we, according to the etymology of the Greek word, can call giants those who have served earthly works. Then there follows: All the princes of the earth have risen from their thrones, at the coming of their former prince: so that him whom they formerly honored for his power they might afterward marvel at in punishments, and say: You too have been wounded as we also were: you have become like us. These words have this sense: We thought that we, because of our weakness, had not been able to resist the power of God, and that you alone were the one who would remain in your loftiness; but, as the facts show, you too have been wounded and taken, and have become like us; so that those whom rank separated on earth, punishment unites in hell. Your pride has been dragged down to hell, or your glory, and your corpse has fallen, or, as the Seventy translated, your great gladness, in which you formerly rejoiced when the nations were subject to you. Beneath you decay will be spread, and worms will be your covering. This is the rest of the devil, this the bed of the tempter, who was lifted up into such pride that he dared even to tempt the Lord, saying: All these I will give you, if you will fall down and worship me (Matt 4:9). The decay and the moth and the covering of worms are understood either as the eternal punishments which one's own conscience begets, or as the material of torments, which is born from one's own sins. For just as, so long as there is matter in a corpse and any moisture in the corpse, worms are born from decay, so from the very matter of sins torments are begotten. Hence the Apostle Paul too, death having been slain, to which the prophetic word spoke through Hosea: I will be your death, O death; I will be your bite, O hell (Hos 13:14), says to it: Where is your contention, O death? Where is your sting, O death (1 Cor 15:55)? For when it is dead, there is no one to cut us down: for there will by no means be sin that must be cut down, since the sting of death is sin.

14:12

How have you fallen from heaven, Lucifer, who rose in the morning? You have crashed to the earth, you who wounded the nations? LXX: How has Lucifer fallen from heaven, who rose in the morning? He who sent to all the nations has been crushed to the earth. For Lucifer, who in Hebrew is called ELIL (הילל), Aquila translated howling son of the dawn. For truly he ought to howl and wail, who because of his pride was cast headlong from heaven to earth and crushed. Hence the Savior too says to the disciples: I saw Satan falling like lightning from heaven (Luke 10:18). Not, I see now; but I saw before, when he fell. And if he fell from so great a height because of pride, you too ought not to glory because the demons are subject to you, but because your names are written in heaven; so that whence he fell through pride, you may ascend through humility. This is the prince of the world, who rose in the morning among the other stars, and by his own fault was made from Lucifer into Vesper, and not rising but setting: who wounded the nations, or who sent his attendants to the nations, to deceive all by his fraud. These are the false apostles, deceitful workers, who transform themselves into Apostles of Christ, who sow darnel over the good seed while the teachers of the Churches sleep and are unwilling or unable to resist their malice. And Jacob, and Israel, on whom the Lord has had mercy and whom he has chosen, still says these things to the devil, or, as the Seventy will have it, about the devil, that is, not in the second person but in the third.

14:13-14

You who said in your heart: I will ascend into heaven, above the stars of God I will exalt my throne: I will sit on the mountain of the covenant, on the sides of the North: I will ascend above the height of the clouds, I will be like the Most High. He said these things either before he fell from heaven or after he had fallen from heaven. If he was still set in heaven, how does he say, I will ascend into heaven (Ps 113 [115]:16)? But because we read: The heaven of heaven is the Lord's, when he was in heaven, that is, in the firmament, he desired to ascend into the heaven where the throne of the Lord is, not by humility but by pride. But if he speaks these words after he fell from heaven, we ought to understand arrogance: that even when cast down he does not rest, but still promises himself great things, to be not among the stars but above the stars of God. And while the Lord says to the Apostles: It is enough for the disciple to be as his master, and for the servant as his lord (Matt 10:25), and says to the Father: Holy Father, grant that as I and you are one, so these also may be one in us (John 17:11), this one arrogates so much to himself that he boasts he will set his throne above the stars of heaven, which have not fallen. And what he adds: I will sit on the mountain of the covenant, on the sides of the North, for which the Seventy translated, on a lofty mountain, above the high mountains which are toward the North, let us refer to what is said in Jeremiah: From the North evils will blaze forth upon all the inhabitants of the earth (Jer 1:14). And that the pot set on fire is kindled from the face of the North. This is the North, the harshest wind, from which the Lord wishes to free his captives and bring them back into the holy city, saying: I will say to the North, Bring; and to the South-west wind, Do not hold back; bring my sons from a distant land (below, Isa 43:6). But that which can seem contrary to this, the mountains of Zion, the sides of the North, the city of the great king, is easily resolved. For those who once were in the sides of the North, most hardened, afterward through penance began to be in the city of God. Always a Lucifer of this sort seeks to ascend above those who bear the image of the heavenly, and who shine in the Church like the stars of God: and to sit on the mountain of the pact or covenant, that is, in the Church, which is set on high and possesses inhabitants who were once from the sides of the North. He has so forgotten himself that he wishes to ascend above the clouds, which the Lord commanded not to rain rain upon Israel, and to which the truth of the Lord reaches, to whom Obadiah also says: Though you be exalted like the eagle, and set your nest among the stars of heaven, thence I will drag you down, says the Lord (Obad 4). Unhappy Judas, who like a cloud was sent with the other Apostles to rain rain upon Israel, and was like a star among the other stars, to whom the Lord said: Let your light shine before men (Matt 5:16), by his own fault received the devil as his rider, who, to complete his words of pride, dared even to say this: I will be like the Most High, so that, as Christ has his Prophets and Apostles, so I too may have false apostles. All these things are to be referred to the heretics, who, though they are below, boast with their prince that they are on high.

14:15

But you will be dragged down to hell, into the depth of the pit. LXX: But now you will go down into hell, and to the foundations of the earth. You will not go down to hell of your own accord, for this belongs to the Lord the Savior, to free the bound from hell, but you will be dragged down to hell against your will, so that you who could have climbed to the heights through virtues are dragged down to punishments through vices. The saints have the wings of an eagle and the wings of a dove, and can say: I will fly away and be at rest (Ps 54 [55]). But the ungodly, like the Egyptians, sank like lead in the mighty waters, and sank into the depth like a stone (Exod 15). Hence also iniquity, or, as it is better in the Hebrew, ungodliness, is seen sitting upon a talent of lead (Zech 5). Therefore what we read elsewhere: Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled (Luke 18:14), the king of confusion also suffered, so that he was dragged down to the foundations of the earth, or, as it is more truly in the Hebrew, into the depth of the pit. Of the foundations of the earth it is written in Deuteronomy: A fire has been kindled in my fury, it will burn down to the lowest hell. It will devour the earth and its foundations (Deut 32:22), namely those who are earthly. Of the pit too, that by it the depths of hell are signified, these are the testimonies: I am counted with those who go down into the pit. And: They have laid me in the lowest pit (Ps 87 [88]:5, 7). For just as a pit receives the waters that run down into it, so hell receives souls: into which pit Benaiah went down in the time of snow and cold and slew a lion in it (2 Sam 23, and 1 Chr 11). Hence the heretics too forsake the Lord, the fountain of living water, and dig for themselves broken pits which cannot hold water. Of these pits, which do not have the fervor of the Holy Spirit, and are not like the prophet Jeremiah, who according to the Seventy translators said: I found warm water in the desert (Jer 2), but, as love grew cold, have lost the warmth of the Holy Spirit: that is the pit of which the same Jeremiah speaks: As a pit cools water, so wickedness cools those who have it (Jer 6:7). Would that they, according to the Apocalypse of John, were either hot or cold (Rev 3), that is, either believed or did not believe at all, lest through lukewarmness and the pretense of faith they be cast out by the Lord!

14:16-17

Those who see you will bow down to you, and will look closely at you. Is this the man who troubled the earth? who shook kingdoms? who made the world a desert, and destroyed its cities, and did not open the prison to its prisoners? Or, as the Seventy translated: did not release those who were being led away? Those who see Nebuchadnezzar, the Babylonian king, fallen from heaven to hell, with the gaze not of the eyes but of the heart, will bow down in the humility which is contrary to pride, and will look closely at him, saying these things: Is not this the man, or the human being, who troubled, or stirred up the earth? And the sense is this: he who had said, I will be like the Most High, and boasted himself God, is proved to be a man, of whom it is said in the ninth psalm, which is properly against the devil: Arise, O Lord, let not man prevail (Ps 9:20). And in the Gospel: An enemy man sowed tares over it (Matt 13:25). Hence we read it said to him and his companions: I said, You are gods, and all sons of the Most High. But you will die like men, and you will fall like one of the princes (Ps 81 [82]:6). And to the same, under the figure of the prince of Tyre, it is said: Because your heart has been exalted, and you have said, I am God, I have dwelt in the dwelling of God in the heart of the sea: yet you are a man and not God, and you have set your heart as the heart of God (Ezek 28:2). This man, this human being, troubled the whole earth, namely those who hear with Adam: Earth you are, and into earth you shall go (Gen 3:19), and shook kingdoms, or kings, whose heart is in the hand of the Lord (Prov 21). He shook them, it says, he did not overthrow them. Hence one of those who had been shaken, and yet had not fallen, said: But my feet were almost moved (Ps 72 [73]:2). And the Apostle tells believers to take up the armor of God and stand against the snares of the devil (Eph 6). But the house that is founded upon the rock is shaken by no storm (Matt 7). There follows: Who made the world a desert, or, as according to the Hebrew all the others besides the Seventy translated, as a desert. For by vices and sins he made the world, which in Hebrew is called THEBEL (תבל), a desert, so that it had no virtue, or was subject to the same vices with which the solitude of the nations is filled. He also destroyed the cities of that same world, to make synagogues of the devil out of the Churches of Christ, and to pollute the purity of the true faith with heretical filth. But also to its prisoners, that is, the world's, he did not open the prison. We were all prisoners, and were held shut up in prison, to which prisoners the Savior said, come out, and to those who were in darkness, be uncovered. For the Lord sets free those in fetters. And those freed by him give thanks, saying: You have broken my bonds (Ps 115 [116]:17; Jer 2, Prov 5). For each one is bound fast with the cords of his own sins: and these cords and bonds the Apostles too can loose, imitating their master, who had said to them: Whatever you loose upon earth will be loosed also in heaven (Matt 18). And the Apostles loose them by the word of God, and by the testimonies of the Scriptures, and by exhortation to the virtues.

14:18-19

All the kings of the nations, all of them, have slept in glory, each one in his own house. But you have been cast out of your tomb like corrupt matter: polluted, wrapped up with the slain and those pierced through by the sword, who go down to the stones of the pit. LXX: All the kings of the nations have slept in honor, a man in his own house. But you will be cast out on the mountains like an untimely birth, abominable, and wrapped up with those slain by the sword who go down to the foundations of the earth. The kings of the nations, to whom, according to the Song of Deuteronomy, God had entrusted the nations to be governed (Deut 32), who were shaken by Nebuchadnezzar and yet not overthrown, in whom sin by no means reigns; but because their heart was in the hand of God, they did not fall at all. For indeed the Savior, just as he is called God of gods, so too is he Lord of lords and King of kings. These kings, then, all of them, have rested in their glory, each one in his own house. For with the Father there are diverse mansions (John 14): and according to the variety of the virtues, differences of dwellings. But Nebuchadnezzar has been cast out of his tomb, and not even in death has he rested from torments. And he has been cast out like corrupt matter, which in Hebrew is called NESER (נצר), which Aquila translated ἰχῶρα, namely putrefaction and filth, which Symmachus translated ἔκτρωμα, that is, an untimely birth, the Seventy a dead thing, Theodotion a shoot: although this very word above (Isa 11:1), where we read of Christ: A rod will come forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower will rise up from its root, the Seventy translated flower, Theodotion shoot, Aquila ἀκρέμονα, that is, sucker. Properly, however, Neser means sucker, which grows at the roots of trees and, torn off by farmers, is thrown away as useless; hence we too translated useless stock. Therefore Nebuchadnezzar, like a useless stock prepared for burning, or polluted like corrupt matter, and wrapped up with those who were slain by him with the sword and went down to the foundations of the pit, will be dragged down into the depth, and will not have fellowship in burial even with those whom he slew. For the punishment of the author of an offense is one thing, and that of him who was compelled by the author another. This is the sword by which very many have been wounded and slain, of which we read in the seventh psalm: Unless you are converted, he will brandish his sword; he has bent his bow and made it ready. And in it he has prepared the instruments of death: he has made his arrows for those who burn (Ps 7:13, 14), namely for those who have received into their heart the fiery darts of the devil. But according to the Seventy, the corpse of Nebuchadnezzar, polluted and pierced through, will lie with very many slain on the mountains of pride, and will be led down to hell. And Symmachus translated foundations of the pit in place of stones of the pit, to signify in other words the depth and the Tartarus of hell.

14:20

Like a putrid corpse, you will not have fellowship with them even in burial. For you have destroyed your land, you have slain your people. LXX: As a garment mixed with blood will not be clean, so neither will you be clean, because you have destroyed my land and have slain my people. Since the Hebrew and the edition of the Seventy differ greatly from each other, let us discuss each separately. Like a putrid corpse, or, as Aquila translated, trampled, you will not have fellowship of burial, not even with those whom you slew. For you are the teacher, they were the disciples: and from him to whom more has been entrusted, more is required. For you have destroyed your land, you have killed your people, namely those who were entrusted to you to govern. Hence he dares to say to the Savior: All these have been delivered to me, and I will give them to you, if you will fall down and worship me (Matt 4:9). And that the corpse of the devil is putrid because of the greatness of his sins, he will not be able to doubt who reads that sin is most foul-smelling, the sinner himself saying: My scars have putrefied and are corrupted because of my foolishness (Ps 37 [38]:6). On the contrary, virtue is of a good odor: hence the love of spiritual brethren is also compared to ointment, which runs down upon the beard, the beard of Aaron, and upon the border of his garment (Ps 132 [133]). And the bridegroom says to the bride: Your odor is sweet, and your face is comely (Song 2:14). And how the corpse of the devil is spiritually trampled, that saying of the Apostle teaches us: God will crush Satan under your feet swiftly (Rom 16:20). And the words of the Lord, who says: I will blot them out like the mud of the streets (Ps 17 [18]:43). This one, because he has destroyed the land entrusted to him, and slaughtered the people committed to him, by no means keeping them alive for God but preparing them as companions of his burial, therefore the seed of the most wicked will not be, nor will it be named, forever. But according to the Seventy it has this sense: O Lucifer, who rose in the morning, who, when you had the works of virtue and of light, were the garment of God, and of whom it could be said: Clothed with light as with a garment (Ps 103 [104]:2): because you have slain many with the sword who went down to hell, and have been polluted with their blood, you will by no means be called the garment of God, but a garment mixed with gore, not stained and polluted, so that you might seem to have something clean, but wholly bloodied with blood. And this is to be noted, that it is said to the devil: as a garment mixed with blood will not be clean, so neither will you be clean. Where then are those who grant the devil penance, and say that he can be made clean? Nor do we on that account at once concede the heresy which asserts that there are diverse natures, and that there is one which never receives healing. For this garment, with which God was once clothed, is not unclean of itself, and was not so made by God; but because it is mixed with blood, and has wholly polluted itself by its own fault, and with evils added to it, it will not be clean. And it will not be clean for this reason: because it has destroyed the land of the Lord and slain his people, destroying and slaying the land of Judea and the land of confession and all the saints: and therefore it will not remain forever. Hence also in the Gospel it is said: Depart into the eternal fire, which has been prepared for the devil and his angels (Matt 25:41). And just as the saint is the garment of God, and a new garment, and is clothed with the tunic of salvation and of gladness, saying: Let my soul exult in the Lord: for he has clothed me with the garment of salvation, and has surrounded me with the tunic of gladness (Isa 61:10), so on the contrary the sinner, who bears the image of the old and earthly man, deserves to hear: Behold, all of you will grow old like a garment, and the moth will devour you (Isa 50:9). But he who has advanced in wickedness, and has been unwilling to cleanse his oldness by newness, will be compared not to an old garment but to the rag of a menstruous woman, saying: We have gone astray, and we have all become unclean; all our righteousness is like the rag of a menstruous woman.

14:21-22

Seed of the most wicked, prepare your sons for slaughter for the iniquities of their fathers: they will not rise up nor inherit the land, nor fill the face of the world with cities. And I will rise up against them, says the Lord of hosts: and I will destroy the name of Babylon and its remnant, and its offshoot and offspring, says the Lord of hosts. LXX: Most wicked seed, prepare your sons for slaughter for the sin of your father: that they may not rise up and possess the land, and fill the land with cities. And I will rise up against them, says the Lord Sabaoth: and I will destroy their name and remnant and seed. For most wicked seed, which the Seventy translated, in the Hebrew is written ZERA MRIM (זרע מרעים), which the others translated seed of the most wicked. Not that the seed itself is evil of itself: for God made all things good (Gen 1); but that from those who are most wicked by their own will an evil seed has sprung, which comes about by will, not by nature. Hence we read in Daniel too: Seed of Canaan, and not of Judah (Dan 13:56). And of good sons it is said by the Apostle: In Christ Jesus through the Gospel I have begotten you (1 Cor 4:15). And in the Gospel: As many as received him, to them he gave power to become sons of God (John 1:12). For everyone who commits sin is of the devil. To this seed, therefore, it is commanded that it prepare for slaughter its sons, namely all most wicked thoughts and evil works, which were born of ungodly fathers, who beyond doubt signify the hostile powers. These most wicked sons are slaughtered in the iniquities of their fathers for this reason: that they may no longer rise up and possess the land, which is to be possessed and filled by the saints, so that cities of the Lord may be built in it. And since the victory of men is not perfect: For unless the Lord guards the city, those who guard it will keep watch in vain (Ps 126 [127]:1): therefore the Lord himself will rise up against the sons of the most wicked, and will destroy out of confusion their name and remnant, and every offshoot and offspring, so that they may no longer sprout in the cities of the Lord. We read in the Gospel (John 8) that the devil is a liar from the beginning, and his father, that is, of the lie; which many not understanding wish the father of the devil to be the dragon who reigns in the sea, whom the Hebrews call Leviathan. And they think this suits the present passage according to the Seventy translators, who said: for the sins of your father: whereas in the Hebrew ABOTHAM (אבתם) plainly signifies not of your father but of their fathers.

14:23

And I will make it a possession of the hedgehog, and pools of waters: and I will sweep it with a broom, grinding it, says the Lord of hosts. LXX: And I will make Babylonia desert, says the Lord, so that hedgehogs dwell in it, and it will come to nothing. And I will make it a gulf of mud, for destruction. When the Lord of hosts has destroyed the name of Babylon, and its remnant, and its offshoot, and all its offspring, he will not be content with its destruction unless he gives it as a possession to the hedgehog, and as pools of waters, and sweeps it, not lightly and casually, but grinding, so that nothing of its old filth remains in it. In the Acts of the Apostles it is written (Acts 10 and 11) that in that linen vessel which, let down by four corners, hung from heaven, all kinds of four-footed beasts and creeping things and birds were contained; which the Apostle afterward explaining says: God has shown me that I should call no man unclean. The characters of men, therefore, were shown in the various animals, just as the Pharisees and Sadducees are called a brood of vipers because of their wickedness, and Herod is called a fox because of his deceits (Luke 3 and 13); and the luxurious and those prone to pleasure are called horses, mad after women (Jer 5): and, Do not become like the horse and the mule, in which there is no understanding (Ps 31 [32]). On the contrary, the innocent are called doves and sheep. Therefore, according to the teaching of the Lord the Savior, who called the cares of this world and the seduction of riches thorns, the hedgehog seems to me to be he who, according to the Apostle, rejoices in the uncertainty of riches (1 Tim 6), and trusts that he is armed, not with the armor of God, but with the thorns and sins of this world, to whom that word of the Gospel is most rightly said: Fool, this night your soul will be taken from you; and what you have prepared, whose will it be (Luke 12:20)? Such inhabitants has Babylon, deserted of virtues, where there is no well-watered field to bear the fruits of various seeds, but barren pools, slimy and muddy, in which animals that delight in mire creep. For this reason the most merciful Lord swept it, grinding most vehemently, and as with a kind of drag-net cleansed it down to the bare ground, so that the Babylonian seeds might perish and it might be inhabited by hedgehogs alone. When we see anyone sunk in the mud of riches, and, as the Seventy translated, in the gulf, that is, in a deep whirlpool, and surrounded as it were by a miry pool, let us not hesitate to call him a hedgehog, an inhabitant of deserted Babylon.

14:24-25

The Lord of hosts has sworn, saying: Surely as I have thought, so shall it be, and as I have purposed in my mind, so shall it come to pass: that I will crush the Assyrian in my land, and on my mountains I will trample him. And his yoke will be taken from them, and his burden will be removed from their shoulder. After the hedgehog has dwelt in deserted Babylon, and in place of well-watered and fertile fields pools have covered everything, so that nothing of the former seed and abundance remains in Babylon, the oath of the Lord will be fulfilled, and what he purposed in his mind will come to pass: that the Assyrian is crushed in his land and trampled on his mountains. For the reckless enemy hastens to seize not only the land of God and all its lower places, but also those who in the service of God have so advanced in virtues that they are compared to mountains, and it is said of them: Its foundations are on the holy mountains (Ps 86 [87]:1). And note the propriety. In the land he is crushed; on the mountains of God he is trampled by the Lord himself. For when all enemies have been put under the feet of Christ, so that the last, death, is destroyed, then the most heavy yoke of the Assyrian, with which he had formerly weighed them down, will be taken from the saints, and the burden, or, as the Seventy translated, κῦδος, that is, glory, will be removed from their shoulder, so that, the yoke of the Assyrians having been taken away, they may see rest, that it is good, and the land, that it is most fruitful, and may put their necks under the yoke of Christ for labor, and become men who till the soil. Hence also Issachar, which means there is a reward, received his name from the virtues. And in the Prophet we read: There is a reward for those who serve the Lord (Jer 31:16); and in another place: Behold the Lord, and his reward is with him (Isa 40:10), who will render to each according to his work. And that the Assyrians, that is, the hostile powers, are crushed and trampled, that word of the Gospel also teaches: Behold, I have given you power to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and upon all the power of the enemy (Luke 10:19). And the words of the Apostle bear witness: God will crush Satan under your feet swiftly (Rom 16:20).

14:26-27

This is the counsel which he has purposed upon the whole earth, and this is the hand stretched out upon all the nations. For the Lord of hosts has decreed, and who will be able to weaken it? And his hand is stretched out, and who will turn it back? For the whole earth the Seventy translated the whole world, at the end of the burden, or vision, against Babylon. What lay hidden is opened: that God purposed his counsel upon the whole earth, that is, the whole world, and not only against the land of the Chaldeans and the Assyrian and Chaldean king; and that his hand is stretched out, or raised, upon all the nations, and not upon the one Babylonian nation. From this it is shown that all the things which have been said pertain not specifically to one province, but generally to the whole world. And what is said: Who will be able to weaken it, and who will turn it back? we ought to take not as of something difficult, as that is read: Who is wise, and will understand these things (Ps 106 [107]:43)? And: Who, do you think, is the faithful and prudent steward (Luke 12:42)? and other things like these; but as of something impossible. For no one will be able to weaken the counsel of the Lord, and to turn back his hand, stretched out or lifted on high, from striking.

14:28ff.

In the year in which King Ahaz died, this burden came. Do not rejoice, all you Philistia, because the rod of him who struck you has been broken. For out of the root of the serpent will come forth a basilisk, and its seed swallowing the bird. And the firstborn of the poor will be fed, and the poor will rest confidently, and I will make your root perish with famine, and I will slay your remnant. LXX: In the year in which King Ahaz died this word came: Do not rejoice, all you foreigners, for the yoke of him who struck you has been broken. For out of the seed of the serpent will come forth the offspring of asps, and out of their offspring will come forth winged serpents: and the poor will be fed through him, and poor men will rest in peace. But he will slay your seed with famine, and will kill your remnant. When Ahaz, who is interpreted κατάσχεσις, that is, holding, or possession, whom we read was a most ungodly king, had died, this weight, or word, comes upon the Philistines. For while he lived and reigned among sinners, neither a weight against the foreigners nor the word of God could come to the Prophet. Indeed I remember having said this above too, when, Uzziah having died, Isaiah saw the Lord sitting upon a throne high and lifted up. And in Exodus we read (Exod 2:23) that after the king of Egypt died, the children of Israel groaned from their works, and cried out, and their cry went up from their works, and the Lord heard their groaning. For unless what was said were mystical, they ought rather to have cried out while he was reigning, when they were slaving at mud and bricks. It is commanded, therefore, to the Philistines, whom they now call Palestinians, and whom the Seventy always translate ἀλλόφυλοι, that is, foreigners; and it is said to them that they should not rejoice nor be glad because they have broken the rod, or the yoke, of him who struck them (Heb 12:6). For whom the Lord loves he rebukes, and he chastises every son whom he receives. And God instructs us as sons when he visits our iniquities with a rod and our sins with scourges, so as not to take away his mercy from us (Ps 88 [89]). This is the rod of which it is written in another Psalm: Your rod and your staff, they have comforted me (Ps 22 [23]:4). This is the rod, and this the yoke, which the Savior wishes to lay upon the necks of all, so that, having put off the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar, they may bear the yoke of Christ. But if anyone throws it off and breaks it, at once out of the seed or root of the serpent, who is the crooked serpent, will come forth the basilisk and asps, and out of the asps will go forth flying serpents, or those that swallow birds. For when the yoke of God has been thrown off and the discipline of the Lord broken, first the seed of the serpent takes root in our thoughts; secondly, from the most evil seed is born the basilisk, which is the king of serpents and is said to kill men by its breath and its look; or the offspring of asps, of which it is said in the Psalm: The poison of asps is under their lips (Ps 13 [14]:3; and 139 [140]:4), which are the various sins, and they burst forth from the most evil treasury of thoughts into evil works. And when they have reigned in foreign men, who are estranged from God, at once winged serpents come forth; so that it is not enough for them to have thought and done what is evil, unless they also seek a defense of their evil works and fashion various heresies. I think the winged serpents are those who exalt and lift themselves up against the knowledge of God and set their mouth against heaven: or those who swallow birds, that is, who with poisoned mouth devour in their jaws all who desire to fly and rise to the heights. And this, for the present, concerning the wicked. But those who have not broken the rod and yoke of him who struck them, but have submitted their neck to the Lord, and are poor in spirit, will be fed, and will say: The Lord feeds me, and I shall lack nothing (Ps 22 [23]:1). And they will hear from the Lord: In most rich pastures I will feed them (Ezek 34; John 10); and they will go in and go out and find pasture. And the poor will be fed through him who strikes them in order to amend them: and they will rest in peace, or, with a careful shepherd, they will live confidently and will rest with Lazarus in the bosom of Abraham (Luke 16). But those who have broken the yoke and rod of him who struck them will suffer perpetual famine, so that they are not nourished by the word of God: but all their remnant will perish, lest anything sprout from the evil seed.

14:31-32

Howl, O gate; cry out, O city: all Philistia is laid low. For smoke comes from the North, and there is none who escapes its column. And what will be answered to the messengers of the nation? That the Lord has founded Zion, and in him the poor of his people will hope. For messengers, that is, Angels, which Symmachus alone translated, all have translated kings, deceived by the ambiguity of the word, because, except for the one letter ALEPH, which is added in the word for Angels, kings and Angels are called by the same name among the Hebrews, that is, MALACHE (Kings מלכי, Angels מלאכי). In the book of Hebrew Names I have found that Philisthiim means falling by the cup. Those, therefore, who have been made drunk with the cup of Babylon and have drunk the wine in which is debauchery, and, among the other vices, have not obtained the kingdom of God because of drunkenness, according to the Apostle (Eph 5), are commanded that their gate should howl and their city cry out. The gate I take to be the mouth of the heretics, with which they blaspheme; the city, the soul, which is a treasury of evil thoughts. This ought to howl and lament, because it is wholly laid low and cast down to the ground, and there is nothing in it of sound understanding and of the wisdom of God. Why does the gate howl? for what cause does the city cry out? because all Philistia is laid low. And why it is laid low the following verse shows: Smoke comes from the North, and there is none who escapes its column. This smoke is raised by the burning darts of the devil; it is harmful to the eyes and contrary to light, and it rises from the North, from which in Jeremiah the pot is set on fire (Jer 1:14), and from which evils blaze forth upon all the inhabitants of the earth, who cannot say: I am a sojourner and a stranger, as all my fathers were (Ps 118 [119]:19); but they dwell in the earth. Hence in Proverbs too it is read: The North is a harsh wind (Prov 25:23; Sir 43). But by another name it is called the right-hand wind; for although of itself it is harsh and left-handed, and with a most hard neck will not receive the yoke of God, it is called right-handed by those who put sweet for bitter and bitter for sweet; who put darkness for light and light for darkness. And there is no one who escapes the column of this smoke; for no one is without sin, not even if his life be of a single day (Job 25). And when Philistia has fallen, and its smoke has penetrated all things, so that no one can escape it, what will be said to the Angels who preside over the several nations, who wonder and desire to know why Zion alone, set on a watchtower and on the heights, has escaped the bitterness of this smoke? What, then, will be said to them? Surely what follows: That the Lord has founded it, and he himself is its foundation. And he has founded it upon the foundation of prudence, righteousness, fortitude and temperance, under which names Christ is understood, of whom the Apostle also says: For no one can lay another foundation besides that which has been laid, Jesus Christ (1 Cor 3:11). But he who is foolish, and speaks foolish things, and whose heart understands vain things, builds his house upon the sand, which has no foundation. In this Zion, therefore, which has been founded by the Lord, the poor, or the meek and humble of his people, will hope, of whom it is said: Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the land (Matt 5:4): and who have heard the Lord saying: Learn from me, for I am meek and humble of heart (Matt 11:29). They have been humbled before glory, and have heard the apostle Peter saying (1 Pet 5:6): Humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in the time of visitation. And these are the poor of whom we read above: The firstborn of the poor will be fed, and the poor will rest confidently.

15:1

The burden of Moab. LXX: The word against the land of Moab. Symmachus and Theodotion: The taking up of Moab. Just as circumcision is both carnal and spiritual, and of the spiritual it is said by the Apostle: For we are the circumcision, who serve God in the spirit, and glory in the Lord, and put no confidence in the flesh (Phil 3:3); and again, to distinguish the spiritual Israel, it is said of the carnal: Behold Israel according to the flesh (1 Cor 10:18): and, You Gentiles in the flesh (Eph 2:11); so Moab is to be taken spiritually, which means from the father, or paternal water, conceived of incest and drunkenness, because he would seem to have been begotten in a manner in the absence, or rather without the knowledge, of the father. In many places of the Scriptures we read of Moab, and especially in the volume of Numbers, when Balak, king of the Moabites, invited Balaam the soothsayer to curse, who among other things prophesied also this mystical word against Moab: A star will rise out of Jacob, and a man will rise up out of Israel, and will strike the princes of Moab (Num 24:17).

15:1

Because by night Ar has been laid waste, Moab has fallen silent; because by night the wall has been laid waste, Moab has fallen silent. LXX: By night the land of Moab perished, for by night the wall of the land of Moab perished. For AR (ער), which Theodotion alone set down thus, as it is read in the Hebrew, Aquila and Symmachus translated city, not considering that between the Hebrew letters AIN and RES it does not have the letter JOD, which, if it were there, would rightly be read as city. Worldly wisdom, of which the Lord speaks through the Prophet: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the prudence of the prudent I will reject (Obad 8; 1 Cor 1:19), because it has as its author the mind, which is begotten by God's creating, seems indeed to be born of the father, which is what Moab means; but because it is adulterous and an adversary to the people of God, it is begotten of incest, of a cave and of night. Hence it perished by night, namely in everlasting error. The Egyptians too in the Red Sea were overwhelmed by the waves at the morning watch, which indicates the time of night (Exod 14). And Lot, while the Sodomites were perishing by night, came to Zoar, and the sun rose for him (Gen 19). Understanding this, the blessed Apostle writes of the saints and the perfect (1 Thess 5:6, 7): We are not of the night nor of darkness, but we are sons of the day. For those who sleep sleep by night, and those who are drunk are drunk by night. But let us who are of the day keep watch, clothed with the breastplate of faith and love. And because he had left the night and had already begun to be a son of the day, he says to believers: The night has gone before, and the day has drawn near; let us walk honestly as in the day, not in revelings and drunkenness, not in chambering and wantonness (Rom 13:12). And when the land of Moab perishes by night, its wall too, which was built by the art of dialectic, was laid waste and destroyed in the same night, and fell silent in eternal silence. Moreover Ar, which means ἀντίδικος, that is, adversary, shows this: that this wisdom, which is the adversary of God, has been overcome by the Church's preaching fighting against it.

15:2

The house has gone up, and Dimon, to the high places, to lament. LXX: Be sorrowful within yourselves, for Dimon will perish, where the altar is: thither you will go up to weep. The whole house of hostile wisdom, and Dibon, which means their flowing, goes up to the high places in which it had grown proud: not to sacrifice victims, but to lament the things in which it had formerly sinned. And truly falsehood passes like a river, and flows by, and can never stand firm in a stable dwelling. But the word of God, which is compacted, is stable. Hence the manna too, which is seen like ice upon the face of the earth, does not flow away, but stands firm. Moreover, according to the Seventy, the Moabites are commanded to grieve and lament, not over others (for this belongs to the perfect) but over themselves, because their Dibon too, that is, their composed discourse, which flowed like a torrent, is to perish: in which they had, as it were, the altar of their consecration, and all worldly riches. Hence it is said in the psalm too: If riches abound, do not set your heart upon them. And the beginning of salvation is to understand and weep over one's own sins.

15:3ff.

Over Nebo and over Medeba Moab will howl: on all its heads baldness, every beard will be shaved. In its crossroads they are girded with sackcloth: and upon its roofs and in its streets everyone howls: he will go down in weeping. And Heshbon and Elealeh will cry out: their voice has been heard as far as Jahaz: for this the armed men of Moab will howl, his soul will howl to itself. My heart will cry out to Moab: its bars as far as Zoar, a heifer of three years: for by the ascent of Luhith he will go up weeping, and on the way of Horonaim they will raise a cry of crushing: for the waters of Nimrim will be desolate: because the grass has withered, the shoot has failed, all greenness has perished. According to the greatness of the work is also their visitation: they will lead them to the brook of the willows: for the cry has gone round the border of Moab: its howling as far as Eglaim, and its cry as far as the well of Elim: because the waters of Dimon are filled with blood. For I will set upon Dimon additions, for those who have fled from Moab, a lion, and for the remnant of the land. Since the whole of this prophecy has almost a single sense, lest I tear it apart by setting it forth piecemeal, I have set it all down together, and I shall run through in brief discourse what seems to me, according to the anagogy, to be meant in each part. Nebo means sitting or prophecy; Medeba, from the forest; Heshbon, thoughts; Elealeh, ascent; Jahaz, deed or command; Zoar, small; Luhith, cheeks; Horonaim, hole of grief; Nimrim, leopards or transgressors; Eglaim, calves or mounds of sand; Elim, rams or strong ones; Dimon, sufficient grief. Since, then, every doctrine contrary to the truth, which is born without the inspiration of God from human sense in the darkness of error, has been laid waste by night, and its arguments, which are understood as walls, have been destroyed by the Church's preaching, so that they have fallen silent in eternal silence, insomuch that their whole faction has been turned to penance and tears, over Nebo, that is, the prophecy and the sitting, that is, their teachers, and over Medeba, where there are no fruitful trees but a barren forest in which wild beasts dwell, of which it is written in the twenty-eighth psalm: And he will uncover the thickets of the forest: there will be howling and lamentation, and all the ornaments of eloquence will be taken from their heads, so that they remain naked and unsightly. And if they seemed to have anything of manliness in the beard, shaved by the churchman, it is shown to be effeminate and weak. In their crossroads too, that is, in the byways of errors, while each one according to his own will fashions what he wishes, he is girded with the sackcloth of penance; and upon the roofs and housetops, on which at first they believed themselves to be lofty, and in the streets (because they do not enter by the narrow way that leads to life, but by the broad way that leads to death), there will be howling. And they will by no means go up into pride, but will go down into weeping. Then they will understand all their thoughts to be vain, which is the meaning of Heshbon, and the ascent of pride to be empty, which is what Elealeh sounds, so that their voice is heard as far as the evil works which they have done, and the command which they thought was God's, condemning themselves by their own confession. Therefore the bars, that is, those who have been firm in Moab and have understood their error, will howl, and will begin to have hope of progress, when their soul has howled to itself. Hence the Prophet, with the feeling of one who suffers with them, speaks to those whose soul was howling to itself, and says: My heart will cry out to Moab, that I may call them to penance. And their bars and all the supports which they seemed to have in their heresies will come as far as Zoar, that is, as far as the little one: and they will be shown to be not strong but fragile. And this Zoar, that is, small penance, if it perseveres, will lead them to perfect salvation: which is what the heifer of three years signifies, according to what we read in Genesis, where Abraham is commanded to offer a heifer, a ram and a goat of three years, namely a perfect sacrifice, so that he might deserve to be the heir of the Lord (Gen 15). And when they have done penance, they will climb to higher things by Luhith, that is, by the tears of the cheeks. And by this, as it were, hole and entrance of grief, they will raise the cry of contrition to the Lord, so that they can say: A sacrifice to God is a troubled spirit: a contrite and humbled heart God will not despise (Ps 50 [51]:19). And this will come about because the waters of Nimrim, that is, the doctrine of the heretics, which is compared to leopards and transgressors, will be desolate and will be brought to nothing. They are leopards whose varieties and spots, in Jeremiah, are not changed (Jer 13), and apostates, of whom we read in the Psalms: I have counted all the sinners of the earth transgressors (Ps 118 [119]:119). Every grass too, and shoot, and whatever seemed green in their discourse, has withered. And they have been visited by God according to the greatness of their sins, so that him whom they had not perceived through benefits they might come to know through scourges. Accordingly they will be led to the valley or brook of the willows, so that no fruit may remain in them. For they say this is the nature of the seed of these trees: that whoever drinks it in a cup is without children. Hence the saints too, who because of their sins have come to be in the confusion of this world, hang their instruments on the willows of the rivers of the Babylonians (Ps 136 [137]). A cry goes round all the borders of the Moabites, either of those who call them to repentance, or of those who lament for their error: so that through their howling they may be able to offer the calves of the lips, and come as far as the fountain of the Lord's rams, or of the strong: because Elim signifies both. And the waters of Dimon, which means sufficient sorrow, or grief, which had polluted many by their sprinkling, will be shown to have been to the deceived peoples not for salvation but for blood. Hence the prophetic word promises that upon the flowing tears, which is the meaning of Dibon, they will redouble not one grief but many additions of grief: so that, after they have done full penance and have fled from Moab, they may have as their prince the lion, God, whom the Seventy called ariel, which means lion of God: whose edition I have forborne to discuss in this place, because it disagrees in very many points with the Hebrew truth, and from what we have translated its sense too can be understood.

16:1

Send forth the lamb, the ruler of the earth, from the rock of the desert, to the mountain of the daughter of Zion. And as a bird fleeing, and as young ones flying from the nest, so will the daughters of Moab be at the crossing of the Arnon. Enter into counsel, call a council: make your shadow like night at midday: hide those who flee, and do not betray the wanderers. My fugitives will dwell with you; Moab, be their hiding place from the face of the destroyer. For the dust is at an end, the wretch is consumed; he has failed who trampled the earth. And a throne will be prepared in mercy, and one will sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David, judging and seeking judgment, and swiftly rendering what is just. What we have translated from the Hebrew, send forth the lamb, the ruler of the earth, can be read thus: send forth the lamb to the ruler of the earth, in the sense, namely, that the lamb itself is not the ruler of the earth, as we interpreted according to the history, but that the lamb is to be sacrificed to the ruler of the earth. This lamb, then, which either is itself the ruler of the earth or is sacrificed to the ruler of the earth, is of the nation of the Moabites, and of those who have fled from Moab and have deserved to have the lion as their prince. And it signifies Ruth, from whom Christ was begotten (Matt 1:5), whom he calls the rock of the desert, because according to the precept of God the Moabites and Ammonites do not enter the Church of God even to the tenth generation and forever (Deut 23). But he who has fled from the desert of Moab (to return from the prophecy to the anagogy), and, despising falsehood, has stood on the mountain of truth, will be like a bird fleeing; and like young ones flying from the nest, lest they be devoured by the Moabite serpents. Thus, he says, will all the daughters, that is, the Moabite souls, be at the crossing of the Arnon, which means their illumination: when, having abandoned their errors, they have crossed over to the knowledge of the truth. It is said therefore to Moab himself, or to him who has escaped from Moab: Do nothing without counsel (Prov 13): and do not be carried about by every wind of doctrine, but follow him who is the Angel of great counsel (Eph 4): and call a council, so that out of the wandering and straying you may make a Church of God. And your shade and tabernacle, in which you formerly thought you were resting, which belonged to night and darkness, set it at midday, that is, in the brightest light, in which you ought to hide those fleeing from error, and no longer betray those who were formerly wanderers.
