Of these women, long before they were born, the prophetic discourse foretells, and calls them from the spectacle of the Lord's Passion and Resurrection, so that they may preach the Gospel, and, according to the Hebrew, teach Jerusalem, or the land of Israel, that this is the Lord and God. For since the people of Israel did not have wisdom at that time, when the Lord suffered, and the prophetic oracle was fulfilled, Save me, O Lord, for the holy one has failed (Ps 11 [12]:1), and, All have turned aside, together they have become unprofitable: there is none who does good, there is not even one (Ps 13 [14]:4), the women are called from the spectacle, so that they may announce to the Apostles what they themselves have seen. But Israel, of which it was said (above, Isa 1:3), Israel has not known me, and my people has not understood, provoked its most clement Creator and maker to bitterness, so that he by no means has mercy on it. These things are indeed said piously; but how they agree with the rest, and are fitted to the times of the consummation of the world, is a difficult interpretation.

27:12

And it will be in that day: the Lord will strike from the channel of the river to the torrent of Egypt. LXX: And it will be in that day: the Lord will shut in from the trench of the river to Rhinocorura. Had he not added, in that day, by which we are taught that what he is about to say is to be coupled with what precedes, we could have expounded a sense proper to this passage; but now everything is to be referred to what precedes. Since the fortified city will be desolate, and the once beautiful one will be left as a desert, and there the calf will lie down and consume the shoots of the vineyard, and all things will be dried up, since it is not a people having understanding, and because of its folly it has obtained no mercy from its Creator: therefore the Lord will strike, or shut in, from the channel or stream of the river to the torrent of Egypt, so that in all Judea, which was once the land of promise, no word of teaching may be found, nothing of the knowledge of the Scriptures; of whom the Apostle too speaks: That we may not give heed to Jewish fables and commandments of men who turn away from the truth (Titus 1:14); and again: For there are many both insubordinate and vain talkers and deceivers, whom one must refute, especially of the circumcision (ibid., 10). And the channel, or stream, of the river, according to the history, we can call the Euphrates, as it is written also in the seventy-first psalm: He will have dominion from sea to sea, and from the river to the end of the world (Ps 71 [72]:8). Others think it is the Jordan. And this must be noted, that in the borders of Judea it is called river, in the territories of Egypt torrent, which has turbid waters and not perpetual ones. For the torrent of Egypt, the Seventy translated Rhinocorura, which is a town on the border of Egypt and Palestine, expressing not so much the words of the Scriptures as the sense of the words. And what we have said, will strike, for which the Seventy translated συμφράξει, that is, will shut in, Aquila and Theodotion translated ῥαβδήσει, which can be understood either as will strike with a rod or will count under the rod the number of his flock, so that it may be taken not in a bad but in a good sense.

And you will be gathered one by one, O children of Israel. LXX: But you, gather one by one the children of Israel. O children of Israel, for which Symmachus translated house of Israel: when your adversaries have been struck from the stream of the river to the torrent of Egypt, that is, from the Euphrates to the Nile, you yourselves will be gathered to the faith of the Lord one by one, because the throng of the Jews did not believe; by which he signifies that few of the Jews will believe in the Lord Savior. Or certainly, O Apostles and apostolic men, since the multitude of the Jews does not believe, bring back from the whole world as many as you can, like sick sheep, to the folds of the Lord, and gather them with the people of the nations, so that that may be fulfilled which the Apostle Paul and Barnabas say to the Jews: It was necessary that the word of God should be announced first to you; but since you have judged yourselves unworthy of salvation, behold, we turn to the Gentiles (Acts 13:46).

27:13

And it will be in that day: a blast will be sounded on a great trumpet; and those who had been lost from the land of the Assyrians, and those who had been cast out into the land of Egypt, will come, and they will worship the Lord on the holy mountain in Jerusalem. LXX: And it will be in that day: they will sound with a great trumpet; and those who had perished in the region of the Assyrians, and those who had perished in Egypt, will come, and they will worship the Lord upon the holy mountain in Jerusalem. In this place the Jews promise themselves empty hopes: that at the consummation of the world, when the Antichrist, their ἠλειμμένος, as it is said, has come, the dispersed people will be gathered from the Assyrians and from the land of Egypt, and will come to Jerusalem, and, the temple having been built, will worship the Lord their God. This cannot stand at all according to the letter. For not from the Assyrians and from Egypt only, but from the whole world, those who are to believe in Christ will be called. This, therefore, is what it signifies: that at the last trumpet, according to the Apostle Paul (1 Cor 15), all who had perished among the Assyrians and in Egypt come to the Lord. Nor did he say all the children of Israel, but all who had perished, by which he signifies the multitude of the nations: that those bound to idolatry and to the magic arts and to philosophy come to the faith of Christ and worship him in the Church. And the great trumpet can be understood as the word of the Gospel, of which we read also in this same Prophet: Go up upon a high mountain, you who bring good tidings to Zion: lift up your voice, you who bring good tidings to Jerusalem (below, Isa 40:9). The holy mountain, then, and Jerusalem is that of which we have often spoken: You have come to Mount Zion and the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and many thousands of angels, and the Church of the firstborn, who are enrolled in the heavens (Heb 12:22). Thus far it has been spoken of the consummation of the world, from the place at which we began to expound, Behold, the Lord will scatter the earth and will lay it bare (above, Isa 24:1), which is contained in the present volume. Now, with Christ helping, nay rather inspiring us, let us pass on to the ninth, which will hold the beginning of another prophecy.

Book Nine

Beset by various troubles, we dictate our explanations of the prophet Isaiah at intervals. So, the eighth volume completed, we now pass, after some space of time, to the ninth: not without the biting and the detraction of the envious, who, not knowing what they hear or what they say, dare to pass judgment on what they do not understand, and despise before they test, and reckon themselves learned and eloquent if they disparage all writers. Despising their spite and their chattering mutter, let us ask God's help, and say with the Psalmist's imprecation: Scatter the nations that desire wars (Ps 67 [68]:31). For the place of the Lord is in peace, which surpasses all understanding. This the prophet too desires when he cries out: O Lord our God, give us peace: for you have rendered all things to us (Isa 26:12). But now let us set out the chapter of Isaiah, and with Moses let us enter into the cloud and the thick darkness, so that our face may be made bright, and, according to the Hebrew, be horned; and let the thunders and lightnings be heard and flash, which the baser common people could not look upon (Exod 19).

28:1

Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim, and to the falling flower of the glory of its exultation, who were on the summit of the most fertile valley, going astray from wine. Behold, the strong and mighty one of the Lord, like the onrush of hail, a whirlwind that shatters; like the onrush of many waters overflowing and sent forth upon a spacious land. With feet shall the crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim be trodden down. And the falling flower of the glory of its exultation, which is upon the summit of the valley of the fat, shall be like an early fruit before the ripeness of autumn, which, when the beholder has looked upon it, as soon as he has taken it in his hand, he will devour it. LXX: Woe to the crown of insolence, the hirelings of Ephraim: a flower falling from glory upon the summit of the fat mountain, you who are drunk without wine. Behold, the wrath of the Lord is strong and harsh, like hail that is borne headlong, having no shelter, which falls violently like a multitude of waters dragging the soil along and making room for itself: with hands and feet shall the crown of insolence, the hirelings of Ephraim, be trodden down. And the flower that falls from the hope of glory on the top of the lofty mountain shall be like an early fig, which whoever sees it will long to devour before he takes it in his hand. Let us speak first according to the history, then according to tropology, and lastly according to the prophetic prediction. The divine word speaks against the ten tribes who reigned in Samaria and who, on account of Jeroboam, who was of the tribe of Ephraim, were called Ephraim. And it calls them a crown of pride, because, compared with the two tribes that were called Judah, they were loftier both in number and in strength. And it calls them the drunkards of Ephraim, since they did not understand their Creator, but in place of the Lord worshiped the golden calves in Dan and Bethel. These were once in the flower of the Lord, and in glory, when they were ruled by David and Solomon and, among the twelve tribes, worshiped God in the temple of Jerusalem; they were on the summit of the most fertile valley, which in Hebrew is called GE SEMANIM (גיא שמנים). This signifies the place where the Lord was betrayed; above the summit of this valley the temple of the Lord is situated. These men were made drunk with the wine of error and madness, which Jeroboam mixed for them. Therefore the Lord threatens them with punishment: that, as a whirlwind of hail shatters all things, and the onrush of overflowing waters sweeps away whatever it finds in its path, so they would be destroyed by the army of the Assyrians, and whatever remained would be carried off to the mountains or cities of Media. He compares the glory of the ten tribes to a crown of varied flowers, which had such beauty that, just as someone who, before summer and autumn come, sees a πρόδρομον fig on the tree, devours it as soon as he has taken it in his hand, so too the Assyrian, when he saw the ten tribes, would lay them waste and devour them, and leave nothing at all of the former people in Samaria. Let this have been said briefly according to the history. Let us pass to allegory. According to our exposition of the prophet Hosea, in which we referred Ephraim and Joseph and Samaria and the ten tribes, which were cut off from the body of the twelve tribes and abandoned the temple of the Lord, to the heretics, these are truly, according to the Septuagint edition, a crown of insolence: they blaspheme the Lord, and do everything for the sake of payment, and have fallen from the glory of the Lord; nor do they follow the slenderness of the manna and the humility of the Church, but they dwell on the most fertile mountain, drunk without wine. Therefore the strong and harsh wrath of the Lord, which is going to punish them, is compared to headlong hail, which falls not on roofs but on the heads of mortals, and to the floods of many waters, which drag along whatever they find in their way. This crown of insolence, the hirelings, are called Ephraim, who, according to the Apostle, for the sake of base gain have fallen from the flower and the hope and the glory of their former faith, and dwell in pride, and are the sweetest food of the devil, who devours them daily (1 Pet 5). According to the prophecy we can say this: that he calls the scribes and Pharisees, who blasphemed the Lord, a crown of insolence. And they were called the hirelings of Ephraim on account of Judas, who, of the tribe of Ephraim and of Iscarioth, a village of that same tribe, sold the Lord for a price; he truly, the flower of apostolic glory, fell upon the most fertile mountain, of which we think it was said: Jacob ate and drank and was filled, and grew fat, and the beloved kicked (Deut 32:15). Or, according to the Hebrew: upon the valley of the fat, that is, Gessemanim: in which the name of the place is also signified in which Judas betrayed the Lord. And it is called the fat valley, or the valley of the fat, on account of its fertility, and on account of the scribes and Pharisees who seized the Lord there: of whom it is written in the psalm: Fat bulls have besieged me (Ps 21 [22]:13). This valley of the fat, that is, Gessemanim, is named a second time in this chapter; and I wonder how the Seventy first called it a fat mountain and afterward a lofty mountain. The betrayer was drunk not with wine but with avarice and the incurable fury of asps, and with the food of the devil, who entered into him after the morsel (John 13), and he was utterly devoured, because his prayer was turned into sin, and not even his repentance had the fruit of salvation. The Hebrew word SACCHORE (שכורי) is ambiguous, and means either drunkards or hirelings. Hence Issachar too means there is a reward; and SACHAR (שכר) is μέθυσμα, that is, drunkenness. And the rest translated drunkards: the Seventy alone translated hirelings.

28:5ff.

In that day the Lord of hosts shall be a crown of glory and a garland of exultation to the remnant of his people, and a spirit of judgment to him who sits upon judgment, and strength to those returning from war to the gate. But these also have not known because of wine, and have gone astray because of drunkenness; the priest and the prophet have not known: they are swallowed up by wine because of drunkenness, they have gone astray in drunkenness: they have not known the seer, they have been ignorant of judgment, or wonderfully. For all the tables are filled with vomit and filth, so that there was no more room. LXX: In that day the Lord Sabaoth shall be a crown of hope, which is woven of glory, for the remnant of the people. They shall be left in a spirit of judgment upon judgment, and strength forbidding to kill. For these have been deceived by wine: they go astray because of strong drink; the priest and the prophet have lost their minds because of strong drink; they are swallowed up because of wine, they have staggered, that is, φάσμα; a curse shall eat this counsel: for this counsel is for the sake of avarice. After the whole land of Samaria, that is, of the ten tribes, has been destroyed by the Assyrian's flood, and the crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim has been trodden underfoot and devoured like an early fig, then the Lord himself shall be a crown of victory to the remnant of the people of Israel, that is, of the two tribes, Judah and Benjamin; and a spirit of judgment to him who sits upon judgment, doubtless to Hezekiah king of Judah; and the strength of those who, when the whole region had been ravaged, returning from battle, shut themselves up in the city. This we shall read in this same prophet (below, Isa 37), when one hundred and eighty-five thousand armed men of the army of the Assyrians were destroyed by the stroke of an angel. But these also, that is, Judah and Benjamin, were made drunk with the wine of idolatry, and, despising the worship of the temple, venerated the images of demons, and did not know the Lord, the seer, who beholds all things. For all their tables, and their whole worship, were filled with vomit and filth, so that not only in the temple but on the tops of the mountains and in wooded places they filled everything with the filth of idolatry, and the Lord had no place of habitation among them. Let this have been said according to the letter. Further, according to tropology, let us follow the former understanding, and not leave the Seventy translators untouched. For when the heretics, who have climbed the most fertile mountain of pride, have been devoured by the mouth of the devil, the Lord shall be a crown of glory to those who dwell in the Church and who, compared with the multitude of the many who go astray, are few in number. And he shall be in a spirit of judgment upon judgment, because the Lord will wash away the filth of the sons and daughters of Zion by the spirit of judgment. But if anyone has blood, he will be purged not by the spirit of judgment but by the fire of burning; and he shall be strength to the people, and shall forbid it to be killed by those who are drunk with the wine of dragons and have gone astray because of strong drink. We have often said that wine is what is made from vines; but strong drink is every drink that can intoxicate and overturn the state of the mind, which Aquila properly translated drunkenness, whether it is made from wheat or barley or millet, or from the juice of fruits, or from the fruit of palms, or from any other kind. Therefore the priests and prophets of the heretics have lost their minds because of strong drink, and are swallowed up because of wine, such as were Prisca and Maximilla and their chief Montanus: and they did not know what they were saying. They are made drunk with wine when they misunderstand and pervert the holy Scriptures; with strong drink, when they misuse worldly wisdom and the snares of the dialecticians, which are to be called not so much bonds as phantasms, that is, certain shadows and images that quickly perish and dissolve. A curse shall possess the counsel of such men, who suppose that godliness is gain, and do everything for the sake of avarice. Of this phantasm the Apostle too spoke: Giving heed to spirits of error and doctrines of demons, speaking lies in hypocrisy (1 Tim 4:1-2). The third explanation is that, after the Lord has overthrown the scribes and Pharisees, and their associate Judas the betrayer, who had been a thief from the beginning, for he himself carried the purse of the money for the poor (John 12 and 13), he then becomes a hope and a crown of glory to those of the Jews who believed in the Lord; doubtless he means the apostles, whom he reserved for the preaching of the Gospel and did not allow at once to shed their blood for Christ. For all the scribes and Pharisees were made drunk with the wine and strong drink of which we spoke above, the priests as well as the false prophets. But their snares and plots came to nothing, since both Judas himself, who betrayed him, did it for money, and the priests, who corrupted the betrayer with money, did it out of fear of their own rejection. For he himself, making a scourge of cords, cast out of the temple those who sold oxen and sheep, and by his own authority overturned the seats of those who sold doves and the tables of the money-changers, saying to them: It is written: My Father's house shall be called a house of prayer, but you have made it a house of trade, or a den of robbers (Matt 21:13). According to the anagogy, that Hebrew text in which we said: For all their tables are filled with vomit and filth, so that there is no more room, can be referred to the heretics, and to the scribes and Pharisees, in this way: that we say all their teaching and all their mysteries are full of vomit and filth, since they do not digest the food of the holy Scriptures nor make it life-giving to the whole body, but void it unripe and stinking, so that God finds no place in them. But I wonder what Theodotion meant, that for the Hebrew word called CISOA (קיאצאה), for which Aquila translated vomit of filth and Symmachus simply vomit, he should say ἐμετὸν δυσαλίας, that is, vomit of dysalia, a word I have not been able to find read anywhere among the Greeks, unless perhaps he coined a new name for a new thing. Indeed among the Hebrews too it is a compound, since vomit is called CI, and SOA filthy. Whatever, then, causes nausea and vomiting can be called δυσαλία.

28:10ff.

Whom shall he teach knowledge, and whom shall he make to understand what is heard? Those weaned from the milk, those drawn from the breasts: for command, command again; command, command again; wait, wait again; wait, wait again; a little there, a little there. For with speech of lip and with another tongue he will speak to this people, to whom he said: This is my rest; refresh the weary, and this is my refreshment, and they would not hear. And the word of the Lord shall be to them: command, command again; command, command again; wait, wait again; wait, wait again; a little there, a little there; that they may go and fall backward, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken. LXX: To whom shall we announce evils, and to whom shall we announce tidings? those who are weaned from the milk, who are drawn from the breast. Expect tribulation upon tribulation; wait for hope upon hope; yet a little, yet a little: because of the mockery of the lips, because of another tongue with which they will speak to this people, saying to them: This is the rest for the hungry, and this the crushing, and they would not hear. And the word of the Lord shall be to them: Tribulation upon tribulation: expect, expect; hope upon hope: yet a little, yet a little; that they may go and fall backward, and be broken, and be endangered, and be taken. Who, he says, is worthy of the teaching of the Lord, who, by the words of the Savior, who says: He who has ears to hear, let him hear (Matt 11:15), understands with the heart what he has taken in with the ears? Who these are the following verse shows: Weaned from the milk, drawn from the breast: those who are no longer fed with the milk of infancy but eat solid food; who are drawn from the breast with Isaac, for which joy Abraham made a great feast (Gen 21); these deserve to hear the mysteries of the Lord and to understand what the priest and the prophet do not know, drunk and swallowed up by wine, who went astray and did not know the seer, because all their tables were filled with vomit and filth. These, when the prophets announced what was to come and threatened torments unless they did what had been commanded, used to say in mockery: Command, command again; command, command again, that is, give orders, give orders, command what we ought to do. And since they abused the patience of God, who defers his wrath in order to show mercy, they used also to say this, jesting, in the person of the prophets: Wait a little while, wait a little, the things we have foretold will come. All this they said among the people, because they did not believe the words of God; and at once the prophet adds: God will no longer speak to you in these words, to command what you ought to do and that you should wait for what is to come, but he will speak to you in present fury, he who had earlier said to the people: This is my rest, refresh the weary: I have labored a long time, in nothing have I found rest. The foxes have holes, and the birds of the sky nests; but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head (Matt 8; Luke 9). And this is my refreshment, that I may at some time rest in you. They would not hear, and despised my warnings; wherefore what they used to say to the prophets in jest: Command, command again; command, command again: wait, wait again; wait, wait again: a little there, a little there, mocking my patience, since they thought I was threatening things I would never do: let them feel it fulfilled in fact, so that they go to destruction and fall backward with an incurable ὀπισθοτόνῳ; and may never advance to the things before, nor be able to say with the Apostle: Forgetting the things that are behind, we stretch forward to those that are before (Phil 3:13); but may they be broken and snared, and be taken either by the Babylonian or by the Roman army. Where we have said: Command, command again; command, command again: wait, wait again; wait, wait again; a little there, a little there, in the Hebrew it is written thus: SAU LASAU, SAU LASAU; CAU LACAU, CAU LACAU: ZER SAM, ZER SAM; and a most unclean heresy is accustomed to misuse these words among simple and deceived people, to cause terror by the novelty of the expressions: namely, that whoever has learned these words and remembers them in their intercourse will pass without any doubt into the kingdom of heaven. We read in the Apostle: In other tongues and with other lips I will speak to this people, and not even so will they hear me, says the Lord (1 Cor 14:21). This seems to me taken from the present chapter according to the Hebrew; and we have observed this in the Old Testament (apart from a few testimonies which Luke alone uses, who had a greater knowledge of the Greek language): wherever anything is cited from the old instrument, they set it down not according to the Septuagint but according to the Hebrew, following no one's translation, but rendering the Hebrew sense in their own language. Symmachus, Theodotion and the Seventy understood this place differently, and because it is long to speak of them all, let us run briefly through the Seventy translators, who are read in the churches. The people of the Jews having been rejected, the priests and prophets who were drunk with strong drink and went astray, and the curse having eaten up the counsel they formed for the sake of avarice, to whom shall we announce the tribulations to come for Christ's sake? to whom the evils in return for which the crown of virtues is prepared? Surely to those who are weaned from the milk, who are drawn from the breast: doubtless he means the apostles: Expect tribulation upon tribulation. He is speaking to the company of the apostles and of all believers, that each should prepare himself not for one tribulation but for many, so that when he has been afflicted and pressed down he may hope again, and have hope upon hope. And if what has been promised delays a little, let him not be unbelieving: for a little, a very little, and what has been promised will come. For tribulation works patience; patience, proof; proof, hope; and hope does not confound (Rom 5:3-5). And this very tribulation will be doubled by the detraction of lips, and by the blasphemies of the persecutors, with which they rage with rabid mouth against the people of God. Further, the apostles and apostolic men will speak to the people of the Jews, saying: This is the rest for the hungry for righteousness, and this the crushing and the narrowness that leads to life. When they preached this, the ungodly would not hear. Hence what was said to the people of God: Endure tribulation, endure tribulation; expect hope, expect hope: yet a little, yet a little, will be turned into punishment for those who would not hear the word of the Lord, so that they fall and go backward, and run into the peril of siege and death, and are taken with no end of miseries. That the Seventy alone translated the Hebrew word DEA, which all rendered knowledge, as evils is an evident error. For the first letter, DALETH or RES, are distinguished by a small stroke. If, then, it is read DEA (דעה), it means knowledge; if REA (רעה), malice: not from the evil that is the contrary of good, but from distress.

28:14-15

Therefore hear the word of the Lord, you scornful men, who rule over my people that is in Jerusalem. For you have said: We have struck a covenant with death, and with hell we have made a pact: when the overflowing scourge passes through, it shall not come upon us, because we have made a lie our hope, and by a lie we are protected. LXX: Therefore hear the word of the Lord, you afflicted men and princes of this people that is in Jerusalem: Because you have said: We have made a testament with hell, and a pact with death: if the passing tempest rushes on, it shall not come upon us, since we have made a lie our hope, and by a lie we shall be protected. What we said above, that the princes of the Jews used to say to the prophets with mockery: Command, command again; wait, wait again, and other things like these, by which it is shown that they in no way believed the words of the prophets but held their prophecy in contempt, the present chapter shows, in which they are called scornful men. These are the scribes and Pharisees, who rule over the people of God in Jerusalem, whom the Seventy call afflicted men and princes of the people of Jerusalem. For they said, not in word but in deed: We are like the other nations too: we have a pact and a covenant with hell and with death: we have despaired of salvation once for all. Surely the captivity will come a long time hence, since you say: Yet a little, yet a little: wait, wait again. So when we are dead we shall not feel this scourge of captivity and this tempest. For once for all we have believed a lie, that is, we have had hope in God and in his Law in vain. And therefore we are protected by a lie, because, being dead, we have escaped the threatening captivity. The Hebrew word SOT (שוט) Aquila and Symmachus translated scourge, the Seventy tempest; CHASAB (כזב) too all translated lie, in which the Jews hoped, whose father, according to the Evangelist John, is the devil.

28:16ff.

Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will lay in the foundations of Zion a tried stone, a corner stone, precious, founded with a foundation: he who believes, let him not hasten. And I will set judgment in the weight, and righteousness in the measure: and hail shall overthrow the hope of falsehood, and waters shall overflow the protection. And your covenant with death shall be blotted out, and your pact with hell shall not stand; when the overflowing scourge passes through, you shall be trodden down by it. When it passes through, it shall take you away: for in the morning, at daybreak, it shall pass through, in the day and in the night, and vexation alone shall give understanding to the hearing: For the bed is straitened, so that one must fall out, and a short cloak cannot cover both. LXX: Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will put into the foundations of Zion a precious stone, chosen, a corner stone, honorable, in its foundations; and he who believes shall not be confounded. And I will set judgment in hope, and my mercy in the weight; and those who trust vainly in a lie, since the tempest shall not pass through us, and shall not take from us the testament of death, also your hope in hell shall not remain. If the coming tempest passes through, you shall be trodden down by it: when it passes through, it shall take you in the morning, in the morning it shall pass through: by day and by night there shall be a most evil hope. Learn to hear, you who are in tribulation: We cannot fight, and we ourselves are too weak to be gathered together. I had said to you, he says: Hear the word of the Lord, you scornful men, or afflicted princes of my people, and do not have a covenant with death nor a pact with hell, you who, despising my precepts, have made a lie your hope, and, boasting, or rather despairing, say: by a lie we shall be protected. Therefore the Lord, who is merciful and compassionate, patient and abounding in mercy (Ps 144 [145]), says that, against your will, he will lay in the foundations of Zion a stone chosen and tried and precious and a corner stone. Of this the Apostle too speaks: As a wise architect I have laid the foundation (1 Cor 3:10); and again: For no one can lay another foundation than that which is laid, which is Christ Jesus (ibid., 11). This stone is truly, and a second time, called a stone, just as in Leviticus man, man is said twice; and a corner stone, because it joined together the peoples of the Circumcision and of the Gentiles, of which it is said in the psalm too: The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner (Ps 117 [118]:22). These are the builders and masons who are now called scornful men and princes of the people that is in Jerusalem. Of this stone we read in Daniel too, that it was cut from the mountain without hands and filled the whole world (Dan 2): because the dispensation of the divine offspring took a human body, and the fullness of the Godhead dwelt in it bodily. Upon this stone, which by another name is called the rock, Christ built the Church, and, according to the Hebrew, founded it with a firm foundation; in which whoever believes shall not be confounded, or, according to the Hebrew, let him not hasten: that is, lest the coming of Christ should seem slow to him. For if he delays, according to Habakkuk, let no one despair: because he will surely come, and will fulfill his promises (Hab 2). God promises also to set in it the judgment of the weight: For the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son (John 5:22). And righteousness, or mercy, in the measure, so that he may render to each according to his works, and temper righteousness and mercy each by the other, according to what we read in the psalms too: Mercy and truth have met each other: righteousness and peace have kissed (Ps 84 [85]:11). Your hope also, he says, and your lie, that is, the devil, the father of every lie, the hail of my punishments shall overthrow. And the protection under which you thought you would be safe, a mighty tempest and a multitude of waters shall destroy, so that the friendship and covenant you had with death and with hell, that is, with the devil, shall perish forever. And the scourge, or tempest, of which you had said: When the overflowing scourge passes through, it shall not come upon us, shall come, and you shall be trodden down by it, that is, you shall suffer all the torments which, in your despairing mind, you thought you would never suffer. For it will always rush upon you, and in prosperity as in adversity you will feel the wrath of the Lord, and cruel death will lay you waste. What shall I say of the punishments? The mere dread of punishments and the fear of torments will correct you unto salvation, and will make you understand your evils. And when you have been vexed, then you will know that my prophets spoke the truth. And what follows: For the bed is straitened, so that one must fall out, and a short cloak cannot cover both, has the sense we read in the Apostle: You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You cannot be partakers of the table of the Lord and of the table of idols (1 Cor 10:20-21); and elsewhere: What participation has righteousness with iniquity? What fellowship has light with darkness? What agreement has Christ with Belial? What part has the believer with the unbeliever? What consent has the temple of God with idols (2 Cor 6:14-15)? He speaks under the metaphor of a most chaste husband, who says to an adulterous wife: One little bed cannot hold me and the adulterer with you, and a short cloak cannot cover both the husband and the paramour. O Jerusalem, then, to whom he speaks in Ezekiel too under the person of a fornicating wife (Ezek 16:21), and whom at the beginning of Hosea he calls a harlot and an adulteress (Hos 3), if you wish to be joined in my embraces, cast away your idols: if you serve idols, you cannot have me. This according to the Hebrew. Further, as for what is read in the Seventy: Learn to hear, you who are afflicted: we cannot fight, and we ourselves are too weak to be gathered together, what sense it has, and how it is connected with what goes before, I am entirely ignorant. Unless perhaps the divine word is speaking to the princes of the people and exhorting them to have hope in God and not in death and hell, and to learn to hear the oracles of the prophets; and they answer that, for the weakness of their strength, they cannot fight against the opposing powers, nor be gathered together among the people of God.

28:21-22

For as on the mountain of divisions the Lord shall stand, as in the valley of Gibeon he shall be angry, that he may do his work, his strange work, that he may perform his work, his work is foreign to him. And now do not mock, lest perhaps your bonds be tightened. For I have heard from the Lord God of hosts a consummation and a cutting short upon the whole earth. LXX: As a mountain of the ungodly the Lord shall rise up, and he shall be in the valley of Gibeon; with fury he shall do his works, a work of bitterness, and his fury shall deal as with strangers: and his bitterness is strange. And do not you rejoice, lest your bonds be strengthened, since I have heard from the Lord God Sabaoth things completed and cut short, which he will do upon all the earth. The Lord promised that he would lay a precious stone in the foundations of Zion, so that hail might overthrow the lie and the hope of the ungodly, and a mighty tempest might blot out the covenant with death and the pact with hell. Since the scornful princes would not receive it, just as once, when David reigned, the Lord cut down his adversaries against the Philistines on the mountain of divisions, which in Hebrew was called PHARASIM (פרצים), from which the place also took its name; and as in the valley of Gibeon, under Joshua the leader, when, in the confidence of God dwelling in him, he said: Let the sun stand still at Gibeon, and the moon over against the valley of Aijalon (Josh 10:12), and the sun stood still for the space of one day, and many of the foreigners perished: so the Lord shall be angry against the ungodly and the scornful, that he may do his work. For it is not the Lord's work to destroy those whom he created, but to do a strange work, which pertains to cruelty rather than to mercy. And again he repeats the very same thing in other words: that he may perform his work. It is not his work to punish sinners, but foreign and strange to him that he who is the Savior should punish. Since, then, the Lord is going to rise up from his patience and will by no means spare, just as he did not spare on Mount Pharasim and in the valley of Gibeon, I warn you, O scornful men, by no means to laugh at my prophets, nor to think that what they announce will not come, lest, if you persist in mocking, the bonds of your sins be tightened (For each one is bound fast by the cords of his own sins (Prov 5:22), or the time of captivity come upon you. For what the Lord was postponing in time, the bonds, the captivity and the punishments, or the last day of judgment, he is now about to fulfill in fact, and to consummate and cut short. Therefore I, the prophet, announce to you the things I have learned from the Lord God almighty are to come upon the whole earth, so that you may forestall the impending wrath by repentance. According to the Seventy, the Lord himself is said to be about to rise like a mountain of the ungodly and to be in the valley of Gibeon, that he may do his works, which are all one work of bitterness: and this should by no means seem blasphemous. For it does not say that the Lord will be a mountain of the ungodly, but like a mountain, which seems most heavy to the ungodly and those who bear it. Just as a negligent son and a sick man may think a father and a physician cruel if they restore them to health with blows and with the cautery of discipline. For the Lord will rise up and will be in the valley of Gibeon on account of those who, though for their sins they stand in a low place, are lifted up into pride by the swelling of their mind. For Gibeon means hill: that he may do his works, which are works of bitterness, when he is compelled to change his clemency and, instead of sweet, becomes bitter. Therefore you who are one day to suffer these things, do not now rejoice with that joy with which the rich man too rejoiced, clothed in purple at his banquet and neglecting the poor man Lazarus (Luke 16), lest perhaps your bonds become stronger. For what the Lord is going to do, and to fulfill his sentence in fact, this I have both heard and announced to you in full. And as for what he added: Upon all the earth, according to the history understand the borders of Judea; according to the anagogy, of the whole world.

28:23ff.

Give ear and hear my voice: attend and hear my speech. Will the plowman plow all day that he may sow, will he break up and hoe his ground? When he has leveled its surface, will he not sow gith, and scatter cumin, and put wheat in rows, and barley, and millet, and vetch in their borders? And he will instruct him in judgment; his God will teach him. For gith shall not be threshed with saws, nor shall the wheel of the cart go round over the cumin; but gith shall be beaten out with a rod, and cumin with a staff: but bread shall be crushed. Yet the thresher shall not thresh it forever, nor shall the wheel of the cart vex it, nor shall he crush it with its hoofs. And this has gone forth from the God of hosts, that he might make his counsel wonderful and magnify righteousness. LXX: Give ear and hear my voice: attend and hear my words. Will he who plows plow all day, or will he prepare the seed before he prepares the ground? When he has leveled its surface, will he not then sow gith and cumin, and again sow wheat, and barley, and millet, and spelt in your borders, and you shall be instructed by the judgment of God, and shall rejoice? For gith is not cleaned with harshness, nor does the wheel of the cart go round over the cumin; but gith is beaten out with a rod, and cumin is eaten with bread. For I will not be angry with you forever, nor shall the voice of my bitterness trample you down; and these portents have gone forth from the Lord. Take counsel, exalt a vain consolation. He is now speaking also to the same men to whom he had said above: Hear the word of God, you scornful men, who rule over my people that is in Jerusalem; and he commands them to hear his voice and attend diligently to his speech. Will the farmer, he says, always plow so that he may cast the seed? Will he not first break up the ground and turn over the furrows with the plowshare, and break the lumps lying there with rake and hoe, so that when he has leveled the surface of the earth and first softened the hard fields, he may then scatter gith or cumin, and sow wheat, and barley, and millet, and spelt in their borders, according to the variety of the land and of the seasons: for all things are not sown at once. For spelt, which the Greeks call ζέαν, some understand vetch. And God by his judgment instructs the farmer himself, that is, the sower, by nature, and teaches him to know what cultivation to apply to which seed. Then, when the time of reaping has come, gith and cumin, which are the weaker seeds, are not ground by the wheels of the carts, which, made of iron like saws, are driven round and dragged over the reaped crops; but they are beaten out with a rod and a staff, which are commonly called flails. But bread, that is, the wheat from which bread is made, is ground by iron wheels, and all its stalk is crushed into chaff. Yet it is not always vexed and ground, nor at all times crushed by the hoofs of the wheels; for which in the Hebrew it says by their horses: so that, since he had spoken of the hoofs of the wheels, he might keep the metaphor in the rest. Some would have it that, because he named hoofs and horses, herds of mares are meant, which are usually let into the threshing floors to tread out the grain; but Scripture could not say what the province of Judea did not have. But this, that is, that gith and cumin are beaten out with a rod and a staff, while wheat and barley and spelt, and perhaps millet too, are ground by iron wheels, not forever, is the judgment of God, who in all things shows his wonderful counsel and displays the greatness of his righteousness in all. These things we have said παραφραστικῶς, so that we may more easily understand the sense for which they are said. God dispenses the human race in various ways: now he punishes, now he has mercy; now he rebukes, now he defends; that is, now he plows, now he sows, now he reaps the ripe fruits, and when they are reaped he threshes them on the floors, and governs his world as he will. Gith and cumin, that is, all the nations that did not receive the knowledge of him nor have the precepts of the Law, he corrects with a rod and a staff; but the wheat, that is, the people of the Jews, he will torment with great punishments. For to whom more is entrusted, from him more will be required. And the servant who knows the will of his lord and does not do it shall be beaten with many stripes (Luke 12:47); and in another place it is written: The mighty shall suffer torments mightily (Wis 6:7). Yet he will not torment them forever. For it is one thing to be ungodly, another to be a sinner. What we have interpreted of the nations and the Jews, others expound of the people and the priests: that the unlearned common people in the day of judgment will be chastised like gith and cumin with a rod and a staff, but the priests, who had the key of knowledge, will be tormented with great punishments; and that this happens by the judgment of the Lord, who shows in all things his wonderful counsel and the truth of his righteousness, so that from those who have received more, more is required. Where we have translated: gith shall be beaten out with a rod, and cumin with a staff, the Seventy, meaning I know not what, translated: but cumin is eaten with bread. Indeed the old Greek translators too, in rendering the Hebrew, were silent about this expression, perhaps because they had nothing to say. And that passage in which we, according to the Hebrew, have put: Yet the thresher shall not thresh it forever, nor shall the wheel of the cart vex it, nor shall he crush it with its hoofs, the Seventy translated not word for word but according to the sense: For I will not be angry with you forever, nor shall the voice of my bitterness trample you down: showing that refreshment is to come to sinners after torments, and that these things have gone forth from the Lord as portents and wonders. Hence sinners who are afterward to be punished are commanded to take counsel and exalt their consolation, by no means a vain one, as was added by the Seventy, but consolation absolutely. For God would never command them to exalt their vain consolation, which would be of no profit to them.

29:1ff.

Woe to Ariel, Ariel, the city which David besieged. Year has been added to year, the solemnities have rolled round. I will surround Ariel with a rampart, and it shall be sad and mourning; and it shall be to me like Ariel. And I will set as it were a ring round about you, and I will cast up a mound against you, and set up fortifications for your siege. You shall be brought low, you shall speak from the earth, and your speech shall be heard from the ground, and your voice shall be like that of a python from the earth, and from the ground your speech shall mutter. And the multitude of those who winnow you shall be like fine dust, and the multitude of those who have prevailed against you like passing ash. And it shall be suddenly, at once: it shall be visited by the Lord of hosts with thunder and the shaking of the earth, and with the great noise of whirlwind and tempest, and of the flame of devouring fire. And the multitude of all the nations that have fought against Ariel, and all who have made war and besieged and prevailed against it, shall be like the dream of a night vision. As the hungry man dreams and eats, but when he has awakened his soul is empty; and as the thirsty man dreams and drinks, but after he has awakened he is still faint and thirsty, and his soul is empty: so shall be the multitude of all the nations that have fought against Mount Zion. LXX: Woe to Ariel, Ariel, the city which David besieged. Gather the produce, eat year upon year, for you shall eat with Moab: for I will press Ariel hard, and its strength and its riches shall be mine, and I will encompass you like David: and I will throw up a rampart round about you, and set towers around you, and your words shall be brought low to the earth, and your speeches shall sink into the earth. And your voice shall be like that of those who speak from the earth, and down to the pavement your voice shall grow weak. And the riches of the ungodly shall be like dust from a wheel, and the multitude of those who have oppressed you like ash that is swept away; and it shall be in an instant, suddenly, from the Lord Sabaoth. For there shall be a visitation with thunder, and shaking, and a great noise, a mighty tempest, and a flame of devouring fire. And the riches of all the nations that have made war against Ariel, and all who have fought against Jerusalem, and all who have gathered against it and afflicted it, shall be like one who sees a dream by night. And they shall be like those who hunger in their sleep and eat, and when they rise their dream is vain; and like one who thirsts in a dream and drinks, and when he rises he will still thirst, and his soul has hoped in vain: so shall be the riches of all the nations that have made war against Mount Zion. Where we have translated Woe, in the Hebrew is written OI (הוי), which among them is sometimes used in the vocative case, so that it does not lament Ariel but calls it; although in the present place it is to be taken as a lament. Ariel too means lion of God; and for city, which Aquila translated πολίχνην, that is, little town or little village, they read in the Hebrew CARIATH (קרית), which properly signifies village, and in the Syriac language is called Cartha; whence the village of the woods too is called CARIATH JARIM (קרית יערים). Indeed above too (cf. Isa 1:21), where we read: How has the faithful city Zion become a harlot?, for city Cariath is written, that is, village: which, to express Aquila's translation word for word, we can call citylet. Therefore Ariel, that is, lion of God, is the name given to Jerusalem, once most strong; or, as others think, to the temple and altar of God that was in Jerusalem. And what follows: Which David besieged, for which Symmachus translated camp of David, and Theodotion circumvallation of David, in the Hebrew reads HANA (חנה), which the most learned of the Hebrews held to signify dwelling place. If, then, we read: which David besieged, let us refer it to that time when David took the citadel of Zion, while the blind and the lame resisted, and Joab first climbed the heights of the buildings (1 Chr 11). But if according to Symmachus and Theodotion, it is to be understood that David restored and fortified it; year has been added to year, or taken away, as Aquila translated; and the solemnities have rolled round. For when the temple was overthrown and the Jewish worship taken away, all their festivity perished. And the Lord says that he will surround Ariel with a rampart, with the Babylonian army, and that it will be sad and mourning when it has been destroyed by them. And again, under Jeshua son of Jozadak the high priest, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, and Ezra and Nehemiah, when Haggai and Zechariah prophesied, it will be like Ariel, in that it will have the likeness of the ancient temple, but not have its magnificence and adornment. A second time also the Lord threatens that he will surround Ariel with a ring, and cast up a mound against it, and set up fortifications for its siege, and that what he himself says, lamenting Jerusalem in the Gospel, will be fulfilled: If you knew the things that are for your peace, for days shall come upon you, and your enemies shall surround you with a rampart, and besiege you, and you shall be brought low to the ground (Luke 19:42ff.). And Jerusalem shall be trodden down by the nations until the time of the nations is consummated. For in other words the prophet now says the same thing: that, brought low, it speaks from the earth, and its speech is heard from the ground; and its voice is like that of a python from the earth, and from the ground it mutters like sparrows; so that by these words he signifies the νεκυομαντείαν of the magicians, by which they are said to call up souls and to hear the thin voices of shades, or rather of demons. Indeed for python Aquila translated magician, which in Hebrew is called CHEB (כאב), for which the Seventy translated those speaking from the earth. By these words it is indicated that the ruin of the temple will remain until the consummation of the world, so that, having collapsed into ashes, it will never be raised again. And so great an army of Roman power will encompass you, O Ariel, that it will be compared to countless dust, like ash flying through the air. Hence he compares to dust and ash not the weakness of those who made war against them, but their multitude, which is equal to the countless sands. And this will be suddenly, at once, so that in the midst of peace sudden wars arise under Nero, and the Lord of hosts visits Jerusalem with thunder, and with the shaking of the earth, and with the whirlwind of tempest, and with the flame of devouring fire, by which he signifies that the temple was to be burned. And the Romans, who, when the Jews had been overcome and Jerusalem overthrown under Titus and Vespasian, offered to the Capitol spoils from the vessels that once were God's, and thought that what they had done was the work of their own valor and of the power of their gods, not of the wrath of God, will possess all their riches as in a dream and in a vision of the night. And as one who is hungry thinks, while sleeping, that he is eating in his dreams, and one who is thirsty, his throat parched with thirst, drinks rivers, and when he has awakened his thirst becomes fiercer, having been mocked by an empty drink: so the multitude of all the nations which, subject to Roman power, fought against Mount Zion, will have their riches as in a shadow and a cloud and a dream of the night, riches which they will leave behind by an early death. In the place where we have put: all who have made war and besieged and prevailed against it, the Seventy translated: and all who have fought against Jerusalem, which is not in the Hebrew. At the beginning of this chapter too, where we have said: Year has been added to year, or taken away, they translated: gather the fruits, or produce, year upon year: eat, for you shall eat with Moab. And the sense is: before the acceptable year of the Lord, of his preaching, comes, or rather the two years, of which we read in the Canticle of Habakkuk according to the Hebrew: In the midst of two times you shall be known (Hab 3), sow for yourselves in tears, that you may reap in joy (Ps 125 [126]). It is written in the Gospel according to John that the Lord came to Jerusalem at three Passovers, which make two years (John 2:13). And what follows: For you shall eat with Moab, is not in the Hebrew. Of this we can say that, unless they gather for themselves the fruits of repentance, they will begin to eat with those who do not enter the Church of the Lord forever. The other points in which they seem to differ are plain, and from what we have expounded their interpretation is easy. I know that I have read that Ariel means my light of God, which is far otherwise. For here the first syllable is written with ALEPH and RES (אר): but light, which in Hebrew is called OR, has between ALEPH and RES the middle letter VAU, which is not found in the present name. And they refer all that is now said against Ariel to the heretics, who reckon their own doctrine to be the light of God, and who are to be overcome by the true David: and all their solemnities are to be taken away, and their present joy changed into future sorrow; and God commands them to do penance, lest they begin to eat with the Moabites and be like the Gentiles. For he himself will overcome Ariel, and will encompass all their strength and riches with his army. And with towers, that is, with the teachers of the Church, he will bring their words low to the earth, so that they will by no means set their mouth against heaven, but will be written in the earth and speak from the earth, and become like dust shaken off by a wheel; and all the riches of the ungodly will be compared to a point and a moment of time, when he visits them in his majesty, descending in whirlwind and tempest and the fire of punishment; and they will understand that all their riches, and the pomp of their words, and the twists of their arguments, are like the dream of one who eats and drinks in vain: they who have made war against Jerusalem, the vision of peace, or against Ariel, the mightiest lion, and lastly against Mount Zion, upon which the city of the Church is set and cannot be hidden.

29:9ff.

Be stupefied and wonder: waver and stagger, be drunk, and not with wine; reel, and not with drunkenness. For the Lord has mingled for you a spirit of deep sleep: he will close your eyes; your prophets and your princes, who see visions, he will cover. And the vision of all shall be to you like the words of a sealed book, which, when they give it to one who knows letters, they will say: Read this, and he will answer: I cannot, for it is sealed. And the book shall be given to one who does not know letters, and it shall be said to him: Read; and he will answer: I do not know letters. For spirit of deep sleep the Seventy translated compunction; Theodotion ecstasy of mind; Aquila καταφορὰν, that is, heavy sleep; which in Hebrew is called THARDEMA (תרדמה), and which Scripture records was sent by God upon Adam (Gen 2), when the woman was made from the rib of his side. And Jonah snored in this same sleep in the ship (Jonah 1). And the whole prophecy after the overthrow of Jerusalem and the temple, that is, of Ariel, is against the scribes and Pharisees, who, having the key of knowledge, neither enter themselves nor allow others who wish to enter. And they are commanded to be made drunk with stupor and wonder, or rather, according to the Septuagint, with the dissolution of the whole body and ecstasy of mind, and to reel and waver: staggering not with wine nor strong drink, but with the spirit of deep sleep, or of the Lord's compunction, so that, understanding their evil, they may at some time do penance and say with the prophet: I was turned in my weakness, while the thorn is fastened in me (Ps 31 [32]:4). Know, then, O scribes and Pharisees, who are the princes of the Jews, that the Lord is repaying you in kind. For when you heard the Lord the Savior, you would not understand, and you closed your eyes lest you should see him, and made your ears heavy lest you should hear. Therefore he too will close your eyes, which are the prophets, through whom you used to see the knowledge of God. Or he will close your eyes and those of the prophets, who are your princes. For the Law and the prophets were until John the Baptist (Luke 16): so that while you do not see, those may see of whom the later passage (cf. v. 18) testifies: And in that day the deaf shall hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind shall see and exult. For the Lord came for judgment, that the Jews who see might not see, and that those who were blind, namely the people of the nations, might see and contemplate the Lord (John 9). Hence he significantly did not say that the vision of all the prophets is sealed to all who read; but to you, he says, it shall be sealed, to whom I now speak, to whom I foretell that these things will come; or he will close forever the eyes of your princes, who, according to the Septuagint, boasted that they saw things hidden and secret. And all holy Scripture, he says, shall be to you closed and sealed, so that you, who suppose you know the letters of the Law and the oracles of the prophets, and meditate day and night with unwearied mouth on the volumes of the Scriptures, may not understand what you read; as it is written in the Apocalypse of John: Who is worthy to open the book and to loose its seals (Rev 5:2)? And when no one had been found to open the seals, he says that he wept, and that at last he was granted a word of God to him: Do not weep: behold, the lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has prevailed to open the book and to loose its seals. The lion of the tribe of Judah is the Lord Jesus Christ, who loosed the seals of the book, not, properly, of one book, as many think, the psalms of David, but of all the Scriptures, which were written by one Holy Spirit; and therefore they are called one book. Of this Ezekiel testifies in mystical speech (Ezek 2) that it was written within and without: in the sense and in the letter. Of this the Savior too speaks in the psalms: At the head of the book it is written of me (Ps 39 [40]:8); not of Jeremiah, not of Isaiah, but in all holy Scripture, which is called one book. Since, therefore, the teachers of the Jews to this present day cannot read and open the seals and lay open the mysteries of the Scriptures, if you give that book to the unlearned people, who are devoured by their own teachers, they will confess that they do not know letters and therefore cannot read. And of two evils it is much lighter to confess ignorance of the Law than to boast of wisdom and not be able to know what is said.

29:13-14

And the Lord said: Because this people draws near with its mouth, and glorifies me with its lips, but its heart is far from me, and they have feared me by the commandment of men and by doctrines; therefore, behold, I will proceed to cause wonder in this people by a great and astounding marvel: for wisdom shall perish from its wise men, and the understanding of its prudent men shall be hidden. LXX: And the Lord says: This people draws near to me with its mouth, and honors me with its lips, but its heart is far from me: in vain do they worship me, teaching the precepts and doctrines of men. Therefore, behold, I will proceed to remove this people: for I will remove them, and I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and hide the understanding of the prudent. The Lord used this testimony against the Pharisees in the Gospel of Matthew, saying: Why do you also transgress the commandment of God for the sake of your traditions (Matt 15:3). And again: Hypocrites, well did Isaiah prophesy of you, saying: This people honors me with its lips, but its heart is far from me. And in vain do they worship me, teaching the doctrines and precepts of men (ibid., 6-9). In this we ought to note what we have often pointed out: that the Evangelists and Apostles did not translate word for word, nor follow the authority of the Seventy translators, whose edition was already being read at that time, but, as Hebrews and men instructed in the Law, used their own words without loss to the sense. The people of the Jews draws near to God with its mouth and lips, because it boasts that it holds to the worship of the one God and rejects idols; but its heart is far from him, because it does not receive the Lord Jesus Christ. For he who does not receive the Son does not receive the Father. And at the same time let us learn how a person draws near to God, or becomes far from him. He speaks through Jeremiah too: I am a God who draws near, and not from afar, says the Lord (Jer 23:23 LXX). We draw near to God with the mind, not with the body; as we read of Moses too: Moses alone drew near to God; but the others did not draw near (Exod 24:2). For he prayed to God in spirit and in truth, and approached him with understanding and spirit. But these, of whom it is written that they are taken from the womb and instructed from boyhood to old age, and meditate day and night on the Law of God, do not draw near to God, because they accept the traditions of the Pharisees and scribes, which make them far from God; and they are whitened sepulchres, which outwardly appear beautiful but within are full of dead men's bones: they chose Barabbas and rejected the Lord (Matt 23:27). Therefore he threatens, according to the Seventy, that he will proceed, not to remove them to the Assyrians and Babylonians, but to scatter them through the whole world. According to the Hebrew, he says that he will cause great wonder and an astounding marvel to the people of the Jews, so as to destroy the wisdom of those who did not receive the power of God and the wisdom of God, and to hide and conceal the understanding of the prudent: that is, lest they find him who is contained in the letter. From this place the Apostle Paul, writing to the Corinthians, set down a testimony: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the understanding of the prudent I will reject (1 Cor 1:19): setting out the same sense in other words; not that God is an enemy of wisdom, of which he is the father, and through whom all wisdom among men exists; but he set it down with an addition, as it is in the Hebrew: of the wise of the people and of its prudent, that is, of the people of the Jews. And truly God worked a great marvel in the people after the coming of the Lord the Savior, so that at one and the same time Jerusalem burned, and the temple fell, and all the knowledge of the teachers was taken away; fulfilling what was said above (cf. Isa 3:1ff.): Behold, the Ruler, the Lord Sabaoth, shall take away from Jerusalem and from Judah the strong man and the strong woman: all the strength of bread and all the strength of water; the giant and the man of war, and the judge, and the prophet, and the diviner, and the elder, and the captain of fifty, and the wonderful counselor, and the wise architect, and the prudent hearer, and the rest that the prophetic word wove together.

29:15-16

Woe to you who are deep of heart, to hide counsel from the Lord, whose works are in darkness, and they say: Who sees us, and who knows us? This thought of yours is perverse, as if the clay should think against the potter, and the work say to its maker: You did not make me; and the thing formed say to him who formed it: You do not understand. LXX: Woe to those who make deep counsel, and their works shall be in darkness, and they say: Who sees us? who shall know us, and what we are doing? shall you not be reckoned as the potter's clay? Shall the thing made say to its maker: You did not make me wisely; or the thing formed to him who formed it: You did not make me? Against the same men of whom he had said above: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the understanding of the prudent I will reject, or, as the prophet writes, hide, the word of God is now also directed: those who are wise in themselves and prudent in their own sight. Of whom that can most rightly be understood: They have failed, searching with searching (Ps 63 [64]); since it is written of the wisdom of God: For if anyone be perfect among the sons of men without your wisdom, he shall be reckoned as nothing (Wis 9). They think God does not know their counsels because their works are in darkness, and they say: Who sees us? and who knows us? And the wise of this world, and the teachers of the heretics, and the Pharisees of the Jews say this: that no one understands them; not remembering what is said to God: Darkness shall not be dark to you: and the night shall be lit up as the day (Ps 138 [139]:12). And: As is his darkness, so also is his light (Gen 3). Deceived by this error, Adam and Eve, hearing the sound of the feet of God walking in paradise, hid themselves under the tree in which was the knowledge of good and evil; and Cain too, saying: If you cast me out today from your face, I shall be hidden (Gen 4:14), with like folly thought that God did not know. And through Amos it is said of the ungodly and sinners: If they hide themselves from my eyes in the depth of the sea, there I will command the serpent, and it shall bite them (Amos 9:3). Hence, however wise someone may be and of the most ardent talent, if he does not have the wisdom and teaching of God, let us say of him: Unless the Lord builds the house, they labor in vain who build it. Unless the Lord guards the city, he who guards it watches in vain (Ps 126 [127]:1). And let us make a saying like it: Unless the Lord helps knowledge, he labors in vain who thinks himself wise. Unless the Lord keeps our heart with all watchfulness, he watches in vain who thinks it can be kept by his own diligence. This thought of yours, he says, is perverse: that you should think the maker does not know what he has made, and the Creator is ignorant of his creature; as if the clay and the work should say to the potter and its maker: You did not make me, or you did not make me well, nor do you understand your handiwork. The Apostle uses this testimony in other words in writing to the Romans, where he discusses the deep knowledge of God and seeks to refute the false charge of men: O man, who are you to answer back to God? Does the thing formed say to him who formed it: Why have you made me thus? Or has not the potter power over the same clay to make one vessel unto honor and another unto dishonor (Rom 9:20-21). In all these that rule must always be observed: the Evangelists and Apostles translated from the Hebrew into Greek as seemed good to them, without loss to the sense.

29:17ff.

Is it not yet a little while, and a short time, and Lebanon shall be turned into Charmel, and Charmel shall be reckoned as a forest? And in that day the deaf shall hear the words of the book, and out of darkness and gloom the eyes of the blind shall see. And the meek shall increase their joy in the Lord, and the poor among men shall exult in the Holy One of Israel: for he who prevailed has failed. The scorner is consumed, and all who watched for iniquity have been cut down: who made men sin by a word, and tripped up him who reproved in the gate, and turned aside in vain from the righteous. Let the Jews answer, and the friends of the bare history alone, who seek not fruit on the tree but only the leaves and the shade of words, which quickly withers and perishes: how at the coming of the Lord the Savior (since from the times of Isaiah to the dispensation of the flesh he assumed is, compared with eternity, a short and little space of time) Lebanon, a mountain of Phoenicia, was turned and transferred into Mount Carmel, which in Hebrew is called CHERMEL (כרמל), and lies on the border of Palestine and Phoenicia, overlooking Ptolemais (though another mountain too is called Carmel in the holy Scriptures, where lived Nabal the Carmelite (1 Sam 25), a foolish and wicked man, who had as wife Abigail, who on her husband's death married David; for while he lived she could not take David as husband, lest she be called an adulteress if she were joined to another man); and how Charmel is reckoned as a forest and as unfruitful trees? Since they cannot say this, let them hear that Lebanon, which means whitening, refers to the people of the nations, which, washed in the Lord and its former filth purged away, ascending wholly clean, leans upon the Savior in the person of the Church; and of it it is said in the Song of Songs: Who is this who comes up whitened, leaning upon her kinsman (Song 8:5); and that this people is transferred into Charmel, that is, into the knowledge of circumcision, so as to recognize the mysteries of the spiritual and true circumcision, and to be in the place once held by the people of the Jews; while those who would not receive Christ are reckoned as a forest and as barren trees, which cannot praise the Lord with the fruit-bearing trees. When Lebanon has been changed into Charmel, and Charmel into a forest, then those who before were deaf and could not hear the words of the prophetic book (of which we said above that all holy Scripture is called one book, as the Preacher says (Eccl 12:11): The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails fixed deep, which are given from the councils by one shepherd) shall hear, and shall speak, those to whom the Savior will say: Ephphetha, which means be opened (Mark 7). And where we translated: out of darkness and gloom the eyes of the blind shall see, whose interpretation is easy, Aquila and Theodotion and Symmachus translated: The eyes of the blind shall see darkness and gloom: to show that the mysteries of Christ were to be laid open to the people of the nations, which before was blind, according to what is said: Dark water in the clouds of the air (Ps 17 [18]:12). And in the same psalm it is written of God: He made darkness his hiding place (ibid., 12). And in Proverbs we read: A wise man hearing these things will be wiser, and the prudent will possess government; and he will understand a parable and dark speech, the sayings of the wise and riddles (Prov 1:5-6). Indeed Moses too, that he might understand and see God (Exod 20), entered into the cloud and into the thick darkness, of which it is said in the Psalm: Thick darkness under his feet (Ps 17 [18]:10). When those who were before blind have either beheld all the mystical things, or have lifted their eyes from blindness and darkness to see, so that the true light may rise for those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death: then the meek, of whom it is written: Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the earth (Matt 5:4); or the poor, whose prince says in the psalms: This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him (Ps 33 [34]:7); and: who shall judge the poor of the people, and shall save the sons of the poor (Ps 71 [72]:4), of whom it is said to the Jews: You have despised the counsel of the poor man: these shall increase their joy in the Lord, so that he who glories may glory in the Lord (2 Cor 10); and the poor among men, or those despaired of and despised by men, who before had no knowledge of the Law, shall exult in the Holy One of Israel, who says: Be holy, for I am holy (Lev 11:44). And there is every exultation, because he who prevailed has failed. The scorner is consumed, or the arrogant and proud one, who had said: By strength I will do it, and by wisdom; I will remove the bounds of the nations and lay waste their strength; who mocked all, so much so that the saint too said: My loins are filled with illusions (Ps 37 [38]:8). And all who watched for iniquity have been cut down, or destroyed, whose destruction, because of their evil watchings, does not slumber: who made the whole race of men sin by a word of blasphemy, so that they denied the Word of God and set their mouth against heaven. He means the demons, who, wicked themselves, made all men sin in speech, blaspheming with various dogmas; and as far as in them lay they tripped up him who reproved in the gate and in judgment, and made him turn aside from righteousness, who was in the gates of the daughter of Zion, lifted up from the gates of death; and who rebuked those who hated him who reproved in the gates. What we have understood of the devil and his angels, the Nazarenes think was said against the scribes and Pharisees: that the δευτερωταί have failed, who before mocked the people with most wicked traditions, and watched day and night to deceive the simple, who made men sin against the Word of God, so that they denied Christ the Son of God.

29:22ff.

Therefore thus says the Lord to the house of Jacob, he who redeemed Abraham: Jacob shall not now be confounded, nor shall his face now blush: but when he sees his sons, the works of my hands, in his midst sanctifying my name: and they shall sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall proclaim the God of Israel; and those who err in spirit shall know understanding, and the mutterers shall learn the Law. LXX: Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the house of Jacob, which he separated from Abraham: Jacob shall not now be confounded, nor shall he now change his face; but when he sees his sons, my works: for my sake they shall sanctify my name, and they shall sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall fear the God of Israel; and those who err in spirit shall know understanding, and the mutterers shall learn obedience; and what follows, ÷ and the stammering tongues shall learn to speak peace ⁚, is to be marked with an obelus. When, he says, the deaf have heard the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind have seen, and Lebanon has been turned into Charmel, and Charmel reckoned as a forest, so that the meek and the poor rejoice in the Lord, and the proud man and the scorner fail: then Jacob shall be confounded, who now, for the time being, is not confounded. He means the times of Isaiah. And his face shall blush, so that blushing and confusion may be an occasion of salvation, especially when he sees his sons, that is, the Apostles and apostolic men, who were of the race of the Jews, performing the mighty works of the Lord in the midst of the nations, and proclaiming the name of Christ to the Gentiles, and saying: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name (Matt 6:9). For they will sanctify the Holy One who sprang from Jacob, and will teach the God of Israel among the nations, so that, having abandoned idols, they say: How false are the idols our fathers possessed, and there is none among them who gives rain; and then those who now err in spirit shall know the understanding of God, and those who once murmured against the Lord in the wilderness shall learn the Law, of which before they had no knowledge. For if they had received Moses, they would have received the Lord Jesus Christ too, since Moses spoke of him. What at the beginning of the chapter we translated according to the Hebrew: Thus says the Lord to the house of Jacob, he who redeemed once Abraham, and brought him out of the Chaldeans, and led him into the land of promise (Gen 11), is perfectly plain. But what the Seventy translated: Thus says the Lord concerning the house of Jacob, which he separated from Abraham, can be understood thus: that he separated the scribes and Pharisees, who blasphemed the Lord, from Abraham, who saw the day of the Lord and rejoiced (John 8). For if they had been sons of Abraham, they would have done the works of Abraham. And the Apostle argues that those are to be called sons of Abraham (Heb 11) who have the likeness of Abraham's faith, that is, the people of the nations, which was called the son of Abraham not from works but from faith.

30:1ff.

Woe, you deserting sons, says the Lord: that you should take counsel, and not from me; and weave a web, and not by my Spirit; that you might add sin upon sin. You who walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked my mouth, hoping for help in the strength of Pharaoh, and having confidence in the shadow of Egypt. And the strength of Pharaoh shall be to you for confusion, and the confidence in the shadow of Egypt for disgrace. For your princes shall be in Tanis, and your messengers have come as far as Hanes. All are confounded over a people that will not be able to profit them: they were not for help nor for any use, but for confusion and for reproach. LXX: Woe, you transgressing sons, says the Lord. You have taken counsel, and not through me; and a pact, not through my spirit, that you might add sins to sins: you who go to go down into Egypt, and have not asked me, that you may receive help from Pharaoh and be protected by the Egyptians. The protection of Pharaoh shall be to you for confusion, and to those who trust in Egypt, a reproach. For there are in Tanis princes, most evil messengers. In vain shall they labor for a people that will not profit them for help, nor for use, but for confusion and reproach. After the prophecy against Ariel, and the other things that the preceding discourse set forth up to this place, there now begins another prophecy, which is shown to have been fulfilled after the hundred and fifty years that lay between Isaiah and Jeremiah.
