Now the worm, which in Hebrew is called THOLATH (תולעת), is the name given, for its lowliness and contempt, to the choir of the Apostles, imitating the Savior, who speaks in the psalm: I am a worm, and no man, a reproach of men, and the outcast of the people (Ps 21 [22]:7). For as a worm penetrates the earth, so the apostolic word penetrated the cities of the nations, and entered first into the hardest hearts. And rightly they are called few out of Israel, because in comparison with the whole world very few of the Jewish nation believed, to whom the Lord says in the Gospel: Do not fear, little flock (Luke 12:32). Or, according to the Hebrew, dead out of Israel, who say with the Apostle: I die daily (1 Cor 15:31); and elsewhere: I am crucified with Christ. Yet I live, not I; but Christ lives in me (Gal 2:20). And what follows, I have made you like a new threshing wagon, having sawing teeth, signifies this: that the preaching of the Gospel crushes the adverse powers and the spiritual wickedness that lifts itself up against the knowledge of God, which, according to the variety of their pride, are called mountains and hills; and when these are carried off and scattered after the manner of a whirlwind, let Israel exult and rejoice in the Lord, the Holy One of Israel. We can also say that the churchman, having the sawing teeth of the Gospel preaching on a new wagon, which works not in the oldness of the letter but in the newness of the spirit, crushes the hardest hearts of unbelievers, separating the wheat from the chaff and crushing the mountains and hills, that is, all the chiefs of the heretics, so that, crushed and ground down, they are reduced to dust and are taught that they are nothing, so that those who had been wrongly gathered together may be divided for their own good.

41:17ff.

The needy and the poor seek water, and there is none; their tongue is parched with thirst. I the Lord will hear them; I the God of Israel will not forsake them. I will open rivers on the sloping hills, and fountains in the midst of the plains. I will make the desert into a pool of waters, and the trackless land into streams of waters. I will put in the wilderness the cedar and the thorn, and the myrtle, and the olive tree. I will set in the desert the fir, the elm and the box together, that they may see and know and consider and understand together that the hand of the Lord has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created it. LXX: And the poor and the needy will exult; for they will seek water, and there will be none; their tongue has dried up for thirst. I the Lord God will hear them, the God of Israel, and I will not forsake them; but I will open rivers on the mountains, and fountains in the midst of the plains; I will make the desert into marshes, and the thirsty land into watercourses. I will put in a land without water the cedar, and the box, and the myrtle, and the cypress, and the poplar, that they may see and know and think and understand together that the hand of the Lord has done these things, and the Holy One of Israel has shown it. The people of the nations, poor and meager, which did not have the knowledge of the truth, seeks wholesome waters through various teachers and the diverse doctrines of the philosophers, and does not find them, because there are none; their tongue is parched with thirst, without the Law and the Prophets. For, according to the faith of the Gospel, it had spent all its substance on physicians (Luke 8), and could not be freed from the gore of idolatry and the blood of victims. Therefore the Lord, the God of Israel, did not wholly forsake them, nor let them perish for ever, but opened rivers on the sloping hills, or on the mountains, and fountains in the midst of the plains. These rivers took their beginning from that river which is read of in the Psalms: The rush of the river gladdens the city of God (Ps 45 [46]:4); and in another place: The river of God is filled with waters. These waters and fountains flowed from that fountain who speaks through Jeremiah: They have forsaken me, the fountain of living water (Jer 2:13). And above in this same Prophet it is said: They will drink waters from the fountains of the Savior. Of these also it is sung in the Psalms: Bless the Lord God from the fountains of Israel (Ps 67 [68]:27). And he made, he says, the desert into a pool of waters, and the trackless land into streams of waters. Of these waters the Savior too spoke in the Gospel in mystical language (John 4:13-14): Whoever drinks of the water that I shall give him will not thirst for ever; but the water that I shall give him will become in him a fountain of water springing up into eternal life. And again: If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink. Whoever drinks of the water that I shall give him, out of his belly will flow rivers of living water (ibid. 7:37-39). But this, says the Evangelist, he spoke of the Holy Spirit, whom those who believed in him were to receive. Since, then, the multitude of the Church, once a desert, had been watered with life-giving waters, therefore, according to the Seventy, there spring up in it the cedar, and the box, and the myrtle, and the cypress, and the poplar; according to the Hebrew and the other translators, the cedar, the setta, and the myrtle, and the olive tree, and the fir, and the elm, and the box together. These varieties of trees signify the diversity of spiritual grace. And because the nature of the others is known to all, let us discuss only the Hebrew SETTA (שטה), which Theodotion translated thorn. It is a kind of tree growing in the desert, resembling the white thorn, of which all the wood of the ark and the furnishings of the tabernacle were made, which are called Settim (Exod 37): a wood that does not rot and is very light, and that surpasses all woods in solidity and beauty, as much in strength as in sheen. The cedar, too, and the cypress and the myrtle are of the finest fragrance and do not rot. The elm also and the poplar, or the box, are either joined to vines to wed them, or are most fit for various works. And all these are set together in the wilderness, so that not even one string of the Lord's lyre, and no power of the graces of the Church, may seem to be lacking: so that all may understand, and together know in their mind, that the hand of the Lord has accomplished all these things, so that in the dryness of the nations streams of virtues should be found, and in a land once deserted and full of salt the cedar and the cypress and other trees should spring up, whose loftiness and crown hastening toward heavenly things the olive tree should illuminate, which is the nourishment of light and the rest of those who labor.

41:21ff.

Bring your judgment near, says the Lord; bring forward whatever you may have, said the king of Jacob. Let them approach and tell us whatever things are to come; tell the former things that have been, and we will set our heart on them and we will know their last end; and show us the things that are to come. Declare the things that are to come hereafter, and we will know that you are gods. Do good also, or evil, if you can, and let us speak and see together. Behold, you are of nothing: and your work is of that which is not; an abomination is he who has chosen you. LXX: Your judgment is near, says the Lord God; your counsels have come and drawn near, says the king of Jacob. Let them draw near and declare to us the things that are to come; or tell the former things that were, and we will apply our mind, and we will know what the last things are. Tell us also the things to come, and declare the things that are to come at the last, and we will know that you are gods. Do good and evil, and we will marvel, and we will see together whence you are and whence your work is: from a land of abominations they have chosen you. As we said above that there are two Jacobs and two Israels, of those who do not believe and of those who believe in the Lord the Savior, so, when the nations have been called, and rivers and fountains have burst forth in the once desert Church, and it is wonderfully leafy with a variety of trees, all of them full of abundance, those of the nations who refused to believe in Christ are summoned to judgment, to answer why they refused to see and know and consider and understand that the hand of the Lord has done these things and the Holy One of Israel has created all things. Let your idols approach, he says, which you think most mighty. Or bring forward whatever you may have in yourselves, and lay open your counsels: on what ground, with what mind, you refused to receive the manifest truth. And at the same time an apostrophe is made to the idols themselves, which are without sense and possess the faculty neither of hearing nor of answering. Tell us, he says, either things past or things to come, and show your power by the outcome of events. Now this signifies that after the coming of Christ all the idols fell silent. Where is Delphic Apollo, and Loxias, and the Delian, and the Clarian, and the other idols that promised knowledge of the future, which deceived the most powerful kings? Why could they foretell nothing of Christ, nothing of his Apostles, nothing of the ruin and abolition of their temples? If, then, they could not foretell their own destruction, how could they announce what concerned others, whether evil or good? But if anyone says that many things were foretold by idols, it must be known that they always joined falsehood to truth, and so tempered their sentences that whether something good or something evil happened, either could be understood. Such is that oracle to Pyrrhus king of the Epirotes: I say that you, son of Aeacus, the Romans can conquer. And to Croesus: Croesus, having crossed the Halys, will destroy the greatest kingdoms. There is also another sign that idols are not gods: that they can do neither good nor evil. Not that idols, or the demons that sit by idols, have not often done evil; but that, unless power has been granted to them by the Lord, they cannot do it. Indeed, in the Gospel they beg to have power over the herd of swine (Matt 8). And in Job we read that without the Lord's command he [the devil] could not destroy even the beasts and possessions of the holy man (Job 1). Nor is this to be wondered at in God's case, since even the Apostle Paul delivers some to Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme (1 Tim 1). Or else it must be said that mute images of men, without sense, can do neither good nor evil, nor know things past nor things to come, because they are of nothing and of that which is not, and it is not so much they as he who worships them that is worthy of abomination. For the idols of the nations are silver and gold, the works of men's hands. They have a mouth, and will not speak (Ps 113 [115]:13). How then can they know and announce things to come, or relate things past, and do good or evil, when they have neither the sense of men nor that of brute animals? Nor does it matter of what material they seem to be made, since all are earthly.

41:25f.

I have raised up from the North, and he will come from the rising of the sun; he will call upon my name, and he will bring on rulers as mud, and as a potter treading the ground. Who has announced it from the beginning, that we may know; and from the first, that we may say: You are righteous? There is none announcing, nor foretelling, nor hearing your words. The first will say to Zion: Behold, they are here; and to Jerusalem I will give a bearer of good tidings. And I looked, and there was not even any of these who would enter into counsel, and, when asked, would answer a word. Behold, all are unrighteous, and their works are vain; their images are wind and emptiness. LXX: But I have raised up him who is from the North, and him who is from the rising of the sun; they will be called by my name. Let princes come, and as the clay of the potter, and as a potter treading clay, so you will be trodden down. For who will announce to you the things that are from the beginning, that we may know the things that are in the future, and we will say that it is true? There is none who foretells , nor who hears your words. I will give a beginning to Zion, and I will comfort Jerusalem on the way; for of the nations there is none, and of their images there was none who announced; and if I ask them, Where are you from? they will not answer me; for they are your makers, and they lead you astray in vain. He still speaks against the idols, and against those who after the coming of Christ refused to forsake them. And while they remain in error, he says that he himself has raised up the people of the nations from the North. For from the North evils will blaze forth upon all the inhabitants of the earth. And to Jeremiah it is said: What do you see, Jeremiah? And he answered: A pot set on fire, and its face from the face of the North (Jer 1:13). But they are raised up from the North, so that they may believe in him who has come from the rising of the sun, of whom we read above: Who raised up the righteous one from the East, or righteousness? And in another place: Behold a man, the Dayspring is his name (Zech 6:12). He will call them by my name, so that, forsaking their images, they may worship the one God. For he himself says in the Gospel: I have come in the name of my Father, and you did not receive me; another will come in his own name, and you will receive him (John 5:43). He will tread down the princes and rulers and all the pride of the world, and they will be made subject to him as clay to the potter, so that from them he may make one vessel for honor and another for dishonor (Rom 9). These things, which, according to prophetic custom, I say that I have done as though they were already past, or, according to Symmachus, which I promise as future, none of the demons and idols can foretell. Hence all the oracles fell silent, because there is no one who announces, no one who hears, while the once brutish hearts of the Gentiles have understood their error and forsaken false prophecies. And the Lord will speak first to Zion, that is, to his Church, and will say to her: Behold, here are your sons, whom I have given to you through faith in me. And he means the Apostles, who preached the Gospel in the whole world. Zion and Jerusalem differ in name; but as there is one city, so also there is one Church. Let all the nations, therefore, which follow the error of idols, be questioned by us, so that they may answer whence they are. And this will be the answer of them all: that all follow vanity and the winds, and worship the works of their own hands. Whatever we have said of the idols and the nations, let us refer to the doctrines of perversity, and to their chiefs, the heresiarchs: that while Christ announces the peace of the Church and shows them the way of truth, they follow error and are likened to wind and whirlwind. The Hebrews interpret the one raised up from the North and coming from the rising of the sun as the Assyrian and the Persian, who came to Jerusalem and trod down all its princes; and none of the idols which they worshiped knew that this would come, but the Lord alone, who punished them for their sins.

42:1f.

Behold my servant, I will uphold him; my chosen one, in him my soul is well pleased. I have put my spirit upon him; he will bring forth judgment to the nations. He will not cry out, nor will he accept a person, nor will his voice be heard outside. A bruised reed he will not break, and smoking flax he will not quench; in truth he will bring forth judgment. He will not be sad nor troubled, until he sets judgment in the earth; and the islands will wait for his law. LXX: Jacob my child, I will take him up; Israel my chosen one, my soul has received him. I have put my spirit upon him; he will bring forth judgment to the nations; he will not cry out, nor will he let go, nor will his voice be heard outside. A broken reed he will not break, and smoking flax he will not quench; but in truth he will bring forth judgment. He will shine and will not be broken, until he sets judgment upon the earth; and in his name the nations will hope. Jacob and Israel are not found in the present passage, which the Evangelist Matthew too did not set down, following the Hebrew truth. We say this to the shame of those who despise our work. This has been discussed more fully in the little Commentaries on Matthew, and in the book which we recently wrote to Algasia. Meanwhile it must be noted that where it is written of the choir of the Apostles, they are called both Jacob and Israel and the seed of Abraham, to whom, as to men and servants, it is said accordingly: Do not fear, worm Jacob, and Israel small in number. But where the prophecy is of Christ, it is read without Jacob and Israel: Behold my servant, I will uphold him; my chosen one, in him my soul is well pleased. And in what follows: I have given you as a covenant of the race, as a light of the nations, to open the eyes of the blind, and to bring the bound out of their chains, and those who dwell in darkness out of the prison house. Nor is it to be wondered at if he is called a servant, made of a woman, made under the law (Gal 4); he who, though he was in the form of God, humbled himself, taking the form of a servant, and was found in fashion as a man (Phil 2). In him the soul of God was well pleased, seeing that all virtues were in him; nay rather, that he himself was the power and wisdom of God. I have put, he says, my spirit upon him: the Spirit who descended in the form of a dove. He will bring forth judgment to the nations, which before they did not know. He will not cry out: for he will be gentle and meek; and he will not accept a person in judgment, or he will not lift up (it is understood) his voice on high. Or, according to Symmachus, he will not be deceived, understanding all the snares of the devil; or, according to the Seventy, he will not let go, namely the people of the Jews, calling them to repentance. Nor will his voice be heard outside: for he did not preach the Gospel outside Galilee and Judea among the other nations. And if we read that he was in the borders of Tyre and Sidon (Matt 15), or in the region of Caesarea Philippi, which is now called Paneas, still it must be known that it is not written that he entered those cities themselves. A bruised reed, or a broken one, he will not break. For he will be easy to appease toward all, and will give pardon to sinners, saying to the woman: Take heart, daughter, your sins are forgiven you (Luke 7:48). And smoking flax, or, as the others translated, dim and dark, he will not quench: those who were near to being quenched were preserved by the clemency of the Lord (which we have discussed in the works mentioned above concerning the Jews and the nations); but he will judge all things with truth, in no way fearing the scribes and Pharisees, whom he boldly called hypocrites (Matt 7, 15, 22, 23 throughout, and Luke 6, 12). But what follows, He will shine and will not be broken, until he sets judgment upon the earth, the Evangelist Matthew did not set down (Matt 12); or else the words in the middle, between judgment and judgment, were removed by a scribe's error. And it signifies that, rising from the dead, he enlightened all, and was not broken by death, until he set judgment upon the earth, he who said in the Gospel: For judgment I came into this world, that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind (John 9:39). For this we translated: He will not be sad, nor troubled, but he will keep an evenness of countenance at all times: what the philosophers falsely boast of Socrates, that he was never sadder or happier than usual. For this Aquila and Theodotion translated: He will not darken, and he will not run, until he sets judgment in the earth. And the sense is: he will deter no one by sadness of countenance, nor will he hasten to punishment, he who has reserved the truth of judgment for the last time. And what follows, and the islands will wait for his law, the Seventy set down more plainly: in his name the nations will hope; these are called islands in the Scriptures because they lie open on every side to the inroads of persecutors. And by his law let us understand not that which was given through Moses, but the Gospel: For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem (above, Isa 2). Of this law Jeremiah too prophesies: Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will make a new covenant, not according to the covenant which I once made with their fathers (Jer 31:31-32).

42:5-6f.

Thus says the Lord God, who creates the heavens and stretches them out, who makes firm the earth and the things that spring from it, who gives breath to the people that is upon it, and spirit to those who tread on it: I the Lord have called you in righteousness, and have taken hold of your hand, and have kept you, and have given you as a covenant of the people, as a light of the nations, that you might open the eyes of the blind, and bring the bound out of confinement, out of the prison house those who sit in darkness. I am the Lord, that is my name; my glory I will not give to another, nor my praise to graven images. The former things, behold, they have come; new things too I declare; before they spring up, I will make you hear of them: It was uncertain who had said before: Behold my servant, I will uphold him; my chosen one, in him my soul is well pleased. I have put my spirit upon him; he will bring forth judgment to the nations. For after the condemnation of the idols the speech had burst out suddenly: Behold my servant, and the rest, which we interpreted as spoken in the person of the Father concerning Christ. So, lest he leave it ambiguous who had said the foregoing, he adds and says: Thus says the Lord God, who creates the heavens and stretches them out. Or, as the Seventy translated: Who made the heaven and fixed it. The Creator and Lord of the universe, therefore, himself promised the coming of his Christ, he who not only stretched out the heavens and fixed them, but also made the earth firm with its lofty mass, and all things that spring from it: so that his invisible things may be clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made (Rom 1), his eternal power also and divinity. He gave breath to all who dwell on the earth, by the first law of mortals: for God breathed into the face of Adam the spirit of life, and he became a living soul (Gen 2). But spirit he gave properly to those who tread on the earth and subject the wisdom of the flesh to their own power. He, then, whose praises are so great, spoke these things to him whose law the islands and the nations await: I the Lord have called you in righteousness: of whom he himself speaks in the Gospel: Righteous Father, the world does not know you (John 17:25); so that he might be the God not only of the Jews but also of the nations. And I have taken hold of your hand, because whatever the Son works, the Father works. And I have kept you, you who yourself preserve all things. And I have given you as a covenant of the people of Israel, to whom I had promised beforehand that you would come. And as a light of the nations, which sat in darkness and in the shadow of death, that you might open the eyes of the blind, who before did not see God. And bring the bound out of confinement (Prov 5); for each one is bound fast by the cords of his own sins. And in the Gospel the Lord loosed him whom Satan had bound (Matt 8). Out of the prison house those who sit in darkness, those who were living in the night and gloom of error. And what he adds, I am the Lord, that is my name; my glory I will not give to another, does not exclude the Son; for when he says in the Gospel, Father, glorify me with the glory which I had with you before the world was (John 17:5), the Father himself answered: I have both glorified it, and will glorify it. For he did not say: My glory I will give to no one, for if he had said that, he would have excluded the Son too; but my glory I will not give to another, besides you, to whom I have given it, to whom I will give it. Hence I greatly admire the propriety of holy Scripture, in that all the translators, who are accustomed to disagree in many other places, translated the word AHER (אחר) with one voice another. And that we may know that by this sentence not the Son but the idols are excluded, the following words bear witness: Nor my praise to graven images. For which the Seventy have: nor my powers to images. For since Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God, he contains in himself all the powers of the Father. There follows: The former things, behold, they have come. And the sense is: What I have spoken, what I have promised through Moses and the Prophets, all has been fulfilled. But now I announce to you the Gospel, the calling of the nations, the passion of Christ, the newness of faith: so that as you see the former things fulfilled in fact, so you may also believe that the things I now promise will come,

42:10-11f.

Sing to God a new song, his praise from the ends of the earth, you who go down to the sea, and its fullness, the islands and their inhabitants. Let the desert and its cities lift up; Kedar will dwell in houses; give praise, you inhabitants of Petra; from the top of the mountains they will cry out. They will give glory to the Lord, and will declare his praise in the islands. The Lord will go forth as a mighty one, as a man of war he will stir up zeal; he will shout and cry aloud; he will prevail over his enemies. I have always held my peace, I have kept silent, I have been patient; like a woman giving birth I will speak; I will scatter and swallow up at once. I will make the mountains and hills desolate, and I will dry up all their grass; and I will turn the rivers into islands, and I will dry up the pools. And I will lead out the blind into a way that they do not know, and in paths of which they are ignorant I will make them walk. I will turn darkness before them into light, and crooked things into straight. These words I have done for them, and I have not forsaken them. They have turned back; let them be confounded with confusion, who trust in a graven image, who say to a molten image: You are our gods. LXX: Sing to the Lord a new song; his dominion is glorified, and his name from the top of the earth; those who go down to the sea and sail it, the islands and their inhabitants. Rejoice, O desert, and its villages, the farmsteads and the inhabitants of Kedar. Those who dwell in Petra will rejoice; from the top of the mountains they will cry out. They will give glory to God; they will declare his powers in the islands. The Lord God of powers will go forth and will crush war; he will stir up zeal, and will cry out over his enemies with strength. I have held my peace from the beginning; shall I always hold my peace and endure? Like a woman giving birth I have been patient; I will burst forth and will dry up at once; I will lay waste mountains and hills, and I will dry up all their hay. And I will turn the rivers into islands, and I will dry up the marshes. And I will lead the blind by a way that they do not know, and I will make them tread paths of which they have been ignorant; I will turn darkness into light for them, and crooked things into straight. These words I will do for them, and I will not forsake them; but they have turned back. Be confounded with confusion, you who trust in graven images, who say to molten images: You are our gods. He who had said before, The former things, behold, they have come; new things too I declare; before they spring up, I will make you hear of them, and had promised that he would tell what they did not know, declares in the following discourse what those new things are, commanding the Apostles and apostolic men to sing a new song, in no way in the oldness of the letter, but in the newness of the spirit; and not only in the old Instrument, but in the new; and that his praise should reach even to the ends of the earth. For his going forth is from the highest heaven, and his circuit even to its height (Ps 18 [19]). The sound of the Apostles went out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world. Or, according to the Seventy: Glorify his name in the ends of the earth: so that in the whole world the name of Christ may be announced to the nations. And who these are who are to sing the new song, the following words declare: You who go down, he says, to the sea, and sail it, or the fullness of the sea. For Jesus, seeing the Apostles on the shore by the sea of Gennesaret mending their nets, called them and sent them into the great sea (Luke 5), so that from fishers of fish he might make them fishers of men; and they preached the Gospel from Jerusalem as far as Illyricum and the Spains, capturing in a short time even the might of the city of Rome itself. Or certainly they went down to the sea and sailed it, enduring the storms and persecutions of this world. By the islands too and their inhabitants understand either the diversity of the nations or the multitude of the Churches. Let, he says, the desert and its cities lift up their voice, of which we have also spoken above. Or let the desert rejoice, and its villages, and Kedar, which was once an uninhabitable region beyond Arabia, of the Saracens; and the inhabitants of Petra, which itself is also a city of Palestine. And this signifies that the people of the nations, formerly a desert as regards the knowledge of God and bound by the errors of idolatry, is turned to the praises of the Lord. Or, because Kedar means darkness, and, according to the Apostle (1 Cor 10), the rock is Christ, all believers are commanded that those who were before in darkness, and now believe in the Lord the Savior, should cry aloud from the top of the mountains and openly preach Christ, those to whom it was said also above (cf. Isa 40:9): Go up on a high mountain, you who bring good tidings to Zion; lift up your voice with strength, you who bring good tidings to Jerusalem. And I will set his glory in the islands, of which we spoke before. And the prophetic word describes the glorious coming of the Savior, of which the Apostle Paul also speaks: According to the illumination of the glory of the great God and our Savior Jesus Christ (2 Cor 4; 2 Tim 1:10); and compares him to a most mighty man, who is about to fight against his adversaries and to stir up zeal. Of this it was prophesied also in the Song of Deuteronomy: They have moved me to jealousy with that which was not God, and have provoked me with their idols; and I will move them to jealousy with a nation that is not, and with a most foolish nation I will provoke them (Deut 32:21). He will also shout and cry aloud against his enemies, openly rebuking their unbelief and declaring with a loud cry: I have held my peace, I have always kept silent, I have been patient, or, as the Seventy translated: I have held my peace; shall I always hold my peace (Eccl 3:7)? So that what is said through Solomon may be fulfilled: A time to keep silence, and a time to speak. And the sense is: For a long time I have often borne you when you sinned; but because I had kept silent before, I will no longer keep silent. And as a woman giving birth pours forth the infant into the light, and makes open what was before held shut in her womb, so I will now bring forth my pain and the forbearance which I always had over your crimes, and I will scatter your counsels; and at one time I will swallow up the whole nation, and all the pride of your mountains and the swelling of your hills. And the grass, of which it was said above, Truly the people is grass, that is, princes as much as the common herd, I will reduce to a desert. This was added in the Seventy, which had passed over these words in silence, from the edition of Theodotion (see above, Isa 40:7). And when I have dried you up and destroyed you from head to foot, then I will make the rivers of my teaching run in the islands of the nations, and I will reduce your pools or marshes to dryness, so that among the nations there may be the knowledge of the Scriptures, and among you the dryness of teaching. And I will lead the blind by the way which before they did not know, of whom we also read above: I have given you as a covenant of the people, as a light of the nations, that you might open the eyes of the blind. These will be led by the way of which Christ speaks: I am the way, or by the way of the knowledge of God; and I will make them walk by the paths of the Prophets. Then their darkness will be changed into light, and crooked things will be turned into straight, so that they may understand what they read, and with the eyes of the heart behold the clear light of Christ in the Old Testament. And at the same time he adds: These words which I have done, or I will do for them: no longer promising things to come, but rendering what I had promised before. But while I say these things, the people of the Jews has turned back, so as not to believe him who promises, and to be confounded in its errors, and to neglect the pledge of God, having before believed in idols. Or, when the fullness of the nations has come in, then the people of Israel too will be converted (Rom 11), and will repent of its error, through which it had before served idols. Or certainly, after the calling of the nations, he returns to the beginning, so as to say that all the nations which refused to believe the Gospel are to be confounded in their idols.

42:18-19ff.

You deaf, hear, and you blind, look, that you may see. Who is blind but my servant? and deaf but he to whom I have sent my messengers? Who is blind but he who has been sold? and who is blind but the servant of the Lord? You who see many things, will you not keep them? you who have open ears, will you not hear? And the Lord willed to sanctify him, and to magnify the law and exalt it. But this is a people plundered and laid waste; all are the snare of young men, and they are hidden in prison houses; they have become a prey, and there is none to rescue; a plunder, and there is none to say: Give back. Who is there among you who will hear this, who will attend and listen for the time to come? Who gave Jacob up to plunder, and Israel to those who lay waste? Was it not the Lord himself, against whom we have sinned? And they would not walk in his ways, and they did not hear his law. And he poured out upon him the indignation of his fury, and strong war; and he burned him round about, and he did not know it; and he set him on fire, and he did not understand. LXX: You deaf, hear, and you blind, look up, that you may see. Who is blind but my children, and deaf but those who rule over them? Who is blind but he who has received; and the servants of God have been blinded. You have often seen, and have not kept watch; your ears are open, and you have not heard. The Lord God willed that he should be justified, and should magnify praise. And I saw, and the people was laid waste and plundered. For there is a snare in the chambers everywhere, and in the houses together, in which they hid them. They became a plunder, and there was none to rescue the prey, and there was none to say: Give back. Who is there among you who will hear these things and know the things to come? Who gave Jacob up to plunder, and Israel to those who lay waste? Was it not God, against whom they sinned? And you would not walk in his ways, nor hear his law. And he brought upon them the anger of his fury, and war prevailed against them, and those who burned them round about; and each one did not know, nor did they lay it to heart. Lest anyone should think that what is said, You deaf, hear, and you blind, look, that you may see, belongs to the people of the nations, which before was deaf and blind (as the Jews strive to prove by a foolish interpretation), the prophetic word itself shows who ought to be understood as the deaf and the blind. Who, he says, is blind but my servant, and deaf but he to whom I have sent my messengers? There is no doubt that he means the Prophets. Who is blind but he who has been sold by his sins? Who is blind but he who formerly was the servant of the Lord? To him it is said: O Israel, you who see many things, and have very many Prophets through whom to know the commandments of God, will you not keep what has been commanded you? You who have open ears, will you not hear what is said? Of whom we also read above: Hearing you will hear, and will not understand; and seeing you will look, and will not see; for the heart of this people has been made fat (Isa 6:9). The Lord, he says, willed to sanctify him, and to magnify his Law, and to exalt and raise up the people lying prostrate. But he refused to do the will of God, and therefore he was plundered and laid waste by his adversaries, whom we ought to understand either as demons or as enemies. All are the snare of young men, and they are hidden in prison houses. Or, as the Seventy translated, There is a snare in the chambers everywhere, and in the houses together, in which they hid them: signifying the scribes and Pharisees, who deceived the wretched common people and everywhere laid snares against the Lord the Savior and his Apostles (Luke 11), having the key of knowledge, neither entering themselves, and forbidding others who wished to enter. And beautifully he called their breasts, in which the worst thoughts dwelt, prisons. Therefore they became a prey and a plunder, and there was none to free them and to speak a word on their behalf. And at the same time the Prophet exhorts them that, if all cannot hear, at least a few may know the things to come and understand from whom they have suffered these things, and may recognize the causes of their devastation, they who would neither hear nor do what had been commanded in the Law. Therefore the Lord poured out upon them all his anger and an indignation full of fury, so that he who before had kept silent would no longer hold his peace, and would chastise them not with words but with punishments and torments; and a most mighty war would seize them, which they could in no way escape, showing the ferocity of the Romans. And though he has been burned on every side and has no soundness in him, yet he does not understand the cause of his punishment: that he has been punished because he did not receive the Son of God.

43:1ff.

And now thus says the Lord who creates you, Jacob, and forms you, Israel: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you, and I have called you by your name: you are mine. When you pass through the water , I will be with you, and the rivers will not cover you. When you walk into the fire, you will not be burned, and the flame will not burn in you; for I am the Lord your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior; I have given Egypt as your propitiation, Ethiopia and Saba for you. Since you have become honorable in my eyes and glorious, I have loved you, and I will give men for you, and peoples for your life. Do not fear, for I am with you; from the East I will bring your seed, and from the West I will gather you. I will say to the North: Give; and to the South: Do not hold back; bring my sons from afar, and my daughters from the end of the earth. And everyone who calls upon my name, I have created him for my glory, and I have formed him, and I have made him. Bring forth the people that is blind and has eyes, that is deaf and has ears. All the nations are gathered together, and the tribes are assembled. Who among you will declare this, and will make us hear the former things? Let them bring their witnesses and be justified, and let them hear and say: Truly you are my witnesses, says the Lord, and my servant whom I have chosen, that you may know and believe me, and understand that I myself am he. Before me no god was formed, and after me there will be none. I am, I am the Lord, and besides me there is no savior. I have declared, and I have saved; I have made it heard, and there was no stranger among you. You are my witnesses, says the Lord, and I am God, and from the beginning I myself am, and there is none who can deliver from my hand; I will work, and who will turn it back? LXX: And now thus says the Lord who made you, Jacob, and created you, Israel: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by your name, you are mine; and if you pass through water, I am with you, and the rivers will not overwhelm you; and if you pass through fire, you will not be burned; the flame will not consume you; for I am the Lord your God, the Holy One of Israel, your savior. I have made Egypt your exchange, and Ethiopia and Syene for you. Since you have become honorable, and have been glorified in my sight, I also have loved you, and I will give men for you, and princes for your head. Do not fear, for I am with you; from the East I will bring your seed, and from the West I will gather you. I will say to the North: Bring; and to the Southwest: Do not hold back; bring my sons from a far land, and my daughters from the ends of the earth, all who are called by my name; for in my glory I have created him, and I have fashioned him, and I have made him; and I have brought forth the blind people, who have eyes and are blind, and their ears are deaf. All the nations are gathered together, and their princes have assembled. Who will declare these things? or who will declare to you the things that are from the beginning? Let them bring their witnesses, and be justified, and let them hear and speak true things. Be witnesses for me, and I am a witness, says the Lord God, and my child whom I have chosen, that you may know and believe and understand that I am. Before me there was no other god, and after me there will be none. I am God, and besides me there is no Savior. I have declared, and I have saved; I have reproached, and there was no stranger among you. You are my witnesses, and I am the Lord God from the beginning, and there is none who can deliver out of my hands. I will do it, and who will turn it back? The Hebrews interpret these things of the second coming of the Savior, when, after the fullness of the nations, all Israel is to be saved. But we in no way think that the promise is made to those to whom it was said above: Who is blind but my children, and who are deaf but those who rule over them? and the servants of God have been blinded. And again: The people has been laid waste and plundered, and things like these. Finally he adds: He poured out upon him the indignation of his fury, and strong war; and he burned him round about, and he did not know it; and he set him on fire, and he did not understand. Therefore, as we said above that there are two Jacobs and two Israels, one fleshly and the other spiritual, of those who refused to believe in the Savior and of those who received the Son of God, so this too is now to be understood: that the choir of the Apostles is summoned, and the first Church of Christ gathered from the people of the Jews, to understand its Creator and Maker, who is the founder both of its soul and of its body; and not to fear persecutors, because it has been redeemed by the blood of Christ, who has called it by his name and, out of intimacy, calls it in a special way his own people; but to preach without hesitation and to dread no dangers. And what he adds, waters and rivers, and fire and flames, describes the onslaught and fury of the persecutors, who begrudge the salvation of the nations and do not want the word of the Gospel to be preached. The Jews, however, would have the Egyptians understood by the waters, the Babylonians by the rivers, the Macedonians by the fire, the Romans by the flame. And he commands them not to fear for this reason, that the Lord God, their Savior and the Holy One of Israel, is with them, who has made them preach to Egypt, Ethiopia and Syene, and to the furthest bounds of the world. For Syene the other translators put SABA (סבא), whence came the queen of the South, who came to hear the wisdom of Solomon (1 Kgs 10). Therefore the choir of the Apostles has become honorable in the sight of God and beloved by him; and the salvation of all the men and peoples who have been called through them to the Gospel will also be reckoned to the salvation of their own souls. Hence he adds and says: Do not fear, I am with you, I who say to you in the Gospel: Behold, I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the age (Matt 28:20). For from the East and from the West I will bring your sons, to rest in the bosom of Abraham; and from all parts of the world a people of my sons and daughters will be gathered, who either call upon my name or are called by my name, so that they are called Christians, to the glory of their founder. And what follows, Bring forth the people that is blind and has eyes, that is deaf and has ears, many think is said of the people of the nations, who through the teaching of the Apostles began to hear and to see. But let us understand this too of scattered Israel, which was called through the Apostles and believed first; to whom Paul also says: It was necessary that the word of God be preached first to you (Acts 13:46). And the Lord himself in the Gospel: Go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel (Matt 10:6). Then follows: All the nations are gathered together, and the tribes are assembled, that is, together with the people that believed from among the Jews, so that the calling may be twofold, of the circumcision and of the uncircumcision. And what is said, Bring forth, is a word addressed to the Son. Or, according to the Seventy, the Father speaks of the Son, that he has brought forth his blind and deaf people, and joined them to the nations, and made of them many princes of the Church. And the prophet marvels that no one among the nations could foreknow these things, nor know the counsels of God, but only his people, which had received the Law and had the prophets: For God is known in Judea; in Israel his name is great (Ps 75 [76]:1). Or else God himself is the witness and performer of his own words, and so is his child and servant whom he has chosen. There is no doubt that he means Christ, to whom he says also above: It is a great thing for you to be called my child. And all these things will take place so that the truth may be preached to the world, and that those whose mind was before brutish and senseless may know and believe and understand that besides the one God there is no other God, neither before nor after. For the founder of the times never has a beginning, since this very word, ever, belongs to time. And as he has now said, I am a witness, says the Lord God, and the child whom I have chosen, the Lord saying this same thing in the Gospel: The testimony of two men is true. I am he who bears witness of myself, and the Father who sent me (John 8:17-18), so too we must think of his divinity: that there is no God but he who speaks and his child whom he has chosen. And beautifully, besides God the Father there is no other God, because Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God (1 Cor 1), who says in the Gospel: I am in the Father, and the Father is in me (John 14:11). For as the one Lord Christ does not take from the Father his being Lord, so the one God the Father does not take from the Son his being God, he who in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God; he was in the beginning with God (John 1:1-2). And what follows, And besides me there is no Savior, shows that the Son saves all things in the Father. Of him the same prophet testifies: And the Lord will send them a Savior, who will save them (Isa 19). For God, who is wise and strong, cannot be without his own wisdom and power. Since, then, I foretold from the beginning that these things would come, there will be no one who can refuse my will, nor indeed make void what I shall have done. These things are said indeed to Jacob and Israel, but they refer to the apostolic choir and to all of the people of the Jews who have been willing to believe in Christ.

43:14

Thus says the Lord, your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: For your sake I have sent to Babylon, and I have pulled down all the bars, and the Chaldeans glorying in their ships. I am the Lord, your Holy One, the Creator, Israel, your King. LXX: Thus says the Lord God, who redeemed you, the Holy One of Israel: For your sake I will send to Babylon, and I will rouse up all the fugitives, and the Chaldeans will be bound in ships. I am the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel, who have shown Israel your king. According to the Hebrew, the prophetic word is still directed to Israel: that their redeemer, the Lord and the Holy One of Israel, has spoken these things to them: For your sake, you who preach the Gospel with me, to whom I said above, Do not fear, for I am with you, who are witnesses of my will, and who announce my child to an unbelieving world as a second witness, I have sent my Son into Babylon and the confusion of this world. And I have pulled down all its bars, which in Hebrew are called BARIHIM באריחים, and which Theodotion translated strong ones. And the Chaldeans, he says (understand ἀπὸ κοινοῦ I have pulled down), who gloried in their ships: namely those who, like ships, were tossed about among the idols. Of the Chaldeans no one doubts that they signify demons. I the Lord have foretold these things that were to come, I who am your Creator and the king of Israel. But according to the Seventy the sense is far different: I the Lord, who have delivered you from dangers, and the Holy One of Israel: for your sake I will send to Babylon the king of the Medes and Persians, and I will make its inhabitants flee; and the Chaldeans who had taken you captive will be carried in bonds across the Caspian Sea to other nations. I the Lord have decreed these things that are to come, I who have shown that Israel would be the king of believers.

43:16-17ff.

Thus says the Lord, who made a way in the sea, and a path in the rushing waters; who brought forth the chariot and the horse, the army and the strong man: together they have fallen asleep, and they will not rise again; they are crushed like flax, they are quenched. Do not remember the former things, and do not look upon the things of old. Behold, I am doing new things; now they will spring forth; surely you will know them. I will make a way in the desert, and rivers in the trackless land. The beast of the field will glorify me, the dragons and the ostriches; for I have given waters in the desert, rivers in the trackless land, to give drink to my people, my chosen one. This people I have formed for myself; they will tell my praise. LXX: For thus says the Lord, who gives a way in the sea, and a path in the mighty water; who brings forth chariots and horses and a most mighty multitude. But they have fallen asleep, and they will not rise again; they are quenched like quenched flax. Do not remember the former things, and do not consider the old things. Behold, I will do new things, which will now spring forth, and you will know them; and I will make a way in the desert, and rivers in the waterless land. The beasts of the field will bless me, the sirens and the daughters of the ostriches, for I have given water in the desert, and rivers in the waterless land, to give drink to my chosen race, my people, whom I have acquired, that it may tell of my powers. The Lord, who destroyed and cast down Babylon, and pulled down its mightiest from their power, and made captives of all the Chaldeans who were sailing prosperously on the waves of this world, he himself found a way in the rushing waters of the Red Sea, so that his people, freed from Egypt, might pass over. Or, he who made a way in the Red Sea, he himself also found a path in the rushing waters of the river Jordan, so that both the going out from Egypt and the entrance into the land of promise might have a miracle. He sank into the deep the chariots and horses and the whole army of Pharaoh, who fell asleep in perpetual sleep. They were crushed and quenched like flax, in a brief space of time, in a point and a moment. For flax, not yet caught by the fire, is at once quenched because of the lightness of its substance, and dissolves into ash. Therefore I command you this: that among my signs and wonders, by which Babylon, the mightiest city, was overthrown, and by which a way was opened for my people in the Red Sea and in the Jordan, you should in no way remember the old things, since in the Gospel I am going to do far greater things, in comparison with which past things ought to be passed over in silence. For no longer will I find a way in the Red Sea, but in the desert of the whole world. Nor will one river or fountain burst forth from the rock, but many rivers, to refresh not bodies, as before, but thirsting souls; and that will be fulfilled which we read above: You will drink waters from the fountains of the Savior (cf. Isa 12:3). Then what never was done will be done: all the beasts and dragons and ostriches that dwelt in the wilderness of the nations, and were like beasts in the blood of idolatry and the savagery of their manners, will glorify me and praise me together. For dragons, which Theodotion alone, as it is written in the Hebrew, called THANNIM (תנים), the others translated Sirens: monstrous creatures which by their sweet and deadly song cast sailors headlong to be torn apart by Scylla's dogs. And this signifies that those who were formerly given over to pleasure and luxury are turned to the service of the Lord; although it is better to understand dragons, since ostriches are joined to them, so that, since he was speaking once of the beasts of the wilderness, he set down these animals, which are at home in the desert. They will praise me, he says, and will glorify me, the beasts of the field, and the dragons, and the ostriches, because I have given waters in the desert of the nations, and rivers in the dryness of the peoples, so that my people might drink, which I have chosen for myself, or my chosen race, and the people which I have acquired with my blood, that it might tell my praises and my powers.

43:22-23ff.

You have not called upon me, Jacob, nor have you labored in me, Israel. You have not offered me the ram of your burnt offering, and with your victims you have not glorified me. I have not made you serve with offering, nor have I given you labor with incense. You have not bought me sweet cane with silver, and with the fat of your victims you have not made me drunk. But you have made me serve in your sins; you have given me labor in your iniquities. LXX: Not now have I called you, Jacob, nor have I made you labor, Israel. You have not brought me the sheep of your burnt offering, nor have you magnified me with your victims; nor have I made you serve with sacrifices, nor have I given you labor with incense; nor have you bought me incense with silver, nor have I desired the fat of your sacrifices; but in your sins I have defended you, and in your iniquities. While the beasts of the field, the dragons and the ostriches, praise me, you, Jacob, in no way wished to call upon me, nor afterward to labor so as to amend your sin by repentance. And as for your thinking that you have offered me victims and sacrificed rams, know that they were not accepted by me, because they were shared by me and the idols. And he repeats that sense of which he had spoken above: To what purpose is the multitude of your victims to me, says the Lord? I am full of the burnt offering of rams, and of the fat of lambs, and the blood of bulls and goats I do not want. For I have not, he says, required anything precious from you, so as to make you labor in preparing it. I have not exacted offerings from you, nor sought frankincense, nor sweet cane, nor incense and spices of various kinds, with whose smoke you might make me drunk and sate me. But obedience, which is above sacrifice, and the sacrifice of which David says in the Psalms, A sacrifice to God is a troubled spirit; a contrite and humbled heart God does not despise (Ps 50 [51]:19): these I wanted, these I sought. But you have made me serve and labor in your sins, so that I was compelled to say: I have labored in bearing; and I can no longer bear you. Hence God says the same thing also through Hosea: What shall I do to you, Ephraim? Shall I protect you, Israel (Hos 11:8)? What shall I do to you? Shall I make you like Admah, and like Zeboiim? But what the Seventy set down, but in your sins I have defended you, and in your iniquities, can be joined to what precedes thus: that it is God's labor and weariness to defend sinners.

43:25-26ff.

I am, I am he who blots out your iniquities for my own sake, and I will not remember your sins. Put me in remembrance, that we may be judged together; tell, if you have anything, that you may be justified. Your first father sinned, and your interpreters have transgressed against me. And I have defiled the holy princes; I have given Jacob to slaughter, and Israel to blasphemy. LXX: I am, I am he who blots out your iniquities, and I will not remember them. But you, remember, and let us be judged. Tell your iniquities first, that you may be justified. Your fathers sinned, and your princes have acted unjustly against me, and the princes have defiled my holy things. And I have given Jacob up to destruction, and Israel to reproach. You, he says, Jacob and Israel, have made me labor in your sins, and I could scarcely carry the burdens of your iniquities; you whom I in no way call my servants or my children, but address by the bare names of Jacob and Israel, so as to expose and reprove you as sinners. But I, for my own sake, because I am merciful and patient and of many mercies, will blot out all your iniquities in the sprinkling and the blood of the new Testament; I will blot out the old bond that was written against you; and I will no longer remember your sins, which, if you are willing to believe, I am going to forgive you in baptism. Put me, then, in remembrance: if you have anything righteous to answer me, I will gladly receive it, that we may be judged together, and you may convict me of not having done for you what I ought to have done. This sense we read more fully in Micah: My people, what have I done to you, and in what have I troubled you? Answer me: for I brought you up out of the land of Egypt, and freed you from the house of bondage, and sent before your face Moses and Aaron and Miriam. And in the fiftieth Psalm David says to God: That you may be justified in your words, and may prevail when you are judged (Ps 50 [51]:5). Tell, then, if you have anything, that you may be justified. And the sense is: I will not speak first against you, lest you say you have been overwhelmed by a multitude of words; but if you have anything righteous, speak for yourself, so that you may be seen to endure undeservedly the things you suffer. And that you may know that I have mercy on you not for your merit but for my own clemency, I will go back to your fathers and forebears, so that you may understand that you were begotten of sinners: Your first father sinned in the wilderness, namely the whole people of Israel. Or else the author of your race, Abraham, is convicted of having sinned when, as the Lord promised the land of promise to his seed, he answered: Whereby shall I know that I shall possess it? And your interpreters, he says, have transgressed against me (Gen 15:8): Aaron and Moses at the water of contradiction, who spoke as mediators between me and you (Exod 17). And that we may understand that this is not a forced exposition, there follows: And I have defiled the holy princes, of whom it is also sung in the psalm: Their judges have been swallowed up beside the rock (Ps 140 [141]:6). These he says he has defiled for this reason, that they did not enter the land of promise. And I have given Jacob to slaughter, and Israel to blasphemy, so that none of those who had come out of Egypt, except two, entered Judea, but their carcasses lay in the wilderness. According to the Seventy, who added on their own, Tell your iniquities first, that you may be justified, God calls them to repentance, so that they may understand their crimes and sins and obtain pardon. For it is written also in another place: The righteous man is his own accuser at the beginning of his speech (Prov 18:17). And their princes and fathers are said to have violated the holy things of the Lord, not serving the Law of God, but seeking the traditions and commandments of men; on account of whom Jacob perished, and Israel was given to reproach, cast out of his own province, an exile and a stranger throughout the whole world.

44:1f.

And now hear, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen. Thus says the Lord, who makes you and forms you from the womb, your helper: Do not fear, my servant Jacob, and you, Most Upright, whom I have chosen. For I will pour out waters upon the thirsty, and streams upon the dry ground; I will pour out my spirit upon your seed, and my blessing upon your offspring. And they will spring up among the grass, like willows beside flowing waters. This one will say, I am the Lord's; and that one will call in the name of Jacob; and this one will write with his hand, To the Lord; and he will be likened in the name of Israel. LXX: But now hear, Jacob my child, and Israel whom I have chosen. I am the Lord God, who made you and fashioned you from the womb; you will yet have help. Do not fear, my child Jacob, and beloved Israel whom I have chosen; yet I will give water in thirst to those who walk in the waterless land; I will put my spirit upon your seed, and my blessings upon your sons. And they will spring up like grass in the midst of water, and like the willow beside flowing waters. This one will say, I am God's; this one will cry out in the name of Jacob. And another will write on his hand, I am God's, and will cry out in the name of Israel. Where the people of the Jews is accused for its unbelief and blasphemy, it is called by the bare words, without any dignity of name: You have not called upon me, Jacob, nor have you labored in me, Israel; and again: I have given Jacob to slaughter, and Israel to blasphemy (above, Isa 43:22, 28). But where he speaks to the choir of the Apostles, which is from the Jews, the privileges of names are also added: Hear, Jacob my servant, and Israel whom I have chosen: so that servitude comes first, election second. Thus says the Lord, your maker and former, who helped you from the womb (Gen 25), so that while still in your mother's womb you seized your brother's heel; or who at the beginning of the newborn Church preserved you from the persecutors. Do not fear their cruelty, Jacob my servant, and Most Upright, whom I have chosen. He calls Israel by another name; for the Hebrew word ISURUN (ישרון) the others translated εὐθύτατον, or εὐθῆ, that is, most upright and upright; the Seventy alone most beloved, adding Israel of their own. For properly, according to the Hebrews and the faithfulness of the letters, ISRAEL (ישראל) means upright of God; whereas a man seeing God lies not in the letters but in the sound of the word. Hence also the book of Genesis is called εὐθεῖς, that is, of the righteous: Abraham, Isaac and Israel. Do not fear, then, Jacob and Israel, because I will pour out waters upon the thirsty and the dry ground, of which it has often been said: And I will pour out, or I will put my spirit upon your seed, and my blessing upon your offspring, which will be born again of water and the Holy Spirit in baptism. This the Savior also promised in the Gospel, saying: If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink. And at once it is added: But this he said of the Holy Spirit, whom those who believed were to receive (John 7). He also compares those who are born again in baptism to green grass, and to the willow which springs up beside flowing waters and, against the nature of things, bears fruit, though before it was barren, or rather its seed, taken as food, makes people barren. This indeed is read in the first psalm: And he will be like a tree which is planted by the streams of waters, which will give its fruit in its season, and its leaf will not fall. Others understand by the grass and the willows springing up anew a twofold calling: so that the people of the nations is in the grass, and in the willows those of Israel who believed. And at the same time he describes the variety of believers: One will say, I am the Lord's, he who trusts that the works of righteousness are in him; another will call (understand: sinners to repentance) in the name of Jacob, so that they too may supplant vices and sins. Another will write with his hand, I am God's; or, as the Seventy translated, he will write on his hand, I am God's, so that he glories in being a soldier in the new service of Christ's warfare. And he will be likened in the name of Israel. For not all from Israel, but a great part from the multitude of the nations will be likened in the name of Israel, so as to receive the Law and the Prophets and all the graces of the Holy Spirit which were promised to the people of Israel.

44:6ff.

Thus says the Lord, the King of Israel, and his redeemer, the Lord of hosts: I am the first and I am the last, and besides me there is no God. Who is like me? Let him call and declare, and set out the order for me, since I established the ancient people; let them declare to them the things to come and the things that shall be. Do not fear, nor be troubled: from that time I have made you hear, and I have declared; you are my witnesses. Is there a God besides me, and a former whom I have not known? The makers of an idol are all nothing, and their most beloved things will not profit them. They themselves are their witnesses, that they do not see nor understand, so that they may be confounded. Who has formed a god, and cast a graven image that is profitable for nothing? Behold, all its partners will be confounded; for the craftsmen are of men; they will all assemble, they will stand, and they will be afraid, and they will be confounded together. The ironsmith has worked with the file; with coals and with hammers he has formed it, and he has worked with the arm of his strength. He will hunger and faint, he will not drink water, and he will grow weary. The carpenter has stretched out the rule he has formed it with the plane; he has made it with the corner tools, and turned it with the compass; and he has made the image of a man, like a handsome man dwelling in a house. He cut down cedars, he took the holm oak and the oak that had stood among the trees of the forest. He planted a pine, which the rain nourished; and it became fuel for men; he took from them and was warmed; he kindled it and baked bread. But of the rest he has made a god, and has worshiped it; he has made a graven image, and has bowed down before it. Half of it he burned in the fire, and on half of it he ate flesh. He cooked a stew and was filled, and was warmed, and said: Aha! I am warm, I have seen the fire. But the rest of it he made into a god and a graven image for himself; he bows down before it and worships it, and prays to it, saying: Deliver me, for you are my god. They have not known, nor understood; for they have forgotten, so that their eyes may not see, so that they may not understand with their heart. They do not consider in their mind, nor know, nor perceive, so as to say: Half of it I burned in the fire, and on its coals I baked bread; I cooked flesh and ate, and of the rest of it shall I make an idol? Shall I fall down before the trunk of a tree? Part of it is ash; a foolish heart has worshiped it; and he has not delivered his soul, nor will he say: Perhaps there is a lie in my right hand. After the preaching of the Apostles, the calling of the nations, the coming of the Savior, and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, whom he promised he would give to all believers, when, according to the variety of their merits, one will say, I am the Lord's; another will call in the name of Jacob; another will write with his hand that he is the Lord's, and, though sprung from the unbelieving crowd of the Gentiles, will be likened in the name of Israel, so that, forsaking idols, he may be a worshiper of the one God, another περικοπὴ begins, which we have set out whole at once, so as not to divide the continuity of a single sense. And because the Seventy in this passage, except for a few words, do not differ from the Hebrew, we have been content with our own edition, and when it has been understood, the others too will be known. The discourse is against the idolaters of that time when the prophet Isaiah was announcing things to come to the peoples, and it reproves those who, despising the religion of Almighty God, bow down to wooden images and worship the works of their own hands. Let us run through it, then, point by point. Thus says the Lord, the King of Israel, which is to believe in me, and his redeemer, which will receive the coming of my Son: the Lord of hosts, and of powers, and the Almighty. For this is what SABAOTH (צבאות) means in Hebrew. I am the first, and I am the last, I am the Α and the Ω; and besides me there is no God, because the child whom I have chosen is God in me. Of him I said above: Behold my child, whom I have chosen; my chosen one, whom my soul has received; he will bring forth judgment to the nations; and in his name the nations will hope. Nor does he say that he is alone, but that besides his own power and wisdom there is no outside God; and condemning the opinion of many gods, and images, he says: Who, he says, is like me? Let him call the things that are not as though they were, and set out the order of my creation, I who have balanced all things by reason, since I made man upon the earth. Nor do I want this only, but I also ask for knowledge of things to come. Hence you, Israel, whose king and redeemer I am, do not fear the images, which you learned on Mount Sinai are nothing. Or is there perhaps another Creator, whom I have not known? Or besides this is there another world, to show the power of an unknown God? And not only the things that are made, but those also who make them, will be held as nothing. And when the time of vengeance has come, the works of their hands will in no way be able to free them; blind and senseless, they confound their own craftsmen. For who could believe that a god is formed by adze, file and auger and hammer? And that images are either cast in the coals, or by rule, plane and corner tools and compass suddenly rise up into gods? Especially since the cheapness of the art is shown by the hunger and thirst of the craftsman. For a wooden statue is made, expressing the human form, and the more beautiful it is, the more august a god it is thought. It is set in a shrine and shut up in an eternal prison, the thing that grew for a long time in the forests and, according to the variety of trees, was a cedar or a holm oak or an oak or a pine. And in a wondrous manner its chips and shavings are thrown into the fire to warm the god's craftsman and to cook various stews; but the other part is formed into a god, so that, when the work is finished, its maker may worship it and invoke the help of his own work. Nor does he understand or consider, nay, he does not see with the eyes either of the flesh or of the mind, that that cannot be God of which a part has been burned in the fire, nor can the divine majesty be made by the hand of a man. And the prophetic discourse on the mockery of idols is woven more fully, but these things are easy to understand and do not call for a long-winded, nay, a superfluous exposition. On this Flaccus too writes in a Satire, deriding the images of the nations (Satires, book 1, 8): Once I was a fig-tree trunk, a useless log, when the craftsman, uncertain whether to make a stool or a Priapus, preferred that I be a god: thence I am a god, of thieves and birds the greatest terror. . . . . . . . . . . . . And whatever has been said of idols can be referred also to the chiefs of the heresies, who with a crafty heart put together the images of their doctrines and lies, and venerate what they know to have been feigned by themselves. Nor is their own error enough for them, unless they have deceived all the simple into worshiping them. They think gain to be godliness, and devour the houses of widows (1 Tim 6), and, abusing the ignorance of the common people, with the art of dialectic, as with adze and auger, file and plane, they form their god, and forge it with the hammer, and gild it with the charm of rhetorical speech: whose god is the belly, and whose glory is in their shame (Phil 3).

44:21ff.

Remember these things, Jacob and Israel, for you are my servant; I have formed you, you are my servant, Israel; do not forget me. I have blotted out your iniquities like a cloud, and your sins like a mist. Return to me, for I have redeemed you. Praise, O heavens, for the Lord has done it; shout for joy, you ends of the earth; resound with praise, you mountains, you forest and every tree in it; for the Lord has redeemed Jacob, and Israel will glory. LXX: Remember these things, Jacob and Israel, for you are my child; I have formed you as my child; and you, Israel, do not forget me. For behold, I have blotted out your iniquities like a cloud, and your sins like darkness. Return to me, and I will redeem you. Rejoice, O heavens, for God has had mercy on Israel. Sound the trumpet, you foundations of the earth; cry out with gladness, you mountains, you hills and all the trees that are in them; for God has redeemed Jacob, and Israel will be glorious. Since these things are so, and you know that idols are figments of men, O Jacob, and Israel my child, do not forget your Creator, nor do yourself the injury of bowing down to the work of your own hands. And since these are to be utterly destroyed at the coming of my child whom I have chosen, therefore know with all the eagerness of your mind that, as a cloud and darkness and mist is either dissolved by the heat of the sun or thinned out by a sweeping wind, so I will cause your iniquities to be dissolved, and all the sins with which you had before offended me. Only return to me and do penance, for you are to be redeemed with precious blood. If you do this, know that heaven and earth rejoice in your salvation, and all the elements sing together; or the angels who dwell in heaven, and the other powers by which the foundations of the earth are borne; or certainly the Apostles and Prophets, of whom the Apostle also spoke: Built upon the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets (Eph 2:20). The mountains also and the forests, or the hills, which, according to the variety of their virtues, have held the first, the middle and the last places, are bidden to shout for joy and to sound the trumpet, knowing that the Lord has redeemed Jacob, and that he rejoices in the conversion of Israel; or that Israel himself, turned from error, becomes glorious.

44:24ff.

Thus says the Lord, your redeemer, and your former from the womb: I am the Lord who makes all things, who alone stretches out the heavens, who establishes the earth, and there is none with me; who makes void the signs of the diviners, and turns the soothsayers to madness; who turns the wise backward, and makes their knowledge foolish; who raises up the word of his servant, and fulfills the counsel of his messengers; who say to Jerusalem: You will be inhabited , and to the cities of Judah: You will be built, and I will raise up its deserts; who say to the deep: Be desolate, and I will dry up your rivers; who say to Cyrus: You are my shepherd, and you will fulfill all my will; who say to Jerusalem: You will be built; and to the temple: You will be founded. LXX: Thus says the Lord who redeemed you, and who forms you from the womb: I am the Lord who accomplish all things; I alone stretched out the heaven, and made firm the earth. Who else has scattered the signs of the pythons, and divinations from the heart? I who turn the prudent backward, and make their counsel foolish; and I establish the word of my child, and prove true the counsel of his angels; who say to Jerusalem: You will be inhabited; and to the cities of Judah: You will be built, and its deserts will spring up; who say to the abyss: You will be made desolate, and I will dry up your rivers; who say to Cyrus that he should be wise, and do all my wishes; who say to Jerusalem: You will be built; and I will lay the foundations of my holy house. When the idols and the iniquities of Israel have been destroyed and its sins blotted out, when the whole creation will rejoice together, and, according to the faith of the Gospel (Luke 15), the angels in heaven will rejoice over the repentance of sinners, the power of God is described: that it is in no way a great thing for him to redeem Jacob and to restore an upright heart in Israel, whom he formed from the womb. And if this should seem no small thing to anyone, let it not be difficult for him who alone stretched out the heavens; according to what is read elsewhere: Who stretches out the heaven like a skin (Ps 103 [104]:2). Not that the Son is excluded from the stretching out of the heavens, For all things were made through him, and without him nothing was made that was made (John 1:3); but that, as we have often said, the idols are excluded by this sentence. For in the Proverbs of Solomon too it is said in the person of Christ, the power of God and the wisdom of God: When he was preparing the heaven, I was with him (Prov 8:27). For he spoke, and they were made; he commanded, and they were created (Ps 148; Ps 32 [33]:9); and: By the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and all their power by the spirit of his mouth (Ps 32 [33]:6). We press these points frequently, so that no occasion may be left to the heretics for blaspheming Christ. In the establishing of the earth too, when he was making its foundations solid, there was no one with God except him who was in him. He, then, being so great and such, when the time of the foreordained mystery has come, that all idols may be destroyed and the knowledge of God alone may be preached in the world, will destroy and overturn all the prophecies of the diviners, and the signs and portents of the pythons and soothsayers, by which they have deceived the human race; and he will show to be foolish the wisdom of the philosophers, which itself also is the greatest part of error, since by human thoughts they are in no way shown to have comprehended the wisdom of God. He will also fulfill in deed the word of his child, or servant, of whom we spoke above, and the counsel of his messengers, namely of the Apostles and all the teachers, who will announce the will of their master to the nations. He, then, who is to do such great things, whose power I have described in a brief discourse, now says also to Jerusalem, which was to be destroyed by the Babylonians, before it is destroyed, that it will again be inhabited by peoples; and to the cities of Judea, that they will be restored; he who will also raise up its solitudes, so that all may be filled with inhabitants. He, then, who says to Jerusalem and to Judea and its deserts that it will be inhabited and built and raised up, says to the deep or abyss, that is, to Babylon, Be desolate, and I will dry up your rivers, all the power of its kings. Or, because he had spoken of the deep and the abyss, rightly by metaphor he set down rivers too, of which the Psalmist also sings: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept (Ps 136 [137]:1).
