Of this Peter too spoke to Simon: For I see that you are in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity (Acts 8:23). And Paul grieved, seeing the city of the Athenians bound to idolatry. For each one is bound fast by the cords of his own sins (Prov 5). For these bonds of the soul David too prayed in the psalm: Cleanse me, Lord, from my hidden sins, and from those of others spare your servant (Ps 18 [19]:13). It is hard to find one who is not bound by these chains. Rarely is a soul found that does not have this most heavy collar put around its neck, weighing it down to earthly works, so that it looks not to heaven but to the earth. This is related of the woman in the Gospel too, whom Satan had bound for eighteen years, so that, bent over, she could not see the things of heaven (Luke 13). If, then, he says, you take this chain out of the midst of your heart, and scatter bonds of this kind, and the χειροτονίαν, for which the three other translators with one voice translated the outstretched finger, so that not only do you not think evil yourself and not do it, but you do not even disparage your neighbor and point out each person as if with your finger, and speak what does not profit your soul, considering not your own evils but the errors of others: then you will receive what the following discourse adds. Very many of our writers understand χειροτονίαν, that is, the ordination of clerics, which is accomplished not only by the invocation of the voice but by the imposition of the hand (lest, namely, as we have laughed to see in some places, a clandestine invocation of the voice should ordain clerics without their knowing it), in such a way as to take up the testimony of Paul writing to Timothy: Lay hands hastily on no one, and do not share in the sins of others (1 Tim 5:22). For it is no light sin to cast pearls before swine and to give what is holy to dogs (Matt 7), and to bestow ordination to the clergy not on the holy and those most learned in the law of God, but on one's own hangers-on and on the ministers of base services, and, what is more disgraceful than these, at the prayers of silly women. Here we must consider the wisdom of the Apostle, in whom Christ was speaking, who, to show the danger of ordination, joined to it the torments of those who sin: And do not share in the sins of others. As, then, in the ordination of wicked men he who appoints such men is a partaker of their sins, so in the ordination of saints he who chose good men is a partaker of their righteousness. It follows: And the word of murmuring, understood ἀπὸ κοινοῦ: if you take it away from you. Now the word of murmuring is when God speaks against us, Let the murmuring of this people cease from me, and it shall not die; and we refer our sins to God, to make excuses in sins, and say: The heat of the body overcame me, the incitements of youth conquered me, I was created such by God, poverty forced me to theft. So if we do not do the things that have been said, and do the things that are to be said, so as to give to the hungry not, as above, our bread, but our soul, so as to help him in whatever ways we can, and to give not as if out of sadness and necessity but from the soul, receiving rather than giving a benefit, for God loves a cheerful giver (2 Cor 9:7); so as not to refresh the hungry or afflicted soul in part but to satisfy it, and to grieve with those who grieve and mourn with those who mourn (Rom 12): then our light will rise in the darkness, he who says: I have come as light into the world, so that everyone who believes in me may not remain in darkness, but may have the light of life (John 12:46). For the lamp of our body is the eye: if it is single, our whole body will be full of light. But if what ought to be light has been turned into darkness, then the whole body will be dark, and it will be said to us: If the light that is in you is darkness, how great is that darkness itself! (Matt 6:23). Let us consider by what great virtues we may come to the light of God, so that the darkness may be turned into noonday, and we may say with the bride: Where do you pasture, where do you lie down, at noonday? (Song 1:6).

58:11

And the Lord will give you rest always, and will fill your soul with splendors, and will deliver your bones. And you shall be like a watered garden, and like a fountain of waters whose waters shall not fail. LXX: And your God shall be with you always, and you shall be filled as your soul desires, and your bones shall grow fat. And they shall be like a drunken garden, and like a fountain for which the water shall not fail. What has been added in the Alexandrian copies at the beginning of this chapter, And still my praise shall be in you always, and at the end, and your bones shall spring up like grass, and shall grow fat, and they shall possess by inheritance unto generation and generations, is not found in the Hebrew, nor even in the corrected and true copies of the Seventy; hence it must be marked beforehand with an obelus. When the darkness, he says, of your breast has been dissolved by the rising of the light, and noonday has arisen in place of a palpable night, then you will always have God dwelling in you, to fill your soul with splendors. Of these we read in the psalm: With you is the principality in the day of your power, in the splendors of the saints; from the womb before the daystar I have begotten you (Ps 109 [110]:3). Or: you will be satisfied with all that your soul desires, because you yourself have satisfied the hungry soul, and you will be able to say: Bless the Lord, O my soul, who fills your desire with good things (Ps 102 [103]:5); and your bones will be delivered from destruction and from everlasting fire. Or: they will grow fat, so as to recover their former stoutness, having been wasted by the famine of the word of the Lord. This indeed we can understand according to the letter of the resurrection of the bodies which are to fall, and also of the virtues of the soul, which the saint signifies when he says in the psalm: All my bones shall say, Lord, who is like you? (Ps 34 [35]:10). Of these it is also written in Proverbs: A good report makes the bones fat (Prov 15:30). And to those to whom rewards are promised: There shall be health for your body, and healing for your bones (Prov 16:24). Of these again it is written: The Lord keeps all their bones; not one of them shall be broken (Ps 33 [34]:21). On the contrary, he who is a sinner, and has lost the strength and virtue of the soul, laments and says: Our bones are scattered beside hell (Ps 140 [141]:7). For we cannot believe that the bones of sinners are not in hell but beside hell. And a good report makes the bones fat (Prov 15:30), which has nothing to do with the fattening of the body. It follows: And you shall be, or it shall be, that is, either you or your soul, like a watered garden; of which it is written: A fountain went forth and watered the whole face of paradise (Gen 2:6), where in the Hebrew garden is read. This fountain we can call no other than him to whom it is said, With you is the fountain of life (Ps 35 [36]:10), who unceasingly waters his Church and the hearts of all believers.

58:12

And the deserts of ages shall be built up in you; you shall raise up the foundations of generation and generation; and there shall be called in you the builder of hedges, turning the paths into rest. LXX: And the places desert from of old shall be built up for you, and your foundations shall be everlasting for generations and generations; and you shall be called the builder of the wall, and you shall make the paths in the midst to rest. Not only, he says, will your light rise in the darkness, and your darkness be like noonday, and the Lord give you rest always, and you be like a watered garden, and the rest, but there shall be built up in you the things that had been desert for a long time; and the foundations of your dwellings will be laid to endure through many generations; so that either you yourself will be called the builder of hedges and walls, or one will arise in you who will be the builder of hedges and will turn the paths into rest, or, according to the Seventy, will make the tracks in the midst to rest. The Jews, and the friends only of the letter that kills, refer these things to the restoration of the cities of Palestine; and they contend either that they were done under Zerubbabel and Ezra and Nehemiah, or that they will be in the last time: that for the restoration of Jerusalem and of the cities round about, very deep foundations are to be laid, and walls built so high that none of the enemy can enter, and the entry of all foes into them is barred. But we, following the order of the explanation we have begun, say that the things that had been desert among the Jews are built up in the Church, not for a short time but for ever, and that its foundations are to be raised up from both peoples, that is, in two generations. Hence the Apostle said: As a wise architect I have laid the foundation; another builds upon it; but let each one see what he builds upon it (1 Cor 3:10); and in another place: We are God's husbandry, God's building; and again: Built upon the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets (Eph 2:20); and that she, or he who was born in her, is to be called the builder of hedges. Of him we read in the psalm: A man was born in her, and the Most High himself has founded her (Ps 86 [87]:5). These hedges and walls (for this is what φραγμοῦς signifies in the Greek tongue) Scripture records as being set around a field and vineyards: You brought a vine out of Egypt; you cast out the nations and planted it; and a little after: Why have you broken down its wall, and all who pass by the way gather its vintage? (Ps 79 [80]:9 and 13). And in this same Prophet: A vineyard was made for the beloved; describing it in beautiful language, he adds: I built a tower and surrounded it with a wall (Eccl 2:4). Whoever breaks it down, according to Ecclesiastes, a serpent will bite him. It was surrounded for this purpose, that the approach of all beasts into the vineyard of God might be barred. This is the crooked serpent who deceived Eve in paradise; because she had broken down the precepts of God, she was therefore open to his bites, and heard from the Lord: You shall watch for his head, and he shall watch for your heel (Gen 3:15). In the place where we, lest we seem to innovate in anything, interpreted according to the Seventy, because the testimony is widely known, and you shall be called the builder of hedges, in the Hebrew is read and there shall be called in you GODER PHERES גדר פרץ, which Aquila interpreted περιφράκτης διακοπῆς, which we can render according to the sense as one who sets himself against the raging anger of God. Indeed, Symmachus translated setting a wall against the one who strikes (1 Sam 7), such as were Moses and Aaron and Samuel, who withstood the anger of the Lord and, as though by building a wall, set a limit to his indignation. This is also said to Jeremiah: that he should not run to meet the Lord, nor wish to resist his anger, and so shut off his indignation by prayers as by a kind of wall (Jer 7); and to Moses, as though the Lord were being held back by him: Let me go, he says, and I will strike this people (Exod 32:10). A builder, then, of walls, ramparts and hedges of this kind will turn the paths into rest, so that the wrath of God may by no means rage, but the Lord may be appeased toward them, and all the paths of indignation may come to rest.

58:13

If you turn away your foot from the sabbath, from doing your own will on my holy day, and call the sabbath delightful, and the holy of the Lord glorious, and glorify him while you do not make your own ways, and your own will is not found to speak a word. LXX: If you turn away your foot on the sabbaths, so as not to do your own wills on the holy day; and you shall call the sabbaths delightful, holy to the Lord; you shall not lift your foot to work, nor speak a word ÷ in anger from your mouth ⁚. To the one to whom he had said above, Is not this rather the fast that I have chosen: loose the bond of impiety, undo the bundles that weigh down, and the rest, he now too promises rewards, if he is willing to do the things that follow (Exod 20): namely, that he restrain his foot on the sabbaths, and not do his own wills, nor stain the holy day of the Lord with his wills. It is commanded in the Law that on the sabbaths we should do no servile work, kindle no fire, sit in one place, and do only those works that belong to the salvation of the soul. If we take this according to the letter, it cannot be fulfilled at all. For who can do this: sitting the whole day and night on the sabbath, not go away from one place, or rather not even move slightly, since if he did he would be a transgressor of the law? From one commandment, then, which is impossible according to the letter, we are compelled to understand the rest spiritually as well: that we should not do servile work and lose the freedom of the soul, for he who commits sin is the slave of sin (John 8); that we should not carry a burden on the sabbath, such as he carried who says: My iniquities have gone up over my head; like a heavy burden they have weighed heavily upon me (Ps 37 [38]:5); that the iniquity which sits upon the talent of lead should have no power in us; that the pleasure and lust of the body should not set us on fire (Zech 5), for all adulterers, their hearts are like an oven (Hos 7); and the fiery darts of the devil are there to shoot in the dark at the upright of heart (Ps 10 [11]). We are commanded too that, having taken hold of the plow, we should not look behind us; that, having climbed to the height of the roofs, we should by no means wish to come down to take the garments of the world (Luke 9); but that we should hear with Moses, But you, stand here with me (Exod 34:2); and sit with the Lord, weary on the way of this world, at the well of the Samaritan woman, thirsting for the conversion and salvation of those who stray (John 4); that we should hear the Apostle warning, Be firm and immovable (1 Cor 15:58), lest we suffer what Judas the traitor suffered, who lost the place of his ministry and became a transgressor; and let us always remember that sentence: If the spirit of him who has power rises up against you, do not leave your place (Eccl 10:4). He who rests thus on the sabbath washes his hands among the innocent, and does not move his feet to do his own wills: he keeps the delightful sabbaths of the Lord. This sabbath rest, according to the Epistle written to the Hebrews, is promised to us in the heavens, and glory is prepared (Heb 4): so long as we do not make our own ways on the sabbath, nor is our own will found, to speak a word; that is, that we sin neither in deed nor in word. Otherwise, if these things are forbidden only on the sabbath, then on the other six days freedom to sin is granted us. And since it is foolish to believe this, it remains that the sabbath, which means rest, must be sanctified by the faithful at all times, while they do the wills not of the flesh but of the soul. What is added according to the Seventy, in anger from your mouth, is not found in the Hebrew. To this sabbath, to be celebrated with all festivity, the Savior calls us in the Gospel, saying: Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened, and I will give you rest (Matt 11:28); for this is what ἀναπαύσω ὑμᾶς signifies: that, laying down the burdens of sins, we may keep sabbath in Christ and say: He has set my feet upon a rock (Ps 39 [40]:3), and may avoid what the saint says he almost suffered: But my feet were almost moved (Ps 72 [73]:2).

58:14

Then you shall delight upon the Lord, and I will lift you up above the heights of the earth, and I will feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father. For the mouth of the Lord has spoken. LXX: And you shall be confident upon the Lord, and he will lift you up above the good things of the earth, and he will feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father. For the mouth of the Lord has spoken. When you have called the sabbaths delightful, and have not moved your foot on the sabbath to do servile work, nor spoken a word, that is, have always kept silent and fulfilled what is commanded, Keep your tongue from evil, and let your lips speak no deceit (Ps 33 [34]:14), then you will delight in the Lord, and will see fulfilled in yourself: Delight in the Lord, and he will give you the petitions of your heart (Ps 36 [37]:4). Or: you will have confidence in the Lord, according to what is written: He who trusts in the Lord is blessed; and in Jeremiah: Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord, and the Lord shall be his hope (Jer 17:7); and elsewhere: It is good to trust in the Lord rather than to trust in man (Ps 117 [118]:8). And the Lord will lift you up and raise you above the heights and good things of the earth. For the land of the meek and the land of the living is not below but above. Thus it is said to Lot as he fled from the valley of Sodom and Gomorrah: Save yourself on the mountain (Gen 19); and after he had reached it, the sun rose for him in Zoar. Of this land the Lord said: Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the land (Matt 5:4); and many other things which we have often used, among which is this: Honor your father and your mother, and you shall be long-lived upon the land which the Lord your God will give you (Exod 20:12). According to the letter this cannot stand at all; for many honor their parents and die soon, and other men, parricides, live a long time. But so that we may know more surely that this land is in the heights, let us briefly recall the thirty-sixth psalm, in which it is written: The meek shall possess the land, and shall feast in the abundance of peace. After this it adds: Wait for the Lord and keep his ways, and he will lift you up to possess the land (Ps 36 [37]:11); of which it is sung in another place: The righteous shall possess the land, and shall dwell upon it for ever and ever (ibid., 34). This too is impossible: for if the earth shall pass away, this one certainly which we inhabit, how shall the righteous dwell upon it for ever and ever? From this we learn that there is a land which is set in the heights. After this it adds: And I will feed you, or the Lord will feed you, with the inheritance of Jacob your father. For as he who has the faith of Abraham is called a son of Abraham, so he who supplants vices and sins is called a son of Jacob; and whose virtue anyone imitates, his son he is also called. The good things of the land set in the heights, with which the son of Jacob is satisfied, must be taken as those which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor have they entered into the heart of man (1 Cor 2). Of them it is written in the Epistle to the Hebrews: For those who say these things show that they seek a homeland; and if indeed they were seeking that from which they had come out, they had time to return to it. But now they desire a better homeland, that is, the heavenly Jerusalem (Heb 11:14ff.). From this we learn that the fable of the thousand years, in which marriages are promised again, and foods, and the conduct of an earthly life, is to be rejected. For if in the resurrection they will neither marry nor be given in marriage, but will be like the Angels, because they are sons of the resurrection (Matt 22); and the Apostle speaks of the belly and foods: Food for the belly, and the belly for foods; but God will destroy both the one and the other (1 Cor 6:13): how shall we seek again, in an incorrupt, spiritual and immortal body, the vices of our former mortal and corrupt flesh? And we say this not as denying the substance of the glorified body, but as taking away entirely the former works in those who are like the Angels. Otherwise, even in this body of ours we imitate the angelic virtues by fasts and continence and perpetual chastity and charity, and yet we do not lose the substance of our bodies. That we may believe all these things to be future, let us know that they have been promised by God, whose mouth has spoken; so that, as in the hands we understand work, and in the feet walking, and in the belly generation, and in the ears and eyes hearing and sight, so in the mouth we may understand the speech of God.

59:1-2

Behold, the hand of the Lord is not shortened, that it cannot save, nor is his ear made heavy, that it cannot hear; but your iniquities have divided between you and your God, and your sins have hidden his face from you, so that he would not hear. LXX: Is the hand of the Lord not able to save, or is his ear made heavy, that it cannot hear? But your sins separate between you and God, and because of your sins he has turned his face away from you, so as not to have mercy. The things which I have now said I will do, You shall be confident in the Lord, and he will lift you up to the good things of the land, and will feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father, I could have fulfilled before as well. For my hand is not shortened and drawn in, so that I cannot stretch it out to set my people free; nor do I have deaf ears, so that I cannot hear. From this it is shown that the ears of the Lord, which hear the righteous and do not hear sinners, are by no means like our ears, which hear equally the voice uttered, whether of righteousness or of unrighteousness. But the sins, he says, of yours, like a wall set up in the midst, divide you and God. Hence the Savior too in his passion made both one (Eph 2), and, dissolving the middle wall of partition, destroyed the enmity in his own flesh, so that those whom the wall of sins had divided the blood of Christ might join together. He opened the gate of paradise, which had been shut for a long time (Gen 3), and quenched the fiery sword with his own blood, so that the thief might hear: Today you shall be with me in paradise (Luke 23:43). What follows, And because of your sins he has turned his face away from you, so that he would not hear, or so as not to have mercy, shows this: that he could not bear the stench of their sins and their iniquities, but turned away his face, so as not to see their foulness and be compelled at once to strike. Hence the sinner, longing to see the face of the Lord, says in the psalm: How long, Lord, will you forget me to the end? How long will you turn your face away from me? (Ps 12 [13]:1). And elsewhere: Show your face, and we shall be saved (Ps 79 [80]:4).

59:3-4

For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity; your lips have spoken falsehood, and your tongue utters iniquity. There is none who calls for righteousness, nor is there any who judges truly; but they trust in nothing and speak vanities. LXX: For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with sins. Your lips are defiled with iniquity, and your tongue meditates unrighteousness. No one speaks righteous things, nor is there righteous judgment. They trust in vain things and speak empty things, iniquities and sins. What he named above in general, he now sets out in its parts. And we must note that he by no means charges them with the idolatry in which they were held in the times of Isaiah, but with the shedding of blood, of which he had already spoken before: The righteous man perishes, and there is none who considers it. And righteous men are taken away, and no one understands in his heart. For the righteous man has been taken away from the face of iniquity; his burial shall be in peace, and he shall be taken from the midst (Isa 57:1, 2). And although they themselves did not lay hands on the Lord the Savior, yet by crying with one voice of impiety, His blood be on us and on our children (Matt 27:25), they are guilty of his death and have defiled hands. Of them the same Prophet testifies, saying: If you lift up your hands to me, I will not hear. Your hands are full of blood (Isa 1:15). Their lips too and their tongue speak iniquity and falsehood, so that instead of Christ they promise themselves the Antichrist; and there is no one among the people who calls for righteousness and judges truth, or, as it is in the Hebrew, faith, that is, who believes in Christ; but they trust in nothing and speak vanities. Hence the Apostle commands that we should not give heed to Jewish fables and the commandments of men who turn away from the truth (Titus 1). For truly they trust in nothing and follow vanities; in which the Lord's prophecy is fulfilled: I have come in the name of my Father, and you have not received me; if another comes in his own name, him you will receive (John 5:43).

59:5-6

They have conceived toil and brought forth iniquity; they have broken the eggs of asps and woven the webs of the spider. He who eats of their eggs shall die, and what has been warmed shall break out into a basilisk. Their webs shall not serve for a garment, nor shall they be covered with their works. LXX: For they are in labor with pain and beget iniquity. They have broken the eggs of asps and woven the web of the spider. And he who wishes to eat of their eggs, breaking one, will find it rotten, and in it a basilisk. Their web shall not serve for a garment, nor shall they be covered with their works. Those who await the coming of the Antichrist, and cannot say, From your fear, Lord, we have conceived, and been in labor, and brought forth; we have wrought the spirit of your salvation upon the earth (Isa 26:18), rightly conceive pain and bring forth iniquity, so that the one whom they seek with much labor they may receive in iniquity. Of their father it is written: He conceived pain and brought forth iniquity (Ps 7:15). These break and burst the eggs of asps, so as to take their poisons into their own minds; to them it is said in the Gospel: Serpents, brood of vipers (Matt 3:7). And he fittingly set down the eggs of asps and serpents, which are said to produce eggs first. And because they not only retain the poisons of malice in their hearts, but also meditate on the law of the Lord day and night, muttering old wives' fables, therefore it is said: And they weave the webs of the spider, with which they catch flies and gnats and small creatures; but if anything strong comes against them, it flies through as though through empty air. He who eats, he says, of their eggs shall die, that is, he who yields to their counsels, as Abel yielded to Cain when he said, Let us go out into the field (Gen 4:8), will at once be killed; or, as the Seventy translated: He who wishes to eat of their eggs, crushing one, will find it rotten, and in it a basilisk. For he who, deceived at first sight, thinks them the eggs of hens and other birds, which are harmless to eat, if he breaks one before he eats, will at once perceive a most foul stench and stink, and in what has been warmed he will find a basilisk; or, according to Symmachus and Theodotion, an asp. Aquila put a viper, for which in the Hebrew is read EPHEE (אפעה). He, then, who, hearing the Jewish traditions, wishes to prepare himself for the feasts of the thousand years, and, entangled in the delights of the promises, to stretch out his hand to the egg: if before he eats, that is, before he yields to deadly words, he is willing first to consider what is said, and to examine each word and handle its reasoning, he will at once find that in them the Antichrist is being prepared. According to the Hebrew, then, he who eats of their eggs shall die. But he who, according to the Seventy, is willing to break them first, and to look more carefully and see what lies hidden, will find a most foul stench, and the serpent, the prince of all, the devil, lying hidden in their traditions. And because he had said above, They weave the webs of the spider, he explains that the weaving of these webs does no good. Their labor, he says, and all their doctrine does not make the garment of Christ, nor a cloak by which the nakedness of the soul may be covered; but they sweat with fruitless labor, as this same Prophet says: This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me. And in vain do they worship me, teaching the doctrines and precepts of men (Isa 29:13); following these, they neglect the law of God. And so that we may know that works are signified by the web, he added: Nor shall they be covered with their works. Some explain this place thus: The eggs of asps they have split, or broken: that is, they abandoned all the biting words of the Prophets, and wove for themselves the smooth speeches of the false prophets; and whoever eats of them will be struck by the serpent, and will understand that the words of falsehood have profited him nothing.

59:7-8

Their works are useless works, and the work of iniquity is in their hands. Their feet run to evil, and they hasten to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are useless thoughts; desolation and destruction are in their ways. The way of peace they have not known, and there is no judgment in their steps. Their paths have become crooked to them; everyone who treads in them does not know peace. LXX: For their works are works of iniquity, and their feet run to malice; swift to shed harmless blood; and their thoughts are the thoughts of fools. Destruction and misery are in their ways, and the way of peace they have not known, and there is no judgment in their ways. For their paths are perverse, which they pass along, and they do not know peace. Therefore they are not covered with their works, because their works are works of iniquity, which the Apostle calls unfruitful, that is, having no fruits (Eph 5). And their feet run to evil and hasten to shed harmless blood (Prov 1). For they had this custom in the slaying of the Prophets too. To them Stephen said: For which of the Prophets did your fathers not persecute? (Acts 7:52). And the Lord in the Gospel: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the Prophets and stone those who are sent to you (Matt 23:37); and again: All the righteous blood that has been shed upon the earth shall come upon you, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah the son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the Temple and the altar (ibid., 35). Hence it is said to them above as well: For your hands are defiled with blood, and your tongue speaks iniquity (Isa 59:3). And through this practice of cruelty and blasphemy they came to the slaying of the Lord, just as Judas too came by the way of avarice to murder, or rather to sacrilege joined with avarice. What follows, Their thoughts are the thoughts of fools; destruction and misery are in their ways, and the way of peace they have not known, and, above, Their feet are swift to shed blood, the Apostle set down in Romans (ch. 3). Many, not knowing this, think it was taken from the thirteenth psalm, in which the verses were added in the common edition and are not found in the Hebrew; about this we spoke more fully at the beginning of this volume. Rightly did they not know the way of peace, who refused to receive its author. For he is our peace, who says to the Apostles: My peace I give you, my peace I leave you (John 14:27); and to Jerusalem: If you knew the things that are for your peace; for the days shall come upon you, and your enemies shall surround you with a rampart, and besiege you, and dash your children to the ground (Luke 19:42, 43). And those who have not received peace consequently have no judgment in their ways either: namely him of whom it was said above, Behold my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved whom my soul has loved; he shall bring forth judgment to the nations (Isa 42:1). It follows: Their ways are perverse, not by nature, but by their own will. For whatever is perverted and bent is twisted from straight into crooked. The whole doctrine of the Pharisees is a subversion of the truth; whoever walks by it not only does not find peace, but does not even know it, so as to know what he ought to seek.

59:9ff.

Because of this judgment is far removed from us, and righteousness will not overtake us. We waited for light, and behold, darkness; for brightness, and we have walked in darkness. We have groped for the wall like the blind, and we have felt about as if without eyes; we have stumbled at noon as in darkness; in dark places as dead men. We shall all roar like bears, and like doves we shall moan in meditation. We waited for judgment, and there shall be none; for salvation, and it is far removed from us. LXX: Therefore judgment has departed from them, and righteousness does not overtake them. While they waited for light, darkness came upon them. Waiting for it, they shall walk in darkness; they shall grope for the wall like the blind, and shall feel about as though having no eyes. They shall fall at noon as at midnight; like dying men they shall groan; like a bear and like a dove they shall walk together. We waited for judgment, and there is none; salvation has departed far from us. After the accusation of the people of the Jews, the Prophet answers in their person what they ought to say as penitents, if indeed they wish to recover health after their wounds. And I wonder why the Seventy framed the speech as though the Prophet were speaking about them, and not they themselves answering the Prophet's words, when in what follows, overcome by the truth, they did this very thing, saying: We waited for judgment, and there is none; salvation has departed far from us. For our iniquity is great in your sight, and our sins have withstood us, and the rest. In the present time, then, all things are fulfilled. Judgment, which has been announced to the nations, is far removed from the Jews; and righteousness, which has been laid hold of by the nations, will not overtake them. They waited for the light, saying, Send forth your light and your truth (Ps 42 [43]:3), which had been promised them through the Prophets, and they have been seized by the darkness of error. They waited for brightness, and they walked in darkness. So they grope at the holy Scriptures like the blind feeling for a wall, seeking in them only the words and the leaves, not the sense and the fruit which is held in the letters. Then he adds and says: We have stumbled, or we shall fall at noon as in darkness; in dark places, as dead men. For while the sun of righteousness flashes its brightness over the whole world, they linger in darkness, namely as men dead in sin. We shall all roar, he says, like bears, and like doves we shall moan in meditation; so that they are at once cruel and wretched: fierce and savage toward the lowly and those subject to them, fearful and trembling toward those who are stronger, whom they dread as doves dread hawks. We read in another place too: Like a she-bear robbed of her cubs; and in Daniel the bloody kingdom, in which there are three rows of teeth, is compared to a most ferocious she-bear (2 Sam 17:8; Dan 7). And like doves we shall moan in meditation, without sense and understanding of the Scriptures, meditating only on the words, which they chant by heart. But just as the doves of which it is written, Ephraim is like a dove that has no sense (Hos 7:11), and as in the Gospel the simplicity of doves is set against the malice of serpents (Matt 10), so in the present place simplicity without prudence, which is close to folly, is shown in the mere meditation of words. They will wait for judgment, and there will be none; for salvation, understood, they will wait, and there will be none, because it has gone far away to the nations. Here it must be noted that everything is said in the future tense, so as to indicate what the Jews are now enduring.

59:12ff.

Our iniquities are multiplied before you, and our sins have answered against us; for our crimes are with us, and we have known our iniquities: to sin and to lie against the Lord; and we have turned away so as not to go behind our Lord, so as to speak calumny; and we have conceived transgression, and have spoken from the heart words of falsehood. And judgment is turned backward, and righteousness has stood far off, for truth has fallen in the street, and equity could not enter. And truth has been given over to forgetfulness, and he who departed from evil lay open to be a prey. LXX: For our iniquity is great in your sight, and our sins have withstood us. For our iniquities are in us, and we have known our unrighteousnesses. We have acted impiously, and we have lied, and we have departed from our God. We have spoken unjust things and been disobedient. We have been in labor with and meditated from our hearts unjust words. And we have departed from judgment, and righteousness has stood far off, for truth has been consumed in their ways, and they could not pass by the straight road. And truth has been taken away, and they turned aside their mind so as not to understand. He gives the reasons why they roared like bears and meditated like doves, and waited for a judgment that was not there, and for a salvation that passed over to the nations: because multiplied, they say, are our iniquities in your sight, from which you had turned away your face for a long time, so as not to see them, so as not to strike. And our sins have answered against us, so that we have received what we deserved. And our crimes are with us, and we have known our iniquities, which, while we committed them for a long time, we thought to be righteousness. And what are the iniquities? To sin and to lie against God; or, as Aquila translated according to the Hebrew, to deny God: which refers to the Savior. And we have forsaken, they say, our God, saying: We know that God spoke to Moses; but as for this man, we do not know where he is from (John 9:29); so as to speak calumny: If this man were from God, he would not break the sabbath (ibid., 16); and: By Beelzebub the prince of demons he casts out demons (Luke 11:15). And transgression, which in Greek is called more expressively ἀπόστασις, when someone denies God and is convicted of prevarication. We have conceived and spoken from the heart words of falsehood, despising the law of God and following the traditions of men, which they call δευτερώσεις, and which we feigned in our heart: And judgment is turned backward, and righteousness has stood far off. For what share has righteousness with iniquity? What agreement has Christ with Belial? Righteousness has taken its stand among the nations and has departed from us, because truth has fallen in the street. For wide and spacious is the way that leads to death (Matt 7), because they would not enter the narrow way in which truth abides. And truth has been given over to forgetfulness, of which it is written: Truth has sprung from the earth, and righteousness has looked down from heaven (Ps 84 [85]:12). Here we must observe that truth is named often, so that the person of Christ might be shown; forsaking him, they followed falsehood. And he who departed from evil lay open to be a prey. Although this seems obscure, it can be explained thus: when we were fashioning falsehood from our own heart and forsaking the law of God, righteousness stood far off, and truth fell in the streets, and equity could not enter in to us, and the Son of God, who is the truth, was given over to forgetfulness; so much so that whoever wished to depart from the traditions of the Jews at once lay open to plots and persecutions, so that they cast out of the synagogues the man blind from birth who had received his sight (John 9). And after the resurrection of the Lord the Savior they persecuted and stripped all who believed in him, to whom the Churches from the whole world of the nations sent ministrations, for them to distribute through the hands of the Apostles.

59:16-17

And the Lord saw, and it appeared evil in his eyes, that there is no judgment; and he saw that there is no man, and he was at a loss, because there is none to meet him. And his own arm will save for him, and his righteousness itself has strengthened him. He has put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation upon his head. He has put on the garments of vengeance, and is covered as with a cloak of zeal. As for vengeance, as for the repayment of indignation to his foes, and recompense to his enemies, he will repay recompense to the islands. LXX: The Lord saw, and it did not please him, because there was no judgment. And he saw, and there was no man. And he considered, and there was none to defend. And he avenged them with his arm, and upheld with mercy. And he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and set the helmet of salvation on his head. And he was wrapped in the garment of vengeance, and in a cloak, as one repaying vengeance, reproach to his adversaries. Up to this point the prophetic discourse has been woven in the person of the people; now the prophet speaks in his own person. When they said these things, the Lord saw that they made a show of repentance with the mouth and did not practice it in the heart, and it did not please him. For he sought in them the truth of judgment, which had been transferred to the nations, and did not find it. He longed for some righteous man who could meet him in his anger, and did not find one; he who had said above as well: I came, and there was no man; I called, and there was none to hear (Isa 50:2). And because, while they persisted in their crime, not even one righteous man was found, but all had turned aside, together they had become useless, and there is none who does good, there is not even one (Ps 13 [14]), he strengthened him with his arm and righteousness, or mercy, so that those who wish to be converted from error may be preserved not by their own merit but by the clemency of God. Then he put on the breastplate of righteousness, and the helmet of salvation, and the garments of vengeance, and was wrapped in the cloak of zeal; and thus armed he went forth to war, to render vengeance to his enemies, doubtless meaning the Jews who persevered in their blasphemies, and recompense to his foes, when the Roman army surrounded them; and in their victory the Lord is shown to have fought. Paul used this testimony when writing to the Ephesians, wishing us to put on the armor of Christ, by which we may resist the fiery darts of the devil (Eph 6). And what is not found in the Seventy Translators, He will repay recompense to the islands, signifies the cities of Judea, which the Roman army laid waste. For above too (Isa 20) the Lord speaks through the Prophet to the inhabitants of the island, that is, of Jerusalem.

59:19-20

And those from the West shall fear the name of the Lord, and those from the rising of the sun his glory, when he comes like a violent river which the spirit of the Lord drives on; and the redeemer shall come to Zion, and to those who return from iniquity in Jacob, says the Lord. This is my covenant with them, says the Lord: My spirit which is in you, and my words which I have put in your mouth, shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of the seed of your seed, says the Lord, from now and for ever. LXX: And those from the West shall fear the name of the Lord, and those from the rising of the sun the glorious name. For the wrath of the Lord shall come like a violent river, ÷ it shall come with fury ⁚ and he who delivers shall come from Zion. And he shall turn away impieties from Jacob, and this shall be my testament to them, says the Lord. My spirit which is in you, and my words which I have given in your mouth, shall not fail from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your seed, says the Lord, from now and for ever. After the Lord has put on the breastplate of righteousness, and the helmet of salvation, and the garments of vengeance, and the cloak of zeal for the fight, and has come to the contest and to vengeance, to repay his foes and render to his enemies, and to overthrow their islands, that is, their cities and villages, then the foreigners who are to come from the West and the East to rest in the bosom of Abraham (Matt 8), of whom it was also said above (cf. Isa 49:12), Behold, these shall come from afar, some from the West, and others from the North, and others from the land of the Persians, will fear the Lord with that fear which is the beginning of wisdom (Sir 1). Of this we read in many places, of which let us set down a few: Blessed is the man who fears the Lord (Ps 111 [112]:1); and: There is no want for those who fear him (Ps 33 [34]:10); and: The fear of the Lord is discipline and wisdom (Prov 15:33); and: Come, children, hear me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord (Ps 33 [34]:12); and: Blessed is the man who fears the Lord (Ps 127 [128]:4); and: The fear of the Lord adds days (Prov 10:27). That, once Israel has been rejected, the crowd of the nations takes its place, the prophet Malachi teaches more fully, in whom it is said to the Jews: I have no pleasure in you, says the Lord Almighty, and I will not accept a sacrifice from your hands (Mal 1:10, 11); and again of the multitude of the nations: For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name has been glorified among the nations. The author of this blessedness is he who will come like a violent river which the spirit of the Lord drives on; or, as Aquila translated, like a narrow river, the spirit of the Lord its seal; or Theodotion, like an assailing river, the spirit of the Lord is sealed. In this testimony, then, as the Seventy translated it, like a violent river the wrath of the Lord shall come with fury, the last part is not found in the Hebrew. For wrath and fury are not to be set among the promises of God, since in the other things that follow there is the blessedness of things to come, and the threat and punishment of sinners. According to Aquila and Theodotion, the spirit of the Lord which is sealed in Christ confirms the example which is read in John the Evangelist: For him God the Father has sealed (John 6:27); of whom it has already been said before: A rod shall come forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up from its root, and the Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and fortitude, the spirit of knowledge and piety, and the spirit of the fear of the Lord has filled him (Isa 11:1ff.). Hence we too say: The light of your countenance, Lord, is sealed upon us (Ps 4:7). And in Ezekiel the foreheads of the men who groan are sealed with the impression of THAV, the Hebrew letter which is the last among them (Ezek 9). But if we wish to know how the Holy Spirit is a violent river, let us read again the Acts of the Apostles, in which it is written: And when they were gathered together, suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a violent wind, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting. And there appeared to them tongues parted as of fire, and it sat upon each of them; and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:2, 3). It follows: The redeemer of Zion shall come, and of those who return from iniquity in Jacob, says the Lord. For this the Seventy translated: He who delivers shall come from Zion, and shall turn away impieties from Jacob. If, then, he who turns away the impieties from Jacob will come from Zion, we understand this: that a man was born in Zion, and the Most High founded her, he who turns away the crimes of Jacob. But if the redeemer shall come to Zion, and to those who return from iniquity in Jacob, says the Lord, this is the sense: Christ will come, who will redeem Zion with his blood; or, according to the Hebrew idiom, he who is the kinsman of Zion and was begotten of the stock of Israel; for this is what GOEL (גואל), that is, ἀγχιστεὺς, means. And lest we think that all of Zion is redeemed and freed from its crimes, Zion which is bloodied with the blood of the Lord, he added significantly: to those who return from iniquity, if they are willing to do penance, in whom the Lord's prayer may be fulfilled: Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do (Luke 23:34). Theirs, then, is the redemption in Zion, and theirs the kinsman, who from Jacob have received him; and to them he promises, saying: This is my covenant with them, or pact, as all the others translated, or testament, as the Seventy put it. What the covenant, pact and testament is, the following verse shows: My spirit, he says, which is in you, and my words which I have put in your mouth, shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your seed, from now and for ever. This is said either to Isaiah, as it seems to me, or to the Lord, as very many think. With reference to Isaiah, then, the order is connected thus: This is the everlasting pact of the Gospel: that my spirit which is in you, and my words which I have put in your mouth, by which you foretell things to come, shall not depart from your mouth, nor from that of your sons and grandsons and your seed, so that every generation in succession is indicated: namely, that the grace of the Prophets comes upon the Apostles, and through those of Israel who are to believe through the Apostles. What he adds, from now and for ever, agrees with that testimony: Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away (Matt 24:35). Paul, explaining this place carefully, writes to the Romans that there is no distinction of Jew and Greek, but the same Lord of all, rich toward all who call upon him (Rom 10); and that the nations did not believe in such a way that Israel was wholly driven out. For I too, he says, am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God has not cast off his people whom he foreknew (Rom 11:1, 2). And a little after, when he had set down the example of Elijah, complaining to the Lord that he alone was left, and hearing from him that the Lord had left for himself seven thousand men who had not bent the knee before Baal (1 Kgs 19), he added: So then at this present time also a remnant has been saved according to the election of grace. And if by grace, it is no longer of works; otherwise grace is no longer grace. What then? What Israel was seeking, this it has obtained; but the election has obtained it, and the rest have been blinded. And they, if they do not remain in unbelief, will be grafted in. For God is able, he says, to graft them in again (Rom 11:5ff.): not against nature from the wild olive, as the multitude of the nations was grafted in, but according to nature into the good olive, that is, into their own. And at the end he set down, so as to arrive at the present chapter: For I would not have you ignorant, brothers, of this mystery, lest you be wise in your own eyes: that blindness has befallen Israel in part, until the fullness of the nations should come in, and so all Israel should be saved, as it is written: He who delivers shall come from Zion, and shall turn away impieties from Jacob; and this is my testament to them, when I take away their sins (Rom 11:25ff.). We have pursued these things at greater length so that we may understand that whatever promises we have read, and are going to speak of, concerning Zion and Jerusalem, are said not generally to all the Jews, but specially to those of Israel who were chosen in the Apostles and through the Apostles.

Book Seventeen

How many mysteries the number seventeen, which the book of the Explanations on Isaiah has now reached, holds in the holy Scriptures, I should like, Eustochium, virgin of Christ, to run through in a brief discourse. But since I cannot say everything in every place, I give only this brief reminder: that the psalm which is headed with the title of this number is of David, the servant of the Lord, and that he sang the words of the Song on the day on which the Lord delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul, and said: I will love you, O Lord, my strength, and the rest. Now the servant of the Lord is he to whom the Father speaks in Isaiah: It is a great thing for you to be called my servant (Isa 49:6). And in another place: Behold my servant whom I have chosen, and my beloved in whom is well pleased my soul (Isa 42:1). This servant, whose name means strong of hand, on the day on which the Lord delivered him from the hand of Saul, which in our language sounds as sought for or hell, and from all his enemies, who cried out against him: Crucify, crucify such a one (Luke 23), when he ascended as victor to the Father in tawny garments from Bozrah, spoke among other words of one triumphing these: Deliver me from the contradictions of the people; you will set me as head of the nations. A people which I did not know has served me; at the hearing of the ear it has obeyed me (Ps 17 [18]:44, 45). And again concerning the people of the Jews: Alien sons have lied to me; alien sons have grown old, and have limped away from their paths (ibid., 46); to whom Elijah too had said: How long do you limp on both feet (1 Kgs 18:21)? Moreover, a thing that is hard to find in others, this psalm is contained both in the history of Samuel and in that of the Chronicles (2 Sam 22). This number, advancing by increments from one up to seven, comes to the twenty-eighth psalm, which is itself also inscribed 'of David', for the completion of the tabernacle, when the angels are commanded: Bring to the Lord, sons of God; bring to the Lord the young of rams. And all the mysteries of saving baptism and of the Church are sung in it together: The voice of the Lord is upon the waters; the God of majesty has thundered; the Lord is upon many waters; the voice of the Lord in power (Ps 28 [29]:1). And a little after: The voice of the Lord preparing the stags, and he has revealed the thickets, and in his Temple all will speak glory (ibid., 3, 10). And to show the multitude of believers he added: The Lord makes the flood to be inhabited, and the Lord will sit as king for ever. And again, when the mystery of eight is added, it makes the thirty-sixth psalm, the alphabetical one, whose beginning is: Do not be envious among the evildoers, nor be jealous of those who work iniquity. Its exposition belongs not to a preface but to a volume of its own. And not to rehearse many things now: growing by increments up to the number fifteen, in which are the Psalms of the Steps, and in which the vessel of election stays with Peter at Jerusalem, it makes the number one hundred and twenty, those who were the first to believe in Christ and who climbed with the Apostles to the upper room of faith (Acts 5); and the Holy Spirit came down upon them (Gal 1). And after that, advancing in order up to the number seventeen, and possessing the dignity of the Gospel, at the Lord's command it takes from the right-hand side one hundred and fifty-three great fish and places them in the Church (John 21). To her now also the prophet Isaiah speaks.

60:1ff.

Arise, be enlightened; for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you. For behold, darkness will cover the earth, and thick gloom the peoples; but upon you the Lord will rise, and his glory will be seen in you. And the nations will walk in your light, and kings in the brightness of your rising. LXX: Be enlightened, be enlightened, ÷ Jerusalem ⁚ for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you. Behold, darkness will cover the earth, and thick gloom upon the nations. But upon you the Lord will appear, and his glory will be seen in you. And the nations will walk in your light, and kings in your brightness. What we thought about the restoration of Zion and Jerusalem, and about everything that is promised to her by the prophetic oracle, we said more fully at the end of the preceding book, where we explained what that little verse meant: The redeemer will come to Zion, and to those who return from iniquity in Jacob. Now we must touch briefly on what most people think of this passage, so that, once the error has been seen through, we may more easily take up the truth. The Jews and our half-Jews, who expect a golden and jewelled Jerusalem from heaven, contend that these things will come to pass in the kingdom of a thousand years, when all the nations are to serve Israel, and the camels of Midian and Ephah, coming from Sheba, will bring gold and incense, and all the sheep of Kedar will be gathered, and the rams of Nebaioth will come to be sacrificed upon the altar of the Temple that will have been built. They say too that from the islands, and above all in the ships of Tarshish, her daughters will fly like doves, bringing riches of gold and silver; that the walls of Jerusalem will be built by foreigners, with the kings of the nations set over them; that the gates of the city will always stand open, so that by day and by night the riches of Jerusalem and the victims may be brought in; and that everything that lies desolate will be rebuilt with cypress and pine and cedar cut in Lebanon, above all the Temple of the Lord, in which there will be everlasting gladness; so that she will suck the milk of the nations and eat the riches of kings, and there will be such an abundance of all things that they will have gold for bronze, silver for iron, bronze for wood, iron for stones. Her princes too, they say, will enjoy everlasting peace, and bishops will preside over the peoples in righteousness, and her gates will be carved in relief. And what is greater than these, instead of the sun and the moon the Lord himself will shine with everlasting light; and for one man she will have a thousand very strong men, and for little ones she will possess very mighty nations. So say those who desire earthly pleasures, and seek beauty in wives and a great number of children, whose god is their belly and whose glory is in their shame (Phil 3); and whoever follows their error confesses himself, under the Christian name, to be like the Jews. Others, however, assert that all these things were promised to the Jews in a carnal sense, if they had received him who says in the Gospel: I am the light of the world (John 8:12), which enlightens every man coming into the world; so that, just as victims were granted to the people of Israel, not because they were good in themselves, but so that they might not be offered to demons, so too the Lord promises these things to the gluttonous Jews, who seek nothing but the pleasures of the body, so that at least for the sake of their carnal desires and an abundance of wealth they might receive the Son of God; and since they did not receive him, the promises too, they say, became void. Thus to the Canaanite woman pleading for her daughter: I did not come, he says, except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel (Matt 15:24). And to his disciples: Do not go away into the way of the nations, and do not enter the cities of the Samaritans; go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel (Matt 10:5, 6). For this reason the Apostles too first proclaimed the Lord in the synagogues, and when these did not receive the Gospel they said to them: It was necessary that the word should be preached to you; but since you have not received salvation, behold, we turn to the nations (Acts 13:46). For the light came into the world, and the Jews loved darkness rather. Hence the Lord too, when he had wept over Jerusalem, added: If you also had known the things that make for your peace (Luke 19:42). And since she did not receive it, he went on: But now a day will come upon you, and your enemies will surround you with a rampart, and hem you in, and bring you down to the ground together with your children (ibid., 43). But let us, following the former sense, believe that all of this is said to the Church, which was first gathered from the Jewish people, and which through the Apostles passed on to the nations the light that had risen upon her. To her it is said: Arise, be enlightened, so that she who fell in the unbelievers may rise in the faithful; she who fell in the synagogues may rise in the churches; and, once she has risen, may be enlightened, so that she may have no darkness of error at all. For your light, he says, has come, the light that all the Prophets promised, which you were ever awaiting. And the glory of the Lord, which was once upon the tabernacle and his Temple, has risen upon you; of which it is said: Glorious things have been said of you, city of God (Ps 86 [87]:3). For behold, darkness will cover the earth, that is, those who savor earthly things; and thick gloom the peoples, or, as we read in the Hebrew, the tribes: which refers properly to the Jews, of whom it is written in another psalm: For there the tribes went up, the tribes of the Lord, the testimony of Israel (Ps 121 [122]:4). But upon you the Lord will rise, the sun of righteousness, and his glory will be seen in you, of which it is written: And we saw his glory, the glory as of the only-begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth (John 1:14). And the nations will walk in your light. We all shall walk in the light of the Apostles, which shines in the world, and the darkness did not comprehend it. And kings, he says, in the brightness of your rising, when you were first born in Christ. This is fulfilled both spiritually and carnally: so that kings whose heart is in the hand of the Lord, and in whose mortal body sin does not reign (Prov 21), may walk in the brightness of the newborn Church, or in him who has risen in the Church, and may bow their necks to the faith of Christ, the true king (Rom 6). And we see this fulfilled daily, when the Roman princes, the error of idolatry and the fury of persecution being removed, pass over to the faith and tranquillity of Christ. There are some who await in a time to come all these things which we relate as partly fulfilled and wholly to be fulfilled from the first coming of the Savior until the consummation of the world, when, as the fullness of the nations comes in, all Israel is to be saved (Rom 11). Their opinion is by no means to be rejected, provided we know that these things are to be fulfilled spiritually and not carnally. Further, the name Jerusalem and of the nations, which the Seventy set down here, is not found in the Hebrew, and must be marked beforehand with an obelus, against those who assert that everything said here is said to Jerusalem.

60:4

Lift up your eyes round about and see: all these have gathered and come to you. Your sons will come from afar, and your daughters will suck at your side. LXX: Lift up your eyes round about, and see all your sons gathered. All your sons have come from afar, and your daughters will be carried upon the shoulders. It is said to the Church, Zion, which was first gathered through the Apostles; of whom we also read in the Acts of the Apostles that devout men from the whole world were in Jerusalem, who received the word of God, and in the tongues of their own and of foreign nations either heard others speaking or themselves spoke to the rest (Acts 2). And they are commanded to lift up their eyes round about, which the Lord too commanded the Apostles, saying: Lift up your eyes and see, for the crops are already white for the harvest (John 4:35). For out of Zion, and by no means out of Mount Sinai, the law will go forth, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. And she is commanded to lift up her eyes and see her sons gathered, who come from afar. To her it is said in another place too: Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion, proclaim, daughter of Jerusalem: Behold, I come, and I will dwell in your midst, says the Lord (Zeph 3:17); and: Many nations will come to the Lord, and they will be my people, and I will be their God (Zech 2:11). Now we are the sons who come to the Lord from afar, once strangers to the Testament of God and to his promises, having no hope, and without God in the world. But what does the Apostle say? You who were once far off have now been brought near (Eph 2:13). And what follows, And your daughters will suck at your side, signifies that souls that are sucklings in Christ, and in the infancy of baptism, of whom the apostle Peter too speaks, Like newborn babes, desire the rational milk without guile (1 Pet 2:2), suck the milk of the apostles. To such babes and sucklings Paul also spoke: My little children, with whom I am again in labor until Christ be formed in you (Gal 4:19). And in another place: As a nurse cherishing her children, so, longing for you, we desire to impart to you not only the Gospel of Christ but our own souls as well (1 Thess 2:7, 8). But what is said instead of this in the Seventy, your daughters will be carried upon the shoulders, must be considered more carefully. For the sons, who are strong, come from afar by themselves and are gathered to the faith of the Lord. But the daughters, who are weaker and, through the frailty of their sex, have not yet come to the perfect man, are carried on the shoulders of the Apostles, so as to be brought into the bosom of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

60:5

Then you will see and overflow, and your heart will marvel and be enlarged, when the multitude of the sea has been turned to you, and the strength of the nations has come to you. LXX: Then you will see, and you will fear, and you will be astonished in heart: because the riches of the sea, and of the nations, and of the peoples will be transferred to you. When you have lifted up your eyes and beheld your sons and daughters either coming swiftly by themselves or carried on the shoulders of the saints, then you will rejoice, and like rivers you will overflow with sudden waters, and your heart will marvel and be astonished, nay rather will be enlarged, as it hears the Apostle: My mouth is open to you, O Corinthians. And again: Be enlarged, and we too (2 Cor 6:11); lest through narrowness of heart you should be unable to have as your guest Christ, who says in the Gospel: I and the Father will come and will make our dwelling with him (John 14:23). But what is added in the Seventy, and you will fear, is not found in the Hebrew; unless perhaps, after the greatness of the joy, fear crept in, lest she lose so great a good. Or is it not joy to see riches, and the multitude of the sea being transferred and turned to oneself, and the strength of the nations coming to oneself, so that whatever is in the world and on the face of the earth is one's own; and, the faith of the nations being strengthened, to say: I can do all things in him who strengthens me, Jesus Christ (Phil 4:13)?

60:6-7

A flood of camels will cover you, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah. All from Sheba will come, bringing gold and incense, and proclaiming praise to the Lord. All the flock of Kedar will be gathered to you; the rams of Nebaioth will minister to you; they will be offered upon my altar of propitiation, and I will glorify the house of my majesty. LXX: And herds of camels will come to you, and the camels of Midian and Gephar will cover you: all from Sheba will come, bringing gold and incense, and they will proclaim the salvation of the Lord. All the sheep of Kedar will be gathered to you, the rams of Nabaeoth will come, and they will be offered as propitiatory upon my altar; and the house of my prayer will be glorified. After the riches of the sea and the strength of the nations, herds of camels too, and the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah, are promised to Jerusalem, all of which will come from Sheba carrying gold and incense, and, what is greater than these, proclaiming the salvation of the Lord. All the sheep of Kedar too will be gathered to the Church, and the rams of Nebaioth will come, or, as is written in the Hebrew, will minister, and will be offered, or will offer victims upon the altar of the Lord, so that his house may become renowned. Midian and Ephah are regions beyond Arabia, fertile in camels, and the whole province is called Sheba, whence came also the queen of Sheba, who came to hear the wisdom of Solomon, she too bringing gold and incense, carrying much to the peaceable king and receiving greater things from him (1 Kgs 10). Kedar is the region of the Saracens, who in Scripture are called Ishmaelites. And Nebaioth is one of the sons of Ishmael, from whose names the desert is called, which, poor in crops, is full of flocks. Through the familiar names of barbarian nations, then, that are neighbors to Israel, the conversion of the whole world is proclaimed. For in this place Midian means iniquity; Ephah, loosed, or pouring out; Sheba, conversion, or captivity; Kedar, darkness; Nebaioth, prophecies. So herds of camels, loosed from the bonds of iniquity and pouring out their souls to God, will cover Jerusalem with gifts, and all will come from captivity and in their conversion, bringing the gold of faith and the incense of sacrifice. And through these gifts, by no means content with their own salvation, they will advance so far as to proclaim the salvation of God to others as well. That rich man in the Gospel who, like a camel, carried the burdens of riches, and was a camel, would not listen to the Lord's counsels nor be unloaded, so that, the pack cast off, he might fly to heaven on the wings of a dove; therefore he went away sad. And of a camel of this kind the Savior speaks: It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man into the kingdom of heaven (Matt 19:24). He set forth the difficulty of the thing, not its impossibility. Indeed your mother Paula, of holy memory, and your brother Pammachius passed through the eye of a needle, that is, through the strait and narrow way that leads to life, into the kingdom of heaven, leaving behind with its burdens the broad way that leads to Tartarus. Nay, whatever they had they carried into the gifts of the Lord, fulfilling what is written: The ransom of a man's soul is his own riches (Prov 13:8). For the things that are impossible with men are possible with God (Matt 19). Having among their gifts the chief things, gold in understanding and incense of the sweetest odor, and saying: Let my prayer be directed as incense in your sight, and: We are the good odor of Christ in every place (2 Cor 2:15), they proclaim daily the salvation of the Lord by the example of their virtue, so that all the sheep of Kedar may be gathered in the Church and pass from the darkness of error to the light. And let the rams of the Prophets, of whom it is sung in the twenty-eighth psalm, Bring to the Lord, sons of God, bring to the Lord the young of rams, come and be offered, or, according to Theodotion, offer themselves as a sacrifice to the Lord, and become propitiatory victims, so that the Church of Christ may be glorified. Of sheep of this kind the Savior spoke to his disciples: Go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel (Matt 10:6). And again: My sheep hear my voice (John 10:27). And more fully in Ezekiel: Behold, I will seek my sheep and visit them, as a shepherd seeks his flock. Thus says the Lord: I will seek the lost, and bring back the straying, and bind up the broken, and strengthen the weak, and guard the strong, and I will feed them with judgment (Ezek 34:11, 12). And so that we might know who the sheep were, he puts it more plainly: And they will know that I am the Lord their God, and they are my people, the house of Israel, says the Lord God; and you are my sheep, and you are all the sheep of my flock, and I am the Lord your God (ibid., 27, 28). If anyone among the nations is rich, then, let him be saved as a camel, not without gifts and offerings, with which he may proclaim the word of the Lord. If anyone is of the simplicity of sheep and of the authority of rams, let him go up, or be offered upon the altar of the Lord by those who have the power, so that his house may be glorified. But what we noted as written in the Hebrew, The rams of Nebaioth will minister to you, and they will offer upon my altar of propitiation, is properly understood of those who, chosen from the nations for the priesthood, are ministers of the Savior. And if anyone is contentious, and contends that these things were promised in a carnal sense, let us answer him: We have no such custom, nor has the Church of God (1 Cor 11:16). And let us say this too: that even if they were promised carnally to the Jews, still they were promised under a condition, namely that if they had received their light, which had been sent to them, then these things also would follow; that is, that through the desire of gold and an abundance of wealth and of carnal things, by whose allurements this nation was always captivated, they might receive the Son of God sent to them; and since they did not receive him, all was taken away, and the inheritance was given back spiritually to those who received him.

60:8-9

Who are these who fly like clouds, and like doves to their windows? For the islands wait for me, and the ships of the sea in the beginning, that I may bring your sons from afar, their silver and their gold with them, to the name of the Lord your God, and to the Holy One of Israel, because he has glorified you. LXX: Who are these who fly like clouds, and like doves with their young to me? The islands have waited for me, and the ships of Tarshish among the first, to bring your sons from afar, and their silver and gold with them, for the sake of the holy name of the Lord, and because the Holy One of Israel has been glorified. Since the Lord entered Egypt upon a light cloud, and commanded the clouds of the Prophets, to whom the truth of God has come, not to rain showers upon Israel, the Church, first gathered from the people of the Circumcision, marvels that a crowd of nations is flying to her from the whole world, and, having taken the wings of the Holy Spirit, is hastening, according to Symmachus and Theodotion, to their windows, according to Aquila to their floodgates, in order to enter the Church. Or that teachers with their disciples, that is, doves with their young, are flying to the Church from the islands of the nations, which, according to the oracles of the Prophets, will wait for the Lord. The ships of THARSIS (תרשיש) too, that is, of the sea, of which we spoke more fully in the vision of Tyre, will bring the sons of the Church in the beginning of faith, carrying gold and silver. For with the heart one believes unto righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation (Rom 10:10). Of this gold and silver it is written in the sixty-seventh psalm: The wings of a dove covered with silver, and her hinder parts in the gleam of gold (Ps 67 [68]:14). And in the seventy-first psalm: The kings of Tarshish and the islands will offer gifts, and the kings of the Arabians and of Sheba will bring presents (Ps 71 [72]:10). All these things are brought to the name of the Lord God and to the Holy One of Israel, who has glorified him.

60:10ff.

And the sons of strangers will build your walls, and their kings will minister to you. For in my indignation I struck you, and in my reconciliation I have had mercy on you. And your gates will be open continually; they will not be shut by day or by night, so that the strength of the nations may be brought to you, and their kings be led in. For the nation and the kingdom that will not serve you will perish, and the nations will be laid waste with desolation. LXX: And foreigners will build your walls, and their kings will stand by you. For because of my wrath I struck you, and because of mercy I have loved you. And your gates will be open always; they will not be shut by day or by night, so that they may bring in to you the strength of the nations, and their kings who are to be led in. For the nations and the kings that will not serve you will perish; the nations will be made desolate with desolation. Among the other things with which the Church is enriched and the city of the Savior is built, foreigners too and the sons of strangers build her walls, so that the enemy cannot enter nor faithlessness find a place. Foreigners and strangers properly signify the people of the nations, who truly built up the Church of Christ, so much so that their kings and princes minister to her, or stand by her. This is taken either carnally or spiritually. If carnally, we see the Roman Caesars bow their necks to the yoke of Christ, build churches at public expense, and issue decrees of law against the persecutions of the heathen and the snares of heretics. If spiritually, whoever among them are princes in continence, eloquence and holiness, and subjugate the servitude of the flesh to the rule of the soul, these minister to her and stand by her, or give aid to her whom he often forsakes because of her negligence, or strikes with the rod of persecutors, so that he may again love her for his own mercy's sake. Or certainly this must be said: that she who was once afflicted and handed over to captivity in the people of the Jews he reconciles to himself in the calling of the nations, so that her gates are always open, and are shut neither by day nor by night, and stand continually open to those who desire to be saved; that is, that entrance to her is not denied to those who wish to believe, whether in joy or in tribulation. And let the strength, or the riches, of the nations be brought in to her, and let their kings minister to her, or be led to her as captives. This you will understand when you see the most eloquent men led to the faith of Christ, and the wisdom of the wise made foolish, and the prudence of the prudent rejected (1 Cor 1), so that the foolishness of God is wiser than men. But the nation and their kings who refuse to render the Church a good and profitable service, so as to pass over into apostolic dignity, will perish with the perdition that is prepared for the ungodly; and whatever was in them who refused to have God as their guest will be reduced to desolation.

60:13-14

The glory of Lebanon will come to you, the fir and the box and the pine together, to adorn the place of my sanctification; and I will glorify the place of my feet. And the sons of those who humbled you will come to you bowed down, and all who disparaged you will worship the footprints of your feet, and they will call you the city of the Lord, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel. LXX: The glory of Lebanon will come to you, in cypress and pine and cedar together, so that my holy place may be glorified, ÷|÷ and I will glorify the place of my feet ⁚ And the sons of those who humbled you will go to you in fear, ÷ and provoked you ⁚ and all who provoked you will worship the footprints of your feet; and you will be called the city of the Lord, Zion, of the Holy One of Israel. Much is lacking in the Seventy, which I have set down from the Hebrew under asterisks, and what they added I have marked beforehand with an obelus. Lebanon is a mountain of Phoenicia, planted with lofty trees, which the Psalmist describes when he says: I saw the ungodly exalted above measure and lifted up like the cedars of Lebanon (Ps 36 [37]:35). And in another place: The Lord will break the cedars of Lebanon (Ps 28 [29]:5). And many other things which I pass over for the sake of brevity. From this mountain Hiram king of Tyre once sent timber to Solomon at Joppa, for building the Temple of God (1 Kgs 5). From it too Scripture now promises that the fir and the box and the pine, or, according to the Seventy, the cypress and the pine and the cedar, or, according to Aquila, the fir, thaadaor, and thaassur, or, according to Theodotion, Brais, Thadaar, and Theassur, are to be cut together, so that the temple of Zion may be built (2 Chr 2). If that is so, where will the golden and jewelled Jerusalem be? Where the wife of the Lamb? Where the twelve gates adorned with a variety of gems? Unless perhaps she will have jewelled walls and foundations, and the Temple, which ought to be more richly adorned, will be built of wood!
