For this reason we are compelled to take everything spiritually: that the fir, the cypress, the pine and the cedar, once lofty trees of Lebanon, have glorified the Temple of God and the place of his feet, and made it renowned. And not to draw out the sense in a long discourse: do not the holy man and most eloquent martyr Cyprian, and Hilary, the confessor of our own time, once lofty trees in the world, seem to you to have built the Church of God? And what follows, And the sons of those who humbled you will come to you bowed down, or returning, and all who had disparaged you will worship the footprints of your feet, we ought to understand of those who are Christians not by will but by necessity, and who bow with fearful minds through dread of offending those who reign. Or certainly that those who were formerly persecutors afterwards believed: such as was the apostle Paul too, who persecuted the Church of God and was afterwards called a vessel of election (Acts 9). When these things have been so fulfilled that the fullness of the nations enters in, then all Israel will be saved. And she will truly be called the city of the Lord, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel, who stands upon the watchtower and has been gathered from both peoples.

60:15-16

Because you were forsaken and hated, and there was none who passed through I will make you the pride of the ages, a joy from generation to generation; and you will suck the milk of the nations, and you will be suckled at the breast of kings. And you will know that I am the Lord who saves you, and your redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob. LXX: Because you were forsaken and hated, and there was none who helped, I will make you an everlasting exultation, a joy of generations unto generations. And you will suck the milk of the nations, and you will eat the riches of kings. And you will know that I am the Lord who has saved you, and who has rescued you, the God of Jacob. She who before had been forsaken and hated, when the branches in you were broken off because they had not borne fruit, branches which were broken off for this reason, that there was no one who passed through and offered help there, of whom it is said in the psalms, And those who passed by did not say: The blessing of the Lord be upon you (Ps 128 [129]:8): therefore I will make you an everlasting pride, or an exultation and joy of two generations, other branches from the wild olive of the nations being grafted in place of the former branches, which contrary to the nature of the pattern will bear fruit, not of the former bitterness but of the sweetness which they have drawn from the root. You will suck too the milk of the nations, and you will be suckled at the breast of kings. What sense this passage has we explained more fully above, when discussing the little verse, Your sons will come from afar, and your daughters will suck at your side. Or, according to the Seventy, you will eat the riches of kings. These riches, according to the Hebrew truth, are the breasts of kings and teachers, by which the infancy of those born in Christ is instructed and nourished. When you have sucked these and have come to solid food, so that you also eat the riches of such kings, then you will know that I am your Savior, who redeemed you with my blood, or the mighty God of Jacob.

60:17ff.

For bronze I will bring gold, for iron I will bring silver, and for wood bronze, and for stones iron; and I will make your visitation peace, and your overseers righteousness. Iniquity will no more be heard in your land, devastation and destruction in your borders; and salvation will occupy your walls, and praise your gates. LXX: For bronze I will bring you gold, and for iron I will give you silver, and for wood I will grant you bronze, and for stones iron. And I will give your princes in peace, and your bishops in righteousness; and iniquity will no more be heard in your land, nor destruction and misery in your borders; but your walls will be called salvation, and your gates carving. The same thing, according to the nature of its position, is a genus to one, a species to another. And so as not to seem to say anything about the arts of rhetoric and dialectic, I shall give common examples which can instruct the simple reader. My son, who in relation to me is a species and has me as his genus, is a genus to his own son. I shall give another: what is greater to one is smaller to another. A centurion is greater than a common soldier, smaller than a tribune. Five are few compared with ten, many compared with one. So in the restoration of the spiritual Jerusalem, wood will be turned into bronze, and stones will be changed into iron; that is, men once brutish and senseless will be changed into those materials which provide some use to the city. And the bronze and iron themselves, through the increase of virtues, will be changed into gold and silver, so that they have not merely the appearance of usefulness but value as well and beauty. What gold and silver signify in the holy Scriptures we have often said. I will make, he says, your princes in peace, and your bishops in righteousness. For which it is written in the Hebrew: I will make your visitation peace, and your overseers righteousness. Here is the admirable majesty of holy Scripture, that it named the future princes of the Church bishops, all of whose visitation is in peace, and the title of whose dignity is in righteousness: so that they do not respect persons in judgment, and nothing unjust is heard in the land of the Church, nor destruction and unhappiness in her borders. For wherever there is iniquity, and righteousness is not kept, and peace is lost, all these things follow. But instead of all these, he says, salvation will occupy your walls, or the Savior, which in the Hebrew reads JESUS, which properly sounds as the name of the Lord. For he himself is the strength of the walls of the Church, which has her gates in the praise of the Lord, so that those who enter her may first learn to praise the Lord and to confess his name. But as for the Seventy having translated γλύμμα, that is, carving, instead of praise, we can say this: that the gates of the Church, through which we enter her, ought to be engraved with all the virtues.

60:19-20

You will no longer have the sun to give light by day, nor will the brightness of the moon illumine you; but the Lord will be to you an everlasting light, and your God will be your glory. Your sun will no more go down, and your moon will not wane, for the Lord will be an everlasting light, and the days of your mourning will be ended. LXX: And you will no longer have the sun for the light of day, nor will the rising of the moon give you light by night; but the Lord will be to you an eternal light, and God your glory. For the sun will not go down for you, and the moon will not fail you. And the Lord will be an everlasting light, and the days of your mourning will be ended. From this passage we are compelled to refer everything that has been said and is still to be said to the last time, when, as heaven and earth pass away, the office of the sun and the moon will cease, and the Lord himself will be a perpetual light; so that what the χιλιασταὶ assert is to be fulfilled carnally, we believe will come to pass spiritually, differing from them in the nature of the promises, not in the time. To them this must briefly be answered: if for false prophets and sinners the sun goes down at noon, and on the contrary for those who fear the Lord the sun of righteousness rises, why should he not always rise for the saints who says, I am the light of the world (John 8:12), who shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend him (John 1)? For the sun will not burn us by day, nor the moon by night (Ps 120 [121]:6), because we have the Lord as a perpetual light, and the days of our mourning will be ended; we shall by no means be lamenting over the overthrow of Jerusalem, but rejoicing at the building up of the Church. For blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted. Blessed are those who weep, for they shall laugh. Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled (Matt 5). So that, once they have been filled with the flesh of the Lord, they may pour forth the word of the Lord and tell their works to the king (Ps 44 [45]).

60:21-22

And your people will all be righteous; they will inherit the land for ever, the shoot of my planting, the work of my hand, for glorifying. The least will become a thousand, and the little one a very mighty nation. I the Lord will do this suddenly in its time. LXX: Your people, all righteous, will possess the land for ever, keeping the planting, the works of their hands, for glory. He who is small will become thousands, and he who is least a great nation. I the Lord will gather them in time. When the days of mourning are finished and completed, when sorrow will be turned into joy, the people of Zion will be all righteous, not for a short time but for ever; and because it is righteous, it will possess the land of the gentle. Nor is it to be wondered at if, to receive the good things of the promise, it holds the land of the meek and of the living, for which the Prophet sighs, saying: I believe that I shall see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living (Ps 26 [27]:13), since it is the shoot of the Lord's planting and the work of his hands for glorifying God. For every planting, he says, which my heavenly Father has not planted will be rooted up (Matt 15). Or, according to the Seventy, the people that keeps the planting of God and the works of the Lord's hands will be preserved in the glory of the Creator. Of the good planting God speaks through Jeremiah: I planted you a good vine, wholly true, which in Isaiah is called the vine of Sorek (Isa 5). And because Paul, conscious of the virtues of Christ speaking in him, could say, Be imitators of me, as I also am of Christ (1 Cor 11:1), he therefore said to the Corinthians: I planted, Apollos watered, but the Lord gave the increase (1 Cor 3:6). For those planted in the house of the Lord will flourish in his courts (Ps 91 [92]). Then he who was a little one will become thousands, hearing from the Lord: Have authority over five or ten cities (Luke 19:17, 19), so that he is called a χιλίαρχος. And he who had said with the Apostle, To me, the least of all the saints, this grace was given (Eph 3:8), will be prince of a great nation in the heavens, when at the appointed time the Lord sends his angels, and they gather to him all the saints from the height of heaven to its summit (Matt 24): not only from Israel but also from the people of the nations, signifying whom he said: And I have other sheep which are not of this fold, and them also I must gather, that there may be one flock and one shepherd (John 10:16). And he will do this suddenly, so that when everything has been despaired of, then they may be gathered into a very mighty nation. And although we see these things being fulfilled in part daily in the Church, yet they will be more fully fulfilled at the consummation of the world and at the second coming of the Savior.

61:1ff.

The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the meek, to heal the broken in heart, and to preach indulgence to the captives, and opening to those who are shut in; and to proclaim a year of favor to the Lord, and a day of vengeance to our God; to comfort all who mourn; to appoint for those who mourn in Zion, and to give them a crown instead of ashes, the oil of joy instead of mourning, a mantle of praise instead of a spirit of sorrow. LXX: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me; he has sent me to preach the gospel to the poor, to heal the broken in heart, to preach remission to the captives and sight to the blind, to call an acceptable year to the Lord, and a day of retribution, to comfort all who mourn, to give to those who mourn in Zion, to give them glory instead of ashes, the anointing of gladness to those who mourn, a garment of glory instead of a spirit of sorrow. He who said above, I the Lord will gather them in time, or, according to the Hebrew, I the Lord will do this suddenly in its time, says next, The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me: not that the Lord God has a Lord God, but that, according to the dispensation of the flesh he assumed, he speaks the things that are lowly. To him the Psalmist had already said: You have loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of exultation above your fellows (Ps 44 [45]:8). For when fellows are named, understand the nature of the flesh, since God has no fellows of his substance. And because the anointing was spiritual, and by no means of a human body, as it was among the priests of the Jews, he is therefore said to have been anointed above his fellows, that is, the other saints. His anointing was fulfilled at the time when he was baptized in the Jordan, and the Holy Spirit came down upon him in the form of a dove and remained on him (John 1). Of him this same Prophet also said: A rod will come forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower will rise up from its root, and the spirit of God will rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and strength, the spirit of knowledge and godliness (Isa 11:1, 2). Hence the Savior too, after he was baptized in the Jordan, when he had come to Nazareth, where he had been brought up, entered their synagogue on the sabbath day, according to custom; and when he had stood up to read, the book of the prophet Isaiah was given to him, and on opening it he found written: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me; he has sent me to preach the gospel to the poor, to preach remission to the captives and sight to the blind, to set the broken at liberty, to preach the acceptable year of the Lord. Then he rolled up the book, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down; and the eyes of all who were in the synagogue were fixed on him, and he began to say to them: Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your ears; and all bore witness to him, and marveled at the words of grace that came forth from his mouth. If, then, the prophecy was fulfilled at that time, how do some refer what is said here to the times of the consummation? Unless perhaps we can say this: that what was then fulfilled in part is to be fulfilled more fully when the whole people of God will be righteous. For now we know in part and we prophesy in part; but when that which is perfect has come, the things that are in part will be done away (1 Cor 13). He was anointed, then, with the Holy Spirit to bring good news to the poor, or the meek, saying to them in the Gospel: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven (Matt 5:3). And: Blessed are the gentle, for they shall possess the land (ibid., 4). And he was sent to heal those who are broken in heart (Luke 4), and who say: A broken and humbled heart God does not despise (Ps 50 [51]:19). Or, according to Symmachus and Theodotion, to bind up the wounds of sinners, to preach remission to the captives, sight to the blind, or opening to those who are shut in, which Symmachus translated more plainly, release to those in chains. Of whom, or rather to whom, it is said above: Behold, I have set you as a light of the nations, to open the eyes of the blind, to lead out the bound from their chains, and from the prison house those who sit in darkness (Isa 42:6, 7). By the acceptable year and the day of retribution understand the whole time of his preaching, during which he lived in the flesh. This the apostle Paul too interprets of the first coming of the Savior, saying: Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation (2 Cor 6:2). Of this we spoke more fully above (cf. Isa 60). But if retribution is taken not in the rewards of the good but in the punishments of sinners, in accordance with its being called the day of vengeance, it must be understood of the Jewish people, upon whom, after his passion, the wrath of God came at once. And he comforted all who mourn, saying: Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted (Matt 5:5), so that he might appoint for those who mourn in Zion, and give them glory and a crown instead of ashes. Among these was the apostle Paul too, who mourned for Zion and said: For I have sorrow and continual grief (Rom 9:2); and again: I could wish that I myself were anathema from Christ for my brethren and kinsmen according to the flesh, who are Israelites (ibid., 3). And therefore those who mourned and lamented received the oil of joy instead of ashes, seeing that very many of the Jews had believed and were receiving a most pure robe instead of the garment of mourning.

61:3, 5

And in her they will be called the mighty ones of righteousness, the planting of the Lord for glorifying. And they will build the places deserted from of old, and raise up the ancient ruins, and restore the cities deserted and scattered from generation to generation. And strangers will stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of foreigners will be your farmers and vinedressers. LXX: And they will be called generations of righteousness, the planting of the Lord for glory. And they will build the everlasting desert places; those that had formerly been made desolate will be raised up, and they will renew the deserted cities, desolate for generations; and foreigners will come and feed your sheep, and ploughmen and vinedressers of other nations. After both the Apostles and apostolic men have received, instead of ashes and a spirit of sorrow, the oil of joy and the mantle, or, according to the Seventy, the robe of glory and praise, then they will be called generations of righteousness, the glorious planting of the Lord; or, according to the Hebrew ELE (אילי), with both syllables lengthened, mighty ones, and of the righteousness of God, or the planting of the Lord for glorifying; so that, when they have been glorified, or have themselves glorified the Lord, they may build the cities deserted from of old, and raise up the ancient ruins, both of the people of the Jews and of all the nations. They will have not only the skill of building and restoring cities, but they will also be the best of shepherds, so that, the old shepherds being driven away, to whom God had said through Ezekiel, O shepherds of Israel, do shepherds feed themselves, and not rather the sheep (Ezek 34:2)?, they may hear with the apostle Peter: Feed my sheep (John 21:17). And in a wonderful manner they will pass from masons and shepherds to farmers, that is, to ploughmen and vinedressers, so that they may say with the Apostle: We are God's building, God's husbandry (1 Cor 3:9). Thus the Savior asks the scribes and Pharisees, the vinedressers and farmers of the Jews, what he will do to the wicked vinedressers and farmers; and when they answered, He will destroy the wicked wickedly, and give the vineyard to other farmers (Matt 21:41), he went on: The kingdom of God will be taken from you and given to a nation producing its fruits (ibid., 43). The matter needs no interpretation. For how few of the princes of the churches are from the Jews, and not from foreigners and men of outside nations! Formerly serving idols, and strangers to the testament of God and aliens from his promises, having no hope and without God in the world, they now preside over the churches, and with the plough of faith they tame the hard and formerly untamed hearts of the Gentiles to bear fruit, so that they may multiply the seed of the Lord's doctrine with an abundance of good works.

61:6-7

But you will be called the priests of the Lord; it will be said to you, ministers of our God. You will eat the strength of the nations, and you will pride yourselves in their glory. Instead of your double confusion and shame they will praise their portion; therefore in their land they will possess double things; everlasting gladness will be theirs; for I am the Lord who loves judgment, and hates robbery in burnt offering. LXX: But you will be called the priests of the Lord, ministers of our God. You will eat the strength of the nations, and in their riches you will be admirable. Thus they will possess the land a second time, and everlasting joy will be upon their head. For I am the Lord who love righteousness and hate robberies from iniquity. The builders of the deserted cities and the shepherds of the flocks, who are themselves the ploughmen and vinedressers, that is, the sons of foreigners, are themselves also the priests of God, to whom the Prophet now says: But you will be called the priests of the Lord, and it will be said to you, ministers of our God: there is no doubt that he means the princes of the churches. Or certainly it is to be understood of the Apostles, so that the order is: When masons, shepherds, ploughmen and vinedressers from the nations have been set over the churches, you, of whom it was said, A remnant will be saved (Rom 9:27), and, Unless the Lord Sabaoth had left us a seed, we should have been as Sodom, and should have been like Gomorrah (Isa 1:9), will be called priests and ministers of God, such as the sons of David also were, of whom Scripture says: And the sons of David were priests of God (2 Sam 8:18). These will eat the strength of the nations, and in their riches they will be admirable. For the crown of fathers is the glory of their children, and the progress of the people is the feast of the priests (Prov 17). Of riches of this kind Paul wrote to the Corinthians: I give thanks to my God through Jesus Christ that in everything you have been made rich in him, in all speech and in all knowledge, even as the testimony of Christ has been confirmed in you, so that you lack nothing in any grace (1 Cor 1:4ff.). The strength of the nations is the triumph of the Martyrs, and we are proud in their glory, not with that pride which lies in vice, which God resists, that he may give grace to the humble, but with that which is taken for power and glory (Jas 4). Hence Moses too had a horned face (Exod 34), who could say: In you we shall toss our enemies with the horn (Ps 43 [44]:6). And for the pride of glory Aquila translated καὶ ἐν δόξῃ αὐτῶν πορφύρᾳ ἐνδύσεσθαι, that is, you will be clothed in purple, to show the badge of royal splendor. And what follows, Instead of double confusion and instead of shame they will praise their portion, which is not found in the Seventy, I think should be explained thus: Because you had a double confusion, both over the people of the Jews, which had departed from God, and over the nations, which served idols, you will see them, converted to the fear of God, praising their portion: without doubt the Lord, of whom the holy man also spoke: My portion is the Lord (Ps 72 [73]:26). No one can say this except one who has no other portion. Because, then, you had over them a double confusion and the shame of their sin, over which they themselves did not blush, therefore in their land, that is, in the land of the gentle and of the living, they will possess double things, since they will have believed both in the things present and in the things to come. And they will have everlasting gladness. For which we read in the Seventy, thus they will possess the land a second time. And everlasting joy will be upon their head, so that those who had possessed the land within the very narrow borders of Judea afterwards possess the whole world. Of this land the Father speaks to the Savior: Ask of me, and I will give you the nations for your inheritance, and the ends of the earth for your possession (Ps 2:8). This the Lord has granted, who loves the truth of judgment and hates robbery in burnt offering. For which the Seventy translated robbery from iniquity, as though there were some robbery that did not consist of iniquity. What he says, then, is this: God loves the poverty of the righteous more than the gifts of the rich, which come from robberies and iniquity.

61:8-9

And I will give their work in truth, and I will strike an everlasting covenant with them. And their seed will be known among the nations, and their offspring in the midst of the peoples. All who see them will recognize them, that these are the seed which the Lord has blessed. LXX: And I will give their labor to the righteous, and I will set an eternal testament with them. And their seed will be known among the nations, and their descendants in the midst of the peoples. Everyone who sees them will recognize them, that these are the seed blessed by God. God, who loves righteousness and judgment and detests violent burnt offerings (for whatever comes from robbery he reckons as the hire of a harlot and the price of a dog), will himself give the labor of those who will possess the land a second time, and whom he will have crowned with a double gladness, to the righteous, or, as is better in the Hebrew, in truth: so that it is no longer, as in the Law, the shadow of the truth, but the truth itself. And he will strike an everlasting covenant, not such as he had given to Moses, which has passed away, but the covenant of the Gospel, of which Christ speaks: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away (Matt 24:35). And then the apostolic seed will be known among the nations, and all future generations will receive the sowing of God's doctrine; by no means saying that in which the people of the circumcision formerly erred, saying: For what else does God seek but seed? Everyone who sees them will recognize at first sight that they are the seed which the Lord has blessed. For who would not recognize the people of God from their manner of life, their gentleness, continence, hospitality and all their virtues? And who, on the contrary, would not detest the bloody hands of Israel, against whom the Prophet prays, saying: Fill their faces with shame, O Lord (Ps 82 [83]:17)?

61:10-11

Rejoicing I will rejoice in the Lord, and there has exulted my soul in my God: for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, and with the vesture of righteousness he has encompassed me, as a bridegroom adorned with a crown, and as a bride decked with her jewels. For as the earth brings forth its shoot, and as a garden makes its seed spring up, so the Lord God will make righteousness and praise spring up before all the nations. LXX: With joy they will be glad in the Lord; let my soul exult in the Lord. For he has clothed me with the garment of salvation, and has put about me the tunic of gladness. As a bridegroom with a mitre, and as a bride he has adorned me with a woman's finery, and as the earth putting forth its flower, and as a garden makes its seeds spring up, so the Lord God brings forth righteousness and praise in the sight of all the nations. The beginning of the passage according to the Seventy, who said, With joy they will be glad in the Lord, is joined to the end of the preceding passage. But according to the Hebrews it is the opening of another section, in which the Church is brought in answering the words of Christ: Rejoicing I will rejoice in the Lord, and my soul will exult in my God: by no means in the fathers, as the Jews gloried, saying, We are the seed of Abraham, and have never been slaves to anyone (John 8:33), but in God, as Scripture says: Now the multitude of the believers had one heart and one soul (Acts 4:32). And she gives the reasons for her gladness: For he has clothed me with the garment of salvation, and with the vesture, or tunic, of righteousness and gladness, which in Hebrew is called MAIL (מעיל), he has adorned and encompassed me. For as many of us as have been baptized in Christ put on Christ, and have the tunic of righteousness, who has been made for us holiness, righteousness and redemption (Gal 1). And she sets forth a likeness of two companies in the Church, the perfect and the beginners (1 Cor 1). The perfect she compares to the beauty of the bridegroom; the beginners she likens to the adornment of the bride. Paul was perfect, who, like a bridegroom adorned with a crown and to be crowned, or, as Aquila translated, ἱερατευμένος στεφάνῳ, which in our language is bearing a crown as a priest, said by the authority of Christ speaking in him: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the course, I have kept the faith; for the rest, there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness (2 Tim 4:7). And in another place: As many of us, then, as are perfect, let us be thus minded (Phil 3:15). But he was a beginner in comparison with fullness, when he spoke in the person of beginners: When I was a little child, I spoke as a little child, I understood as a little child, I thought as a little child (1 Cor 13:11). And again: We see in part and we know in part, until that which is perfect comes (ibid., 9). And therefore he is likened to the adornment of the bride, who is adorned with a woman's finery, or, as the others translated, with vessels, or with her jewels. And she sets forth examples of another comparison, of which the first refers to the bridegroom, the next to the bride. As the earth brings forth its shoot and is watered by the rains of heaven, and as a garden makes its seed spring up, which longs for the waters of springs and rivers, so, he says, the Lord will make righteousness and gladness spring up before all the nations: by no means before Israel, so as to strike down the haughtiness of the Jews, but before all the nations, which are gathered in the Church.

62:1ff.

For Zion's sake I will not be silent, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, until her righteous one goes forth as brightness, and her savior is kindled as a lamp. And the nations will see your righteous one, and all kings your renowned one, and a new name will be called for you, which the mouth of the Lord has named. And you will be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord, and a diadem of the kingdom in the hand of your God. LXX: For Zion's sake I will not be silent, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not leave off, until her righteousness goes forth as light, and her salvation burns as a lamp. And the nations will see your righteousness, and all kings your glory, and he will call you by a new name, which the mouth of the Lord will name. And you will be a crown of beauty in the hand of the Lord, and a diadem of the kingdom in the hand of your God. The Lord and Savior had said, The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me (Luke 4:18), up to the place where it is written, All who see them will recognize them, that these are the seed which the Lord has blessed (Isa 61:1). After this promise the Church answered, Rejoicing I will rejoice in the Lord, she who in the third of the Psalms of the Steps, in the person of the repentant people, sang joyfully: I rejoiced at the things that were said to me: we shall go into the house of the Lord (Ps 121 [122]:1). Now the person of the prophet is brought in, saying: For Zion's sake I will not be silent, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest. By day and by night, he says, I will not close my mouth, nor will my prayer ever be silent; but I will cry out so long, and join prayers to prayers, until he who was promised comes and enlightens the whole world with his brightness. Who it is whom he seeks, whose coming he longs for, he puts more plainly: Until her righteous one goes forth as brightness, and her savior is kindled as a lamp. Or, according to the Seventy: Until her righteousness goes forth as light, and her salvation burns as a lamp: the light which said in the Gospel, I am the light of the world (John 8:12); which, when it has been kindled in Zion and in Jerusalem, will by no means shine in Judea alone, but it will be said to her: The light that is in you has been kindled; the light that went forth from the Father has begun to burn within your borders, and it will enlighten all the nations (Matt 6). And all kings will see your renowned one, O Jerusalem and Zion: he who was begotten of your stock, who, lifted up in you on the gibbet, drew all men to himself; so that the nations see his righteousness, by which the Creator of all has had mercy on the nations, and kings his glory, by which he was glorified on the cross and subjected all kingdoms to his rule. Indeed she will no longer be called Jerusalem and Zion, but she will receive a new name, which the Lord will have given her, saying to the apostle Peter: You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of hell will not prevail against it (Matt 16:18). This title he derived from the name of the Lord, so that she is called the Lord's. And her people will no longer be called by the old name, Israel, but by a new one, that is, Christian. And she will be as a crown of beauty in the hand of the Lord, and as a diadem of the kingdom in the hand of her God, when the throng of believers has crowned her, and the diadem of empire, which the Martyrs have adorned with the variety of their gems, is in the hand of God, that he may crown his Son with their victories. Hence the apostle Paul too said to the saints: My joy and my crown.

62:4

You will no longer be called Forsaken, and your land will no more be called Desolate; but you will be called My-will-is-in-her, and your land Inhabited, for the Lord has been well pleased in you, and your land will be inhabited. LXX: And you will no longer be called Forsaken, and your land will not be called Deserted any more. For you will be called My will, and your land Inhabited. Instead of Zion and Jerusalem you will be called the Church and the Lord's; instead of Jews they will be called Christians. Nor will you be content with this end of names; but you who before were called forsaken, which in Hebrew is AZUBA (עזובה), will be called EPESI-BA (חפצי־בה), which means my will is in her; and your land, which before was called SEMEMA (שממה), desolate or deserted, will afterwards be called BULA (בעולה), which Aquila translated ἐσχημένη, Symmachus and Theodotion συνωκισμένη, the Seventy οἰκουμένη, all of which signify inhabited and possessed. It is a custom of the Hebrews always to give names to things from what befalls them: as Abram, who was first called high father, when he heard the promise, And in your seed all the nations will be blessed (Gen 12:3), was named father of many nations, that is, Abraham. And above, a name is given to the Lord Savior: Quickly take the spoils, swiftly plunder (Isa 8:1). The sons of Zebedee too, one of whom could utter the voice of thunder (Mark 3), In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God (John 1:1), were called BANEREEM (בני רעם), which means sons of thunder. But what follows, For the Lord has been well pleased in you, and your land will be inhabited, has been passed over by the Seventy; and it gives the reasons why she is called EPHSI (חפצי) and why she is called BULA (בעולה): because the Lord has been well pleased in Zion, and has made habitable her land, which before had been deserted through the error of the Jews. Or we may refer this same thing to the Church, which, possessed before by idols, had been deserted by God.

62:5

For the young man will dwell with the virgin, and your sons will dwell in you. And the bridegroom will rejoice over the bride; your God will rejoice over you. LXX: And as a young man dwelling with a virgin, so will your sons dwell. And it will be that as a bridegroom is glad over a bride, so the Lord will be glad over you. The Apostle too says: Husbands, love your wives, as Christ also loved the Church (Eph 5:25). And when in another place he had set down the example, For this reason a man will leave his father and mother, and will cleave to his wife, and the two will be in one flesh, he added: This is a great mystery; but I speak in Christ and in the Church (Eph 5:31, 32). If, then, because of the shortness of the time, which is straitened, husbands ought so to have their wives as though they had them not, how much more holy will the union between the bridegroom and the bride be? This is the bridegroom of whom it is sung in the eighteenth psalm: And he as a bridegroom coming forth from his chamber (Ps 18 [19]:6). And this is the bride who is written of quite often in the Song of Songs, who has neither wrinkle nor spot (Song 4); whom Paul longs to present as a chaste virgin to one husband, so that she may be holy in body and spirit (1 Cor 2). Of her also, under the title of the beloved, the forty-fourth psalm sings: The queen stood at your right hand in gilded clothing, surrounded with variety (verse 10). As, then, the bridegroom rejoices in the bride, and the young man with the virgin, examples in which there is a holy union, so the Lord will be glad in her whose names have been changed.

62:6-7

Upon your walls, Jerusalem, I have set watchmen; all the day and all the night they will never be silent. You who remember the Lord, do not be silent, and give him no silence, until he establishes, and until he makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth. LXX: And upon your walls, Jerusalem, I have set watchmen, all the day and all the night, who will never be silent, remembering the Lord: for there is none like you if he corrects, and he will make Jerusalem a joy upon the earth. The Prophet had said, For Zion's sake I will not be silent, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, and the rest, up to the place where the passage has now ended: The bridegroom will rejoice over the bride; your God will rejoice over you. And he had promised that he would pray by day and by night that the Savior and Righteous One who had been promised might come and, like a lamp, light up the whole world. After this is brought in the person of God speaking to Jerusalem, that is, to the Church of the firstborn, and to her that was built in the Apostles and through the Apostles: Upon your walls I have set watchmen, whom we can take to be either the angels, or the Apostles and all her princes and teachers. They guard the walls of the Church, so that our adversary the devil, who as a roaring lion goes about and seeks how he may enter (1 Pet 5), may not find an occasion for laying waste the Lord's flock. These watchmen ought not to be silent by day or by night, neither in glad times nor in sad, but ought always to entreat the Lord's mercy, so that his flock and the walls of Jerusalem may be guarded and fortified by his help. Hence the word is directed to these same watchmen and teachers: O you who remember the Lord, and weary his mercy with your prayers day and night, take care that prayer is never silent in your mouth. Give him no silence, understand: the Lord; but be always troublesome, in season, out of season, and imitate the woman who importuned the hard judge. For if he laid aside the fierceness of his mind because of constant entreaty, how much more will the heavenly Father give good things to those who ask him? And you ought to ask for as long as it takes until Jerusalem, which fell in the Jews and is become an example and a curse, is turned into the praise of the whole world. And I wonder what the Seventy meant, instead of what is in the Hebrew, give him no silence, until he establishes and makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth, by saying what does not cohere in sense with what precedes: For there is none like you, if he corrects, and makes Jerusalem a joy upon the earth. Unless perhaps we fit it together with artful speech, so that it is said to the watchmen of the Church that there will be none like those who by their preaching have brought it about that Jerusalem is corrected and becomes the joy of the whole earth.

62:8-9

The Lord has sworn by his right hand and by the arm of his strength: If I give your wheat any more as food to your enemies, and if the sons of strangers drink your wine, for which you have labored! For those who gather it will eat it and praise the Lord, and those who bring it in will drink it in my holy courts. LXX: The Lord has sworn by his right hand and by the strength of his arm: If I give my wheat any more to be food for your enemies, and if the sons of strangers drink any more your wine for which you have labored! But those who have gathered will eat it and praise the Lord, and those who have gathered will drink it in my holy courts. Almighty God, who had said to the Church, Upon your walls I have set watchmen, who will never be silent, and whom I bid never to cease praying until they obtain what they pray for, now swears by his right hand and the arm of his strength. Of this we have often said that it is our Lord and Savior, who according to the Apostle is the power of God and the wisdom of God (1 Cor 1). And he swears that the wheat and wine of Jerusalem will by no means go to be food for enemies, nor will foreigners enjoy her labor; but whoever have sown in tears will reap in joy, and those who have harvested, and, the chaff cast away, have gathered the pure grain into the barns, will themselves eat the labors of their hands, and extol the Lord with everlasting praise, and drink the wine in his holy courts. By these we understand either the many mansions with the Father, if we take it of the future blessedness in the kingdom of heaven, or certainly the churches spread throughout the whole world, in which we are planted, and afterwards shall flourish in the house of the Lord. And when he says, I will by no means give your wheat any more to your enemies, and foreigners will not drink your wine for which you have labored, he shows that the labor of the Jews and all their works were formerly possessed by demons, when they wavered between God and idols, when Elijah said to them: How long do you limp on both feet? If the Lord is God, follow him (1 Kgs 18:21). And according to the typical history which is narrated in the book of Judges, the Midianites came and laid waste its fruits as far as Gaza, so that the food of men was turned into the fodder of brute beasts (Judg 6). Now this is the wheat and this the wine which they will not eat except praising the Lord, and will not drink except in his holy courts; of which the Lord said in his passion: Amen, amen, I say to you, I will not drink of the fruit of this vine until I drink it new in the kingdom of my Father (Mark 14:25). These things are fulfilled in part in the Church, when the Lord says to his disciples: Drink, my friends, and be inebriated, brethren, for wine gladdens the heart of man (Ps 103 [104]). And it is drunk in full light and at midday by Joseph with his brothers (Gen 43). And it will be fulfilled more fully when the earth is inebriated with the blessings of the Lord. The wheat too, from which the heavenly bread is made, is that of which the Lord speaks: My flesh is truly food. And again of the wine: And my blood is truly drink (John 6).

62:10, 12

Pass through, pass through the gates, prepare the way for the people, make the road level, and pick out the stones; lift up a signal to the peoples. Behold, the Lord has made it heard at the ends of the earth: say to the daughter of Zion, Behold, your Savior comes; behold, his reward is with him, and his work before him. And they will call them a holy people, redeemed by the Lord. But you will be called a city sought out, and not forsaken. LXX: Go through my gates, and make a way for my people, and throw the stones off the way. Lift up a signal to the nations; for behold, the Lord has made it heard to the end of the earth. Say to the daughter of Zion: Behold, your Savior comes, having his reward with him, and his work before his face; and he will call it a holy people, redeemed by the Lord. But you will be called a city sought after, and not forsaken. He commanded the watchmen of the walls of Jerusalem, whom he had commanded before not to be silent and never to cease praying, to pass through the gates of Jerusalem and make a way for the people. This the half-Jews contend will come to pass in the last time, when, after the fullness of the nations, Israel is to be saved and return to the Lord. Others think it is to be fulfilled in the kingdom of heaven, when there will be true gladness, and each will receive according to his merit, and they will by no means see the Lord in humility, but will perceive him in the guise of a judge, when he comes upon the clouds with a multitude of angels to render to each according to his work. But we, following the explanation we have begun, can understand these things of the first coming as well, so as to say that the Apostles and apostolic men are commanded to go in and pass through the gates against which hell does not prevail, and to remove every hindrance from the way, so that the people may enter the Church of the Savior without any stumbling block. Hence John too cried in the wilderness: I am the voice of one crying in the desert, as Isaiah said: Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight; every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be brought low (John 1:23; cf. Isa 40:3, 4). And the same sense is now expressed in other words. The churchman chooses the stones, who softens all hardness from the heart of believers; of whom the same Baptist said: God is able from these stones to raise up sons to Abraham (Matt 3:9). Or, according to the Seventy, he throws the stones off the way who separates the unbelieving from the believers. And lest the Jews should think this was said of themselves, there is joined to it: Lift up a signal to the nations, and to the peoples of the Gentiles, so that it is not the narrow confines of the one land of Judea that are called to salvation, but the message is made heard at the ends of the earth, so that the whole world may hear of the passion of the Creator of all. Say, he says, to the daughter of Zion. She is called the daughter of Zion either because she first arose from the Jews, she of whom it says in the Song of Songs, The sons of my mother have fought against me (Song 1:5); or certainly she is called daughter because she received from God the name of adoption. For as many as received him, to them he gave power to become sons of God (John 1). And what is it that the masters and teachers are bidden to announce to the daughter of Zion? Behold, your Savior comes, who in the Hebrew is called Jesus. Hence Gabriel too, to Joseph: And you will call, he says, his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins (Matt 1:21). This Savior is the judge of all believers, to render to each according to his works: to the righteous rewards, to sinners everlasting punishments (Matt 16). And he will call, he says, them, the Lord and Savior himself. Or, according to the Hebrew, they will call them, the Apostles and apostolic men, a holy people, and redeemed by the Lord, who have been redeemed by the blood of Christ. The city itself too will by no means be called forsaken, as she had been called before, whether among the Jews because of their trafficking, or among the nations because of their idolatry, but sought after, as it is said in Hebrew DRUSA (דרושת); so that, according to the growth and variety of their virtues, they may always receive new names.

63:1

Who is this who comes from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? This one, beautiful in his robe, marching in the greatness of his strength. LXX: Who is this who comes from Edom, with tawny garments from Bosor? So beautiful in his robe, violence with strength. This whole passage, from the place where according to the Seventy it is said, Be enlightened, be enlightened, Jerusalem, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you (Isa 60:1), up to the present passage, where it is said, Who is this who comes from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah?, many of our people refer to the end of the world, in which they contend these things are to be fulfilled, whether carnally or spiritually (for the opinion of most is divided). But we, since we read above in this same section too, The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the poor, which the Lord and Savior, having read the volume of Isaiah in the synagogue of the Jews, showed to be fulfilled in himself, saying, Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your ears (Luke 4:21); and since it is now said of the same one that after his passion he ascended to the Father bloodied, we are compelled by necessity to take everything that is said of the first coming of the Savior. For it cannot be, as most of our people strive to make it, that things joined together in the works should be divided in time. Nor do we deny that it is a task of the greatest toil to join all these things together, and so to show that they are to be fulfilled spiritually at the consummation as to teach that they have already been fulfilled in Christ both according to the flesh and according to the spirit. Since, then, the Savior has come to the daughter of Zion, whose reward is with him and his work before him; and the righteous one has gone forth as brightness, and the Savior has been kindled as a lamp; and the bridegroom has rejoiced over his bride the Church, nay rather her God has exulted over her, who is himself both bridegroom and Lord: therefore, according to the assumption of the flesh and the passion of the cross, it is said to him: That your foot may be dipped in blood (Ps 67 [68]:24). And under the name of Judah it is prophesied in Genesis: Judah, your brothers will praise you; your hands will be on the necks of your enemies (Gen 49:8ff.), the sons of your father will worship you. Judah is a lion's whelp; to the prey, my son, you have gone up; resting, you have couched as a lion, and as a lioness: who will rouse him (Gen 49:8, 9)? And again: Binding his foal to the vineyard, and his she-ass, O my son, to the vine, he will wash his robe in wine, and his cloak in the blood of the grape (ibid., 11). This is he whom the angelic powers, seeing him ascend bloodied to the Father, command the other angels, and hear from them: Lift up your gates, O princes, and be lifted up, O everlasting gates, and the king of glory will come in. Who is this king of glory? The Lord strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle (Ps 23 [24]:7, 8). And again: The Lord of hosts, he is the king of glory (ibid., 10). We have set this down beforehand to show that the present passage too agrees with the other testimonies. Hence it is said in the Song of Songs too: My kinsman is ruddy and white (Song 5:10): ruddy in the passion, white in the resurrection. The angels, then, terrified by the strangeness of the thing (for the mystery of the passion and resurrection of Christ, according to the apostle Paul (1 Cor 2), had been unknown to all past generations), ask: Who is this who comes bloodied from the land of Edom? For EDOM (אדם) is expressed in our language as both earthly and bloody. With dyed garments from Bozrah? Many, falling into a pious error, think this is to be understood of the Lord's flesh, that is, BASAR (בשר); but if this word signified flesh, it would be written with the letter SIN in the middle, whereas now it is written with SADE, and means strong and fortified. This we take either of Jerusalem (Ps 59 [60]:11), which formerly was surrounded with very strong walls, in which the Lord suffered; or of hell, of which it is written in the fifty-ninth and in the hundred and seventh psalm: Who will lead me into the fortified city (Ps 107 [108]:11)? in which the souls of the dead are shut up, and which is surrounded with very strong guards. It must be known also that according to the history BOSRA (בצרה) is not in Edom but in Moab. There follows: So beautiful in his robe, marching in the greatness of his strength. Of him the forty-fourth psalm too sings: Beautiful in comeliness above the sons of men. Gird your sword upon your thigh, O most mighty. In your comeliness and your beauty set out, proceed prosperously, and reign (Ps 44 [45]:3-5). For which the Seventy translated, violence with strength. What sense this has, let the prudent reader inquire.

I who speak righteousness, and am a champion to save. LXX: I who speak righteousness, and the judgment of salvation. The Lord answered the angels who asked: Do you ask who I am, who ascend bloodied to the heavens, and that the blood with which I am sprinkled has given me not unsightliness but beauty? I am he to whom the Father has given all judgment (John 5). Of him the Psalmist too said: O God, give your judgment to the king, and your righteousness to the king's son (Ps 71 [72]:1). I who speak righteousness, so as to repay evil to the evil and good to the good; who came to fight against the adverse powers, and to preach remission to the captives, and to free the bound from prison, so that the adversaries may feel punishment and the captives liberty.

63:2

Why then is your clothing red, and your garments like those of men treading the winepress? LXX: Why are your garments red, and your clothing like that of men treading the winepress, full and trodden down? Where it now says red, the Hebrew reads EDOM (אדום). So above too, where Edom is written, it is not the name of a place but a word for blood. And again the angels ask and say: We have learned that you are he who speaks righteousness, and that the salvation of all has been placed in your judgment. Now we wish to know why your garments are as if dyed with new wine; or what cause there was for you to stain with blood the tunic that was woven from the top and cannot be torn, and that had from the virgin's womb such whiteness as no fuller on earth could make? For mercy befits you more than cruelty, whiteness more than gore. To them the Lord answered, not with one little verse as before, but with many words, so as to teach everything to those who did not know, lest they be compelled to ask again.

63:3ff.

I have trodden the winepress alone, and of the nations there is no man with me. I have trodden them in my fury, and trampled them in my wrath; and their blood has been sprinkled upon my garments, and I have polluted all my clothing For the day of vengeance is in my heart; the year of my redemption has come. I looked round, and there was no helper; I sought, and there was none to give aid. And my own arm saved for me, and my indignation itself helped me. And I trampled the peoples in my fury, and made them drunk in my indignation, and brought down their strength to the earth. The Seventy, instead of what we have said, I have trodden the winepress alone, translated full and trodden down, which is rather to be read with the preceding passage than taken as the beginning of the following one. The rest they translated thus: And of the nations there is no man with me; and I trampled them in my fury, and broke them like earth, and brought down their blood to the earth, and I have defiled all my garments. For the day of retribution has come upon them, and the year of redemption is at hand. I looked, and there was no helper; I considered, and there was none to give aid; and my arm rescued them, and my fury came on, and I trampled them in my wrath, and brought down their blood to the earth. For the winepress, which in Hebrew is called GETH (גת), Theodotion set down the Hebrew word itself, PHURA (פורה). But Symmachus is better in this place, and we have followed him. For the word PHURA is ambiguous, and generally signifies both winepress and flask. Something must be said, then, about the winepress: that according to the custom of holy Scripture it is sometimes put for the vengeance and punishment of sinners, sometimes for the gathering of new fruits. It is put for penalties and torments when Jeremiah, lamenting the overthrow of Jerusalem in Lamentations, says: The Lord has trodden the winepress for the virgin daughter of Judah; therefore I weep (Lam 1:15, 16). In a good sense the eighth and the eighty-third psalms are inscribed 'for the winepresses'. Of these we shall speak in their own places, if life goes with us, the Lord granting it. This winepress, in which both punishments for the evil and rewards for the good are trodden out by the Savior, he alone trod, and he had no helper. For neither angel nor archangel, Thrones, Dominions, nor any of the heavenly powers assumed a human body, and suffered for us, and trampled and crushed the adverse powers, but only he who speaks in the psalm: Save me, O Lord, for the holy one has failed (Ps 11 [12]:1); so much so that even the most confident apostle Peter, most firm in the truth of faith, fled terrified with fear, nay even denied the Lord (Matt 27). And what follows, And their blood has been sprinkled upon my garments, and I have polluted all my clothing, must by no means be understood as though we believed that demons and the adverse powers have blood; but everything is to be taken tropologically, when the most merciful God, in order to instruct his people and free them from the bonds of captivity, is compelled to strike the enemies. For the day of vengeance, he says, is in my heart; the year of my redemption has come. Of this we read above too (cf. Isa 61), in a good sense, to preach the acceptable year of the Lord and the day of retribution to our God; and now it is taken both in a bad and in a good sense. In a bad sense: For the day of vengeance is in my heart. In a good sense: The year of my redemption has come; so that at the time when the adversaries are punished, the people of God might be set free, nay rather redeemed by the precious blood of the Lamb, who in the Apocalypse of John is said to have been slain. Of this day of retribution Moses too prophesied by the Holy Spirit: And he will render vengeance to his enemies, and will repay those who hate him. I looked round, and there was no helper; I sought, and there was none to give aid (Deut 32:41). He had also said in the psalm: And I looked for one who would grieve with me, and there was none, and for one who would comfort me, and I found none (Ps 68 [69]:21). For he, though he was in the form of God, did not count it robbery to be equal with God, but emptied himself (Phil 2), taking the form of a servant, and became obedient to the Father unto death, even the death of the cross; and therefore he gave him a name above every name, so that he might save for himself by his right hand those who believe in him, and his indignation, which was against the adversaries, might set the people of God free. Or he rescued the believers by his arm, and no longer put off his fury; and he brought down their blood to the earth, either that of the demons, τροπικῶς, or certainly the blood of the Jews; for which the other translators rendered contention; who strove with all zeal that they might let the bound people go.

63:7

I will remember the mercies of the Lord, the praise of the Lord for all that the Lord has rendered to us, and for the multitude of good things to the house of Israel, which he has bestowed on them according to his indulgence and according to the multitude of his mercies. LXX: I have remembered the mercy of the Lord; I will remember the mighty works of the Lord in all that he has rendered to us: the Lord, a good judge to the house of Israel, will repay us according to his mercy and according to the multitude of his righteousness. Now that the passage on the coming of the Savior has been completed, the first coming, as we judge, the second, as most suppose, in which is understood the voice of one judging, nay rather fighting and slaughtering the adversaries of himself and of his people, and in which he is described as bloodied and victorious, another περικοπή begins, in which the Prophet speaks in the person of the people, recounting God's benefits toward it and the hardness of its own heart, on account of which Jerusalem was given over to burning and Israel to captivity. This the Jews refer to the Babylonian times. But we have shown by order and by reason that it is said of the present time, in which they serve the Romans, and Israel having been shut out, the crowd of the nations has taken its place. Let us run, then, through each member of the discourse, and set them forth briefly, so that the exposition may not be rambling. Pressed by the weight of evils, I have hope in nothing else but in the mercy of God, who shows mercy to thousands of those who love him, and extends his mercy to those who know him. From this it is shown that the mercy of the Lord comes to the aid of those who love and know God. For it is not of him who wills, nor of him who runs, but of God who shows mercy (Rom 9). And unless the Lord builds the house and guards the city, he who builds and guards it watches in vain (Ps 126 [127]). For he himself will grant strength, so that we may do valiantly and be able to say: My strength and my help, and my refuge in the day of my evils (Jer 16). These evils in the present place we ought to take not for vices and sins but for distresses. And as for what follows according to the Seventy, I will remember the mighty works of the Lord in all that he has repaid me, for which the Hebrew contains the praises of the Lord, let us understand signs and miracles, for which 'mighty works' is often put, as there: My glory I will not give to another, nor my mighty works to graven images (Isa 42:8). And elsewhere: They will proclaim his mighty works in the islands, that is, either to the nations of the whole world, or to the churches, which are founded on a firm mass, and are struck rather than overthrown. Sometimes virtue is by no means taken for strength and miracles, but for good conduct, as in that saying of the Apostles, of Peter: Supply virtue in your knowledge (2 Pet 1:5); and of Paul: If there is any virtue, and if any praise (Phil 4:8). In accordance with which it is said in another place too: Better is barrenness with virtue. The first understanding of virtue befits God, the second men. And instead of what we have translated, For all that the Lord has rendered to us, which can be taken both in a good and in a bad sense, Symmachus set it down more plainly as a repayment of good things, saying: For all things in which he has done good to us, and for the multitude of goodness which he has shown toward the house of Israel. For which the Seventy translated: The Lord, a good judge to the house of Israel, has repaid us according to his mercy and according to the multitude of his righteousness. No one can say this except one who understands that he justly bears what he suffers. Thus in the seventy-second psalm, whose opening is, How good is the God of Israel to those who are upright in heart, the prophet speaks in the person of those who are troubled by the judgments of God: But my feet were almost moved, my steps had well nigh slipped, seeing the peace of sinners, and the rest, up to the end of the psalm. Hence the apostle Paul, who had known the Lord as a good and righteous judge, speaks with confidence: There is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, which the righteous judge will render to me; and not to me only, but also to all who love the coming of our Lord and Savior (2 Tim 4:8). Nor is there any difference, as the heretics would have it, between good and righteous, for the same Apostle writes: So the law is holy, and the commandment holy and righteous and good (Rom 7:12), so that goodness is understood as the genus and righteousness as the species. Wherefore he writes to the Romans: For scarcely will anyone die for a righteous man; for perhaps for a good man someone would dare to die (Rom 5:7).

63:8ff.

And he said: Surely they are my people, sons who do not deny; and he became their Savior. In all their tribulation he was not troubled, and the Angel of his face saved them; in his love and in his indulgence he himself redeemed them, and he bore them and lifted them up all the days of the age. But they provoked him to anger and afflicted the spirit of his Holy One and he was turned to be their enemy, and he himself fought them down. LXX: And he said: Is it not my people? Sons will by no means reject. And he became their salvation out of all their tribulation; not an envoy nor an angel, but he himself saved them, because he loved them and spared them; he himself redeemed them, and took them up, and exalted them all the days of the age. But they did not believe, and they embittered his Holy Spirit; he was turned to be their enemy, he himself fought against them. Where we have translated, In all their tribulation he was not troubled, the word which in Hebrew is LO, and is an adverb of negation, for not, can also be read as he himself, so that the sense is: In all their tribulation he himself was troubled, that is, God; so that he himself bore not only our sins but also our tribulations. For he bears our infirmities and grieves for us. Further, the Seventy put down something else which is not found in the Hebrew, not an envoy nor an angel, but he himself saved them, of which we shall speak in its place. So God, who is a righteous judge to the house of Israel, and who tempers the severity of righteousness with the mercy of one who judges, said: I have begotten sons and exalted them, and they have spurned me. Yet because they are my people, and have once been named sons, they will not perish for ever; if they cease to spurn and deny me, they will find a Savior, because in all their tribulation he himself was troubled. Or, he was not troubled, so that he forsook them for a little while, and compelled them, stripped of his help, to pray. Or certainly, he by no means troubled them, but on the contrary, when others persecuted them, he was their helper, and sent his angel to free them from danger. Or, according to the Seventy, he did not wish to save his people through angels and prophets and other holy men, but he himself came down to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, to carry back the sick sheep on his shoulders, and to find the drachma that had been lost, and to run joyfully to meet the prodigal son as he returned. For this reason the bride says in the Song of Songs: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: not through the Patriarchs, Moses and the Prophets, but let him assume my body, let him dwell in my flesh, let the Word become flesh, and so let him kiss me, dwelling in me, that he may be Emmanuel. Not as an envoy, then, nor as an angel, but he himself will save those who have received salvation, not by the merit of their works but by the love of God. For God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life. But if the prudent reader should answer in silent thought, Why have many not been saved, if he himself saved them, and loved and spared his sons, and redeemed them with his blood, and took them up and exalted them once assumed?, a clear reason is given: But they did not believe, and they embittered his Holy Spirit, or the Spirit of his Holy One, which in Hebrew is CADESO (קדש). God, then, willed to save those who desired it, and he called them to salvation, so that their will might have its reward; but they would not believe. Otherwise it is written of John too: There was a man sent from God, whose name was John; he came to bear witness to the light, that all might believe through him (John 1:6). Nor is he at once at fault if many would not believe; but the will of the one who came was this, that all should believe and be saved. And if whoever has exasperated and afflicted the Holy Spirit, or the Spirit of his Holy One, that is, of Christ, exasperates God, it is because the Holy Spirit is of the same nature with the Father and the Son. Wherefore the Apostle commands: Do not grieve the Holy Spirit, in whom you have been sealed (Eph 4:30). This Holy Spirit withdraws from a body subject to sins, and wisdom does not enter a perverse soul (Wis 1). Hence David too, conscious of his sins, prayed that he might not lose the Holy Spirit, saying: And do not take your Holy Spirit from me (Ps 50 [51]:13). And so that we may know that everyone who exasperates the Holy Spirit offends God, and from a friend becomes an enemy and a foe, the apostle Peter speaks more expressively in the Acts of the Apostles: Why have you agreed to lie to the Holy Spirit? You have not lied to men but to God (Acts 5:9). This is the Holy Spirit of whom the Lord said in the Gospel: If you love me, keep my commandments; and I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Paraclete, to be with you for ever, the Spirit of truth (John 14:15, 16). Of him we find also in the Wisdom which is written under the name of Solomon: For the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and will withdraw from foolish thoughts (Wis 1:5).

63:11ff.

And he remembered the days of the age, of Moses, of his people. Where is he who brought them up out of the sea with the shepherds of his flock? Where is he who put in its midst the Spirit of his Holy One? Who led Moses by the right hand with the arm of his majesty; who divided the waters before them, to make for himself an everlasting name; who led them through the depths like a horse in the desert that does not stumble. Like a beast going down into the plain, the Spirit of the Lord was its leader; so you led your people, to make for yourself a name of glory. LXX: And he remembered the ancient days, he who brought up from the land the shepherd of the sheep. Where is he who put the Holy Spirit in them? Who led Moses by the right hand, the arm of his glory. So he led his people through the mighty water in his sight, to make for himself an everlasting name. He led them through the deep like a horse through the wilderness, and they did not labor. And like cattle through the plain the Spirit came down from the Lord, and was their leader: so you led your people, to make for yourself a name of glory. The Lord, who from a protector became the adversary of the people of the Jews, who provoked his Holy Spirit to anger, and who fought them down, himself remembered the ancient days, when Moses prayed for them in the wilderness, saying: Either forgive them this offense, or if you do not, blot me out of the book which you have written (Exod 32:31, 32). Isaiah, then, remembering the ancient history, says: Where is that Moses who brought them up out of the Red Sea? Where is the shepherd of the sheep? Where is he who labored with the other shepherds of the Lord's flock? Who obtained the Spirit of God by his prayer and entreaties, and put it in the Lord's flock? Or certainly it is to be understood thus: Where is that mercy of the Lord with which he once had pity on his people, so as to grant them the grace of the Holy Spirit too; who led Moses his servant to the right-hand side, not to the left, with the arm of his majesty; who divided the waters before them, to make for himself an everlasting name, so that his power might be told even to the present day? For he led his people through the boundless depths of the waters like a horse through the wilderness, and like cattle over the plain, and the Spirit of the Lord was its leader, that is, of the Lord's flock (Exod 14). By Spirit here we ought to understand the angel who was the leader of the people of Israel, according to what is written: Who makes his angels spirits, and his ministers a burning fire (Ps 103 [104]:4). And in the Epistle to the Hebrews: These are ministering spirits, sent forth to serve for the sake of those who are to possess salvation (Heb 1:14). Let us consider whether what is written in the Acts of the Apostles, The Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, and the eunuch saw him no more (Acts 8:39), ought to be taken of an angel. There are some who maintain that the angel did these things in the Holy Spirit. We run through what is plain so as to dwell on what is more obscure.

63:15ff.

Look down from heaven, and see from your holy dwelling and that of your glory. Where is your zeal and your strength? The multitude of your bowels and of your mercies toward me have held themselves back. For you are our father; and Abraham has not known us, and Israel has been ignorant of us. You, O Lord, are our father, our redeemer from of old is your name. LXX: Turn from heaven, and see from your holy house and that of your glory: where is your zeal and your strength? Where is the multitude of your mercies and of your compassions, with which you bore with us? For you are our father, because Abraham has not known us, and Israel has not known us. But you, O Lord our father, deliver us: from the beginning your name is upon us. You who granted such great things to the people as the preceding discourse has related, so that you even deemed us worthy of the fellowship of your Spirit, now too look down from heaven and see our works, if indeed they are worthy of you. Why do you turn away your face from us? Now heaven is called the holy dwelling and the house of his glory (Ps 43 [44]), according to that saying: Heaven is my throne, and the earth the footstool of my feet (Isa 66:1); and in another place: He who dwells in the heavens will laugh at them; and: To you I have lifted up my eyes, who dwell in heaven (Ps 122 [123]:1). Not that almighty God, who holds heaven in his palm and the earth in his fist, is shut in by any place, but that the things which are holier are called his place and dwelling. Thus Solomon, who built the house of God, says in prayer to him: The heavens of heavens and the earth do not suffice you (Sir 16:18). And in the Lord's Prayer it is said: Your will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth (Matt 6:10). Wherever, then, the will of God is done, that is his dwelling and the house of God. As for what follows, Where is your zeal and your strength?, let us discuss it by that testimony in which God, through Ezekiel, speaks to Jerusalem, who had followed her lovers: Now I will not be angry with you, and my zeal has departed from you (Ezek 16:42). And the sense is: Because we have sinned and you have begun to hate us, your zeal has departed from us, the zeal which does not depart when he speaks through Zechariah: I have been zealous for Zion and Jerusalem with great zeal (Zech 1:14). Hence he says too in what follows: And I will be angry over the nations that have gathered against her round about. When zeal departs, the strength of God departs too, and the affection of a father's bowels is overcome, while the incredible mercy of God is conquered by the greatness of our sins, so that he who could not bear to see me oppressed holds himself back from helping me. For you, he says, are our father, you who are the creator of all. Abraham does not know us, and Israel is ignorant of us, because we have offended you, nor do they recognize as sons those whom they perceive not to be loved by their God. A sudden question arises: why did he set down Abraham and Israel, that is, Jacob, and leave the name of Isaac unspoken (Gen 32)? To this we shall answer that, when the beginning and the end are set down, the middle too is named. Or thus: Abraham was called to faith from the nations, and according to the character of his former and his subsequent condition received a change of name. Jacob too reached it only by much toil, to be called Israel. Hence too Abraham had three wives, and Jacob four; but Isaac kept his ancient name from beginning to end, and, signifying the chastity of the Church, was content with one wife. Those, then, who pray for a change from sinners to a better state take on the likeness of those to whom joy succeeded after sorrow. And this is all that they ask: that, since he is their father and has deigned to give them this name, he may not forget his sons, lest through them the name of God be blasphemed among the nations.

63:18-19

Why have you made us stray, O Lord, from your ways? You have hardened our heart, so that we did not fear you. Return for the sake of your servants, the tribes of your inheritance. As if for nothing they have possessed your holy people; our enemies have trodden down your sanctification. We have become as in the beginning, when you did not rule over us, nor was your name called upon us. LXX: Why have you led us astray, O Lord, from your holy way? You have hardened our hearts, so that we did not fear you. Return for the sake of your servants, for the sake of the tribes of your inheritance, that we may possess a little of your holy mountain; our adversaries have trodden down your sanctuary; we have become as from the beginning, when you did not rule over us, nor was your name called upon us. The Epistle which Paul writes to the Corinthians, though it is written to the people of one city, according to the variety of its inhabitants, that is, of saints and sinners, now praises them, now corrects them, now teaches, now rebukes; it calls them to continence; it does not refuse marriage; it draws them back from idolatry; it instructs them about the resurrection; it stretches out a hand to second marriage, lest it give place to fornication. We have said this so that we may understand that the present passage too, which is woven entirely out of the prayer of the people entreating God, belongs either to the righteous or to sinners, and that they now praise the Lord, now raise a question with the Lord and refer their own fault to God. Hence after the rest they say this too: Why have you made us stray, O Lord, from your ways, or led us astray from your way? You have hardened our heart so that we did not fear you? Not that God is the cause of error and of hardness, but that his patience, as he waits for our salvation and does not correct those who do wrong, seems to be a cause of error and hardness. Hence, when he is vehemently angry with some, he withholds his hand from striking and says: I will not punish your daughters when they have committed fornication, nor your brides when they have committed adultery (Hos 4:14). For he scourges every son whom he receives, and he strikes in order to amend (Heb 12). Thus of those who have by no means lost the name of sons, but are drawn back to repentance through punishment, he says: I will visit their iniquities with the rod, and their sins with scourges; but my mercy I will not take from them (Ps 88 [89]:33). For there is a sorrow that leads to life, and there is a sorrow that leads to death. Hence the sinner too says in the psalm: You have made our paths turn aside from your way, and have humbled us in the place of affliction (Ps 43 [44]:19). And for forty years the people wander in the desert, so that they may not find their former way nor return to the Egyptians (Num 32). In Hosea too the paths of Jerusalem are hedged in and closed with thorns, so that she may not follow her lovers, and, compelled by necessity, may return to her former husband (Hos 2). And God is said to have hardened the heart of Pharaoh, so that he would not let his people go, and so that he might be afflicted with ten plagues (Exod 4). This question Paul discussed most carefully to the Romans (Rom 9), and we have touched on it in a certain work. Return, he says, O Lord, or turn us back, for the sake of your servants, Abraham and Israel, who have not known us, or whom we believe to be among the people. For as if for nothing, and without any toil, our adversaries have possessed your holy people. Or, turn us back so that, according to the Seventy, we may possess a little of your holy mountain, since we cannot possess the whole of your mountain; so that when we have had a part we may come to its fullness and contemplate the glory of the Only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth (John 1); of which it is said in this same prophet: In the last days the mountain of the Lord will be manifest (Isa 2:2).
